'''Lee Sung-min''' ({{korean|hangul=이성민}}, born 16 May 1986) is a South Korean former [[football (soccer)|football]] player who play as a Striker.

==Club career==
On November 20, 2008, Gangwon called Lee up as an extra order from 2009 K-League Draft.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&sid1=001&oid=003&aid=0002388592& |script-title=ko:'드래프트 대만족' 최순호 강원 감독, "원하는 선수 다 뽑았다"|date=2008-11-20|access-date=2008-03-16|publisher=[[Newsis]]|language=ko}}</ref> His first goal for Gangwon came on April 22, 2009, in a match against [[Daejeon Citizen]] during the [[K-League Cup 2009|League Cup]] group stage.

For the 2010 season, he dropped down to the second tier of South Korean football, joining [[Korea National League]] side [[Gangneung City FC]]. He proved himself to be a regular starter for his new side.  On 4 January 2011, it was announced that Lee would return to the K-League, joining [[Daegu FC]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://daegufc.co.kr/2010/sub/news_02.asp?bmode=content&uid=1702 |title=대구FC, 김귀화 코치 및 선수 6명 영입 |work=Daegu FC |date=2011-01-04 |language=ko }}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In 2016 season, he has played for the [[Buriram United]] in the [[Toyota Premier Cup]] with [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] just 45 minutes of play was not good enough. His contract was canceled by that he did not play in the [[Thai Premier League]] even once.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://footballchannelasia.com/th/2016/07/05/the-invisible-10-player/11/ |publisher=footballchannelasia |first=Jedsada |last=Chanapinijwong |title=THE INVISIBLE : 10 แข้งต่างชาติที่ไร้ตัวตนในไทยลีก |access-date=6 July 2016 |date=5 July 2016 |language=th |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817034136/http://footballchannelasia.com/th/2016/07/05/the-invisible-10-player/11/ |archive-date=2016-08-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Charlie Campbell''' (born January 5, 1988, in [[Mundelein, Illinois]]) is an American [[Association football|soccer]] player.

==Career==

===College and amateur===
Campbell attended [[Mundelein High School]] and played club soccer for the Chicago Sockers, before going on to play [[College soccer in the United States|college soccer]] at [[Virginia Tech]]. He started in 19 games for the Hokies during his freshman season in 2006, finishing the season with one goal and seven assists and being named to the All-ACC Freshman team. In 2007, he recorded a 'TEAM' save in preserving the Hokies' 1–0 win at then-No. 2 Connecticut in the NCAA Men's College Cup Regional Final. Campbell started at left back for the Hokies' first ever Final Four appearance. In 2008, Campbell suffered a knee injury and was awarded a medical redshirt. In 2010, Campbell transferred to the [[University of Louisville]] for his final year of eligibility and led the Cardinals to their first  College Cup Final Four appearance in school history. Campbell finished third on the team in points registering six goals and two assists. After being crowned the 2010 Big East regular season and 2010 Big East tournament champions, the Cardinals entered the NCAA tournament as the number one overall seed with an undefeated record. The Cardinals lost to The University of Akron in the NCAA championship 1–0. Campbell was named to the 2010 College Cup All-tournament team and is the first player in NCAA Soccer history to play in two NCAA Final Four's with two separate schools. Campbell graduated with a bachelor's degree in finance from Virginia Tech and completed his Master's of Science from the University of Louisville.

===Professional===
Campbell was drafted in the second round, 35th overall, of the [[2011 MLS SuperDraft]] by [[FC Dallas]].<ref>[http://www.uoflsports.com/sports/m-soccer/spec-rel/011311aab.html Louisville Seniors J.T. Murray and Charlie Campbell Selected in the 2011 MLS Super Draft] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110221185839/http://www.uoflsports.com/sports/m-soccer/spec-rel/011311aab.html |date=February 21, 2011 }}</ref> He spent the entire preseason with the 2010 MLS Cup runners-up, and participated in the 2011 Disney Pro Soccer Classic, but was not offered a contract by the team.

Campbell signed for [[Orlando City SC (2010–14)|Orlando City]] of the [[United Soccer League|USL Professional Division]] in May 2011.<ref>[http://www.orlandocitysoccer.com/news/teamnews/index.html?article_id=177 American midfielder Charlie Campbell signs with Orlando City] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110528124846/http://www.orlandocitysoccer.com/news/teamnews/index.html?article_id=177 |date=May 28, 2011 }}</ref> He made his professional debut on May 25, 2011, in a 2–0 win over the [[Richmond Kickers]].<ref>http://uslpro.uslsoccer.com/scripts/runisa.dll?M2:gp::72013+Elements/Display+E+47107+Stats/+2175640{{dead link|date=November 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> After signing, Campbell made 13 appearances in the remaining 18 games during the 2011 USL PRO season. Orlando City won the 2011 regular season and 2011 USL Pro Championship with Campbell playing a key role in the championship game. Campbell also appeared in two U.S. Open Cup matches and made appearances in both the Bolton Wanderers and Newcastle United exhibition matches.

In 2012, Campbell appeared in 20 of 24 league matches for USL regular season champions Orlando City. Campbell also started both U.S. Open Cup matches for City while notching two assists. Following his one-goal and five-assist campaign, Campbell was awarded Clubman of the Year  by manager Adrian Heath.

On January 21, 2013, Campbell signed a seven-month deal with [[Ljungskile SK]] in the Swedish second tier [[Superettan]] after trialing with the club for two weeks. His friend Patrick Hopkins, who plays defender for Ljungskile, had recommended Campbell to the club.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://lsk.se/default.asp?do=document&docid=5082 |title=Charlie Campbell nästa nyförvärv att krita på |access-date=January 23, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402210523/http://lsk.se/default.asp?do=document&docid=5082 |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> Campbell suffered a career ending knee injury prior to the club's third match of the season.

[[Columbia University]] | occupation = [[Fine-art photography|Fine-art photographer]], [[professor]] | employer = | website = {{URL|www.msrachelstern.com/}} }} '''Rachel Stern''' (born 1989) is an American photographer and educator.{{cite web |title=Midnight Artist: Rachel Stern |url=https://www.theindy.org/a/361 |website=www.theindy.org |publisher=The Indy |language=en}}{{cite web |title=Myth and Body: Devan Shimoyama & Rachel Stern |url=https://www.lesleyheller.com/exhibitions/20161023-myth-and-body-devan-shimoyama-rachel-stern |website=www.lesleyheller.com}}{{Cite web |last=Veitch |first=Eleanor |date=2023-07-31 |title=Meet Rachel Stern, the Photographer Reinterpreting Oscar Wilde's Salome |url=https://www.interviewmagazine.com/art/meet-rachel-stern-the-photographer-reinterpreting-oscar-wildes-salome |access-date=2024-09-21 |website=Interview Magazine |language=en-US}} == Education == Stern studied at the [[Rhode Island School of Design]], achieving a BFA in [[photography]] and art history in 2011.{{Cite web |title=BOMB Magazine {{!}} Portfolio |url=https://bombmagazine.org/articles/2015/08/17/portfolio-59/ |access-date=2025-08-26 |website=BOMB Magazine |language=en}} Stern attend and graduated from [[Columbia University|Columbia’s]] MFA Visual Arts program in 2016. In 2014, Stern attended the [[Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture]]. == Career == In 2019, Stern released ''Slow Morpheus,'' a monograph published by [[Matthew Leifheit|Matte Editions]].{{cite web |title=Rachel Stern: Slow Morpheus Launch with Matte Editions |url=https://www.printedmatter.org/programs/events/887 |website=Printed Matter |language=en}} Stern's exhibitions often take inspiration from the [[literary canon]], with her 2023 exhibition at the Camera Club of New York including text from [[Oscar Wilde]]’s ''[[Salome (play)|Salome]].'' Stern's 2016 exhibition ''Yes, Death'' also took inspiration from Oscar Wilde, with the title originating from an Oscar Wilde quote:''“Yes, death. Death must be so beautiful. To lie in the soft brown earth, with the grasses waving above one’s head, and listen to silence. To have no yesterday, and no tomorrow. To forget time, to forget life, to be at peace.”{{Cite web |last=Stern |first=Rachel |date=2016-06-17 |title=Gorgeous, Spooky Photos of Old Cemeteries |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/yes-death-photos-by-rachel-stern/ |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=VICE |language=en-US}}'' Additionally, Stern has taken inspiration from [[Arthur Miller]]’s ''[[The Crucible]]'' and [[Voltaire]]’s ''[[Candide]].'' Stern's photographs have appeared in the New York Times.{{Cite news |last=Rosenblatt |first=Roger |date=2024-12-24 |title=Opinion {{!}} Why 'A Christmas Carol' Endures |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/12/24/opinion/why-a-christmas-carol-endures.html |access-date=2025-02-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} === Exhibitions === * ''Yes, Death - 2016 - Black & White Gallery/Project Space -'' Southampton, NY, USA{{Cite web |title=Rachel Stern |url=http://www.blackandwhiteprojectspace.org/rachel-stern |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=BLACK & WHITE PROJECT SPACE |language=en-US}} * ''More Weight'' ''- 2018 - [[Brandeis University|Brandeis University Art]] Kniznick Gallery -'' Waltham, MA, USA{{Cite web |date=2018-08-15 |title=Theater of the Absurd: Staged Photographs Reflect Witchcraft, Trumpism, and The Crucible |url=http://hafny.org/blog/2018/8/theater-of-the-absurd-staged-photographs-reflect-witchcraft-trumpism-and-the-crucible |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=Humble Arts Foundation |language=en-US}} * ''Orpheus Looked'' ''- 2019 - [[Mercer County Community College|MCCC]] James Kerney Campus Gallery'' - Trenton, NJ{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Patrick |date=2019-04-15 |title=MCCC's JKC Gallery Presents 'Orpheus Looked' by Photographer Rachel Stern - TrentonDaily |url=https://www.trentondaily.com/mcccs-jkc-gallery-presents-orpheus-looked-by-photographer-rachel-stern/ |access-date=2025-08-25 |language=en}}{{cite web |title=MCCC's James Kerney Campus Gallery Presents "Orpheus Looked" by Trenton Photographer Rachel Stern |url=https://www.newjerseystage.com/articles/2019/03/29/mcccs-james-kerney-campus-gallery-presents-orpheus-looked-by-trenton-photographer-rachel-stern/ |website=New Jersey Stage |language=en}} * ''Ghost in The Machine - 2023 -'' ''[[Getty Images]] -'' Online{{Cite web |last=Growcoot |first=Matt |date=2023-10-30 |title=New Exhibit Explores the Phenomenon of Paranormal Photography |url=https://petapixel.com/2023/10/30/getty-images-exhibit-explores-the-paranormal-photography-phenomenon/ |access-date=2024-09-21 |website=PetaPixel |language=en}} * ''One Should Not Look at Anything'' ''-'' 2023 ''-'' [[The Camera Club of New York|Camera Club of New York]] - New York, NY, USA === Teaching === Stern has taught both high school and college courses in photography. As of 2024, Stern is the Assistant Professor of Visual Arts, Photography at [[Union College]] in Schenectady, New York.{{Cite web |title=Rachel Stern {{!}} Visual Arts {{!}} Union College |url=https://www.union.edu/visual-arts/faculty-staff/rachel-stern |access-date=2025-08-26 |website=www.union.edu |language=en}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Stern, Rachel}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American photographers]] [[Category:American erotic photographers]] [[Category:American portrait photographers]] [[Category:American fine art photographers]] [[Category:Rhode Island School of Design alumni]] [[Category:Columbia University School of the Arts alumni]] [[Category:1989 births]]

'''Zack Hoyt''' (born 1990), known online as '''Asmongold''', is an American [[YouTuber]], [[online streamer]], and political commentator. Initially a ''[[World of Warcraft]]'' streamer,<ref name="dotesports">{{Cite news |last=Bogdanos |first=Dionysios |date=September 20, 2016 |title=Asmongold: "If you wanna be successful, you have to be yourself" |work=Dot Esports |url=https://dotesports.com/general/news/asmongold-if-you-wanna-be-successful-you-have-to-be-yourself-11405 |access-date=March 7, 2020 |archive-date=March 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305043615/https://dotesports.com/general/news/asmongold-if-you-wanna-be-successful-you-have-to-be-yourself-11405 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/world-of-warcraft/asmongold-wow |title=What it takes to be one of World of Warcraft's top streamers |last=Bishop |first=Dylan |date=May 29, 2020 |website=PCGamesN |access-date=March 17, 2023 |archive-date=March 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230317171824/https://www.pcgamesn.com/world-of-warcraft/asmongold-wow |url-status=live}}</ref> he built a substantial online following through his gameplay, commentary, and discussions of gaming culture. His content subsequently expanded to include other video games, current events, and politics.

In 2020, Hoyt co-founded the gaming and content creation organization [[One True King]] (OTK).<ref name="OTK">{{cite web |last=Michael |first=Cale |title=Asmongold, Mizkif, Esfand, and more form One True King organization |date=October 11, 2020 |url=https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/asmongold-mizkif-esfand-and-more-form-one-true-king-organization |publisher=Dot Esports |access-date=March 17, 2021 |archive-date=April 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210411191817/https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/asmongold-mizkif-esfand-and-more-form-one-true-king-organization |url-status=live}}</ref> He was also involved in establishing Starforge Systems, a company specializing in gaming computers, in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gutelle |first=Sam |title=Starforge Systems is blasting off with a creator-led approach to custom PCs |url=https://www.tubefilter.com/2022/08/08/starforge-systems-computer-company-otk-one-true-king-mizkif/ |website=Tubefilter |date=August 8, 2022}}</ref>

In October 2024, Hoyt was temporarily suspended from [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]] following remarks about Palestinians, for which he subsequently apologized.<ref>{{cite web |title=Asmongold: Twitch streamer suspended after Palestinian rant |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c75606vd3l6o |website=BBC News |date=October 16, 2024 |access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Zack Hoyt was born in 1990 in [[Florida]].<ref name="birth year 2">{{Cite web |last=Tsiaoussidis |first=Alex |date=August 1, 2022 |title=Who is Asmongold? Everything to know about Twitch's MMO king |url=https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/who-is-asmongold-everything-to-know-about-twitch-mmo-king |access-date=October 30, 2025 |website=Dot Esports |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> Not long after he was born he moved to [[Austin, Texas]].<ref name="Asmongold TV">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7uBSibvtPFE |title=Why It Sucks To Be Born As Asmongold {{!}} Asmongold Reacts |date=2025-01-31 |last=Asmongold TV |access-date=2026-06-26 |via=YouTube}}</ref> He grew up with an interest in video games, particularly [[role-playing games]] (RPGs), and was introduced to ''World of Warcraft'' by a friend in 2006.<ref name="YouTube 2014">{{cite web |title=FAQ With Asmongold |website=YouTube |date=May 24, 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B8qELe1wBV0 |access-date=March 18, 2023 |archive-date=March 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318202257/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B8qELe1wBV0 |url-status=live}}</ref> He quickly became captivated by the game and began playing it extensively.<ref>{{cite web |last=Tsiaoussidis |first=Alex |title=How many hours has Asmongold played WoW? |website=Dot Esports |date=October 27, 2022 |url=https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/how-many-hours-has-asmongold-played-wow |access-date=March 18, 2023 |archive-date=March 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318203133/https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/how-many-hours-has-asmongold-played-wow |url-status=live}}</ref> Hoyt later attended college, but dropped out to focus on his streaming career.<ref name="YouTube 2019">{{cite web |title=Asmongold Story Time: The Origins Of "Sup Yall" And College Years |website=YouTube |date=July 12, 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rN1wGNUwN7U |access-date=March 18, 2023 |archive-date=March 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318202259/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rN1wGNUwN7U |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Career ==
With the release of ''[[World of Warcraft Classic]]'' in 2019, Hoyt's popularity surged, and he became one of the platform's most prominent streamers in that year.<ref name="Vincent 2019">{{cite web |last=Vincent |first=Brittany |title=WoW Twitch streamer Asmongold was most watched in Q3 2019 – StreamElements report |website=Shacknews |date=October 14, 2019 |url=https://www.shacknews.com/article/114473/wow-twitch-streamer-asmongold-was-most-watched-in-q3-2019-streamelements-report |access-date=March 18, 2023 |archive-date=March 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318234608/https://www.shacknews.com/article/114473/wow-twitch-streamer-asmongold-was-most-watched-in-q3-2019-streamelements-report |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Ålander |first=Juhani |date=2021 |title=Katsojainteraktiiviset pelit ja niiden historia |language=fi |trans-title=Viewer Interactive games and their history |publisher=[[Kajaani University of Applied Sciences]]}}</ref> He remained one of Twitch's most popular ''World of Warcraft'' streamers during the ''[[WoW Shadowlands|Shadowlands]]'' launch in 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Down |first=Aaron |date=November 24, 2020 |title=WoW Shadowlands' launch draws in nearly one million viewers on Twitch |work=PCGamesN |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/world-of-warcraft/shadowlands-launch-twitch |access-date=March 11, 2021 |archive-date=January 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126021256/https://www.pcgamesn.com/world-of-warcraft/shadowlands-launch-twitch |url-status=live}}</ref> On July 3, 2021, he played ''[[Final Fantasy XIV]]'' for the first time before hundreds of thousands of viewers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miceli |first=Max |date=July 4, 2021 |title=Asmongold plays Final Fantasy XIV for the first time |url=https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/asmongold-plays-final-fantasy-xiv-for-the-first-time |access-date=September 15, 2022 |website=Dot Esports |language=en-US |archive-date=September 1, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210901122911/https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/asmongold-plays-final-fantasy-xiv-for-the-first-time |url-status=live}}</ref> Hoyt's favor towards ''World of Warcraft'' soured in July 2021, when [[California Department of Fair Employment and Housing v. Activision Blizzard|a lawsuit was filed]] against the game's developer [[Activision Blizzard]] for discrimination against and sexual harassment of female employees. Hoyt subsequently began regularly criticizing Activision Blizzard and providing regular updates on the lawsuit on his streams.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Craig |first1=Matt |date=August 9, 2021 |title=On YouTube and Twitch, the Activision Blizzard harassment lawsuit leaves creators reeling |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/video-games/2021/08/09/activision-blizzard-asmongold-content-creators/ |work=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=August 5, 2026 |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> By August 2021, Hoyt had become one of the largest streamers on Twitch, with over 2 million followers.<ref name="Hate Raid Boycott" /> In October of the same year, leaked data from Twitch showed that Hoyt had earned the 14th-highest amount of money on the platform since August 2019, totalling at over $2.5 million.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Heath |first1=Jerome |title=Full list of all Twitch payouts (Twitch leaks) |url=https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/full-list-of-all-twitch-payouts-twitch-leaks |website=Dot Esports |access-date=9 September 2026 |date=3 October 2025}}</ref>

In 2022, he contacted [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] senator [[Ted Cruz]] to discuss regulating [[loot box]]es in video games. Cruz was non-committal.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chalk |first1=Andy |title=Ted Cruz says he's 'interested' in talking to Asmongold about loot boxes |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/ted-cruz-says-hes-interested-in-talking-to-asmongold-about-loot-boxes/ |access-date=December 27, 2024 |work=[[PC Gamer]] |date=June 21, 2022 |archive-date=May 3, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250503142954/https://www.pcgamer.com/ted-cruz-says-hes-interested-in-talking-to-asmongold-about-loot-boxes/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In early 2024, Hoyt, alongside other prominent YouTubers, aided in spreading "anti-[[woke]]" conspiracism about [[Sweet Baby Inc.]]'s work in promoting [[diversity, equity, and inclusion]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Houle |first=Kamran |date=2024 |title=The Paranoid Style of Internet Politics: Gamer Backlashes and 'Politics' as Imposition |journal=POLIS: Sociology & Anthropology Undergraduate Journal |volume=1}}</ref>

In a [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]] stream on October 14, 2024, Hoyt called [[Palestinians]] "terrible people" from "an inferior culture" that "kills people for their identity" and "is directly antithetical to everything [[Western values]] stand for".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Snavely |first=Adam |date=October 14, 2024 |title='I don't give a f**k, they're terrible people': Asmongold sparks huge backlash with Palestine comments |url=https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/i-dont-give-a-fk-theyre-terrible-people-asmongold-sparks-huge-backlash-with-palestine-comments |access-date=October 15, 2024 |website=Dot Esports |language=en-US |archive-date=May 3, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250503145121/https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/i-dont-give-a-fk-theyre-terrible-people-asmongold-sparks-huge-backlash-with-palestine-comments |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Stedman-2024">{{cite web |last=Stedman |first=Alex |date=October 15, 2024 |title=Asmongold's Twitch Channel Banned Following Racist Rant About Palestinians |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/asmongolds-twitch-channel-banned-following-racist-rant-about-palestinians |access-date=October 15, 2024 |website=[[IGN]] |archive-date=October 16, 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241016051325/https://www.ign.com/articles/asmongolds-twitch-channel-banned-following-racist-rant-about-palestinians |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Polygon Palestine">{{cite web |last1=Diaz |first1=Ana |title=Why Twitch banned Asmongold |url=https://www.polygon.com/culture/467037/asmongolds-twitch-suspension-palestine-explained/ |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |access-date=3 December 2025 |language=en |date=17 October 2024 |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> He also said that they "have genocide built into [[Sharia]] law right now, so, no, I'm not going to cry a fucking river when people who have genocide that's baked into their laws are getting [[Gaza genocide|genocided]]". This statement was later called a "racist tirade".<ref name="Chalk-2024">{{cite news |last1=Chalk |first1=Andy |date=October 15, 2024 |title=Asmongold suspended from Twitch following racist tirade about Palestinians |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hardware/streaming/asmongold-suspended-from-twitch-following-racist-tirade-about-palestinians/ |work=[[PC Gamer]] |access-date=December 3, 2025 |language=en |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> His zackrawrr account on Twitch was banned for 14 days due to violating the platform's hateful conduct policy.<ref name="BBC News-2024">{{Cite news |date=October 16, 2024 |title=Twitch streamer Asmongold suspended after Palestinian rant |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c75606vd3l6o |access-date=October 20, 2024 |work=[[BBC News]] |archive-date=May 3, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250503150556/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c75606vd3l6o |url-status=live}}</ref> Hoyt initially made a brief apology on Twitter which was criticized by ''[[PC Gamer]]'', stating "that quite a few people don't consider 'my bad' a sufficient expression of contrition and reconsideration for espousing grossly racist attitudes".<ref name="Chalk-2024" /> Hoyt later released a more extensive apology stating he had been "slowly devolving into the most mean-spirited, rude, nasty, callous, psychopathic version of [him]self" and he would take a break from streaming. He also stepped down from his leadership positions in OTK and Starforge Systems.<ref name="Polygon Palestine" /><ref name="Chalk-2024-2">{{cite news |last1=Chalk |first1=Andy |date=October 16, 2024 |title=Asmongold steps back from OTK and says 'I need to fix my f***ing life' after racist rant about Palestinians: 'I have been slowly devolving into the most mean-spirited, rude, nasty, callous, psychopathic version of myself' |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hardware/streaming/asmongold-steps-back-from-otk-and-says-i-need-to-fix-my-f-ing-life-after-racist-rant-about-palestinians-i-have-been-slowly-devolving-into-the-most-mean-spirited-rude-nasty-callous-psychopathic-version-of-myself/ |work=[[PC Gamer]] |access-date=December 3, 2025 |language=en |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref>

After [[Elon Musk]] was accused in January 2025 of paying third parties to [[Boosting (video games)|boost]] his ''[[Path of Exile 2]]'' account, Hoyt challenged Musk to prove that he himself had leveled a character to 97 in hardcore mode, after which Musk unfollowed Hoyt on [[Twitter|X]], removed his verification check, and posted a screenshot of their private messages. A [[Community Notes|community note]] under the post stated that leaking private messages without permission generally violated X's guidelines.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gach |first=Ethan |date=January 16, 2025 |title=Elon Musk And Asmongold Are Fighting After The Streamer Accused Him Of Being A Fake Gamer |url=https://kotaku.com/elon-musk-asmongold-poe-2-account-boosting-controversy-1851741223 |access-date=January 16, 2025 |website=[[Kotaku]] |archive-date=January 16, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250116200253/https://kotaku.com/elon-musk-asmongold-poe-2-account-boosting-controversy-1851741223 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gault |first=Matthew |date=January 16, 2025 |title=Why Is Elon Musk Beefing With a Twitch Streamer? |url=https://gizmodo.com/why-is-elon-musk-beefing-with-a-twitch-streamer-2000551256 |access-date=January 16, 2025 |website=[[Gizmodo]] |archive-date=February 9, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250209153258/https://gizmodo.com/why-is-elon-musk-beefing-with-a-twitch-streamer-2000551256 |url-status=live}}</ref> Musk later deleted his tweets, and the two have subsequently interacted with each other on X about other topics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Did Asmongold just end an indie game? Asmongold vs Take Us North controversy explained |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/international-sports/did-asmongold-just-end-an-indie-game-asmongold-vs-take-us-north-controversy-explained/articleshow/123522001.cms |access-date=August 27, 2025 |work=[[Times of India]] |date=August 26, 2025 |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref>

In November 2025, Hoyt was named in a lawsuit filed by the streamer Mizkif as a defendant alongside fellow streamer [[Emiru]], OTK Media Inc., Mythic Talent Management Inc., and King Gaming Labs Inc. for reputational harm, lost earnings, and emotional distress.<ref name="Taylor">{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=Mollie |date=November 5, 2025 |title=One of the biggest streamers on Twitch is trying to take Asmongold and Emiru to court over defamation claims |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hardware/streaming/one-of-the-biggest-streamers-on-twitch-is-trying-to-take-asmongold-and-emiru-to-court-over-defamation-claims/ |work=[[PC Gamer]] |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> The lawsuit came after Emiru accused Mizkif of "psychological and domestic abuse, stalking, harassment, sexual assault, and threats of blackmail", which was then amplified by Hoyt during his livestreams.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Alisia |first1=Powell |title=Top Twitch streamer files defamation lawsuit against fellow streamers |url=https://www.kxan.com/news/top-twitch-streamer-files-defamation-lawsuit-against-fellow-streamers/ |access-date=November 26, 2025 |work=[[KXAN-TV]] |date=November 4, 2025 |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref><ref name=assault>{{cite web |title="Nothing He Is Upset About Is Actionable" Asmongold Has Asked the Court to Dismiss Mizkif's Lawsuit Against Him |url=https://gamerant.com/asmongold-mizkif-lawsuit/ |website=GameRant |date=February 9, 2026 |access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref>

In August 2026, he received a 14-day ban for suggesting that [[2026 Ceuta migrant crisis|migrants, including children, attempting to cross]] from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of [[Ceuta]] should be shot; he refused to apologize for these remarks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Asmongold Officially Banned On Twitch After Disturbing Comments |url=https://www.thegamer.com/asmongold-twitch-ban-august-2026/ |website=TheGamer |date=August 9, 2026}}</ref>

== Views ==
According to ''[[The Atlantic]]'', Hoyt presents his opinions as so common "that disagreeing with him means you're intellectually disabled." His beliefs have been characterized as a brand of conservatism defined by a lack of committed system of beliefs and hostility towards "[[left-wing]] [[identity politics]]". Hoyt has expressed support for [[universal basic income]] and a constitutional right to abortion. He has said that he places no weight on "principles or morality", describing such views as "top-down ideas that are given to you by the elites."<ref name="Kornhaber">{{Cite magazine |last=Kornhaber |first=Spencer |date=April 25, 2025 |title='All We Wanted to Do Was Play Video Games' |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2025/04/how-video-games-took-over-politics-asmongold/682592/ |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250425160732/https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2025/04/how-video-games-took-over-politics-asmongold/682592/ |archive-date=April 25, 2025 |access-date=August 31, 2025 |magazine=[[The Atlantic]] |language=en}}</ref>

On one occasion, he cited [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] congressman [[Al Green (politician)|Al Green]]'s disruption of President [[Donald Trump]]'s [[2025 Donald Trump speech to a joint session of Congress|2025 Congressional Address]], stating that Green's actions make "people think [he's] a fucking [[Retard (pejorative)|retard]]".<ref name="Kornhaber" />

In an article for the ''[[International Journal of Communication]]'', Adam Ruch cited Hoyt as an example of a video game critic who believed that left-leaning, "woke" perspectives were forced into video games. According to Ruch, Hoyt attributed this influence of "woke" perspectives in games to the [[environmental, social, and governance]] investment principle, arguing that left-leaning games were more likely to attract investment from large fund managers.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Ruch |first=Adam |date=2025 |title=Forced: Perceptions of "Woke" Politics in Video Games |journal=International Journal of Communication |volume=19 |pages=2008–2027 |issn=1932-8036}}</ref>

Hoyt has been characterized as typically holding [[anti-trans]] views.<ref name="Pink News Pronouns" /> In 2021, he refused to take part in a boycott against Twitch to protest "hate raids" against streamers of color and LGBTQ streamers claiming the movement needed large streamers to succeed, despite being one of the largest on the platform.<ref name="Hate Raid Boycott">{{cite web |last1=Nightingale |first1=Ed |title=Top Twitch streamer refuses to step up as an LGBT+ ally: 'Nobody gives a fuck' |url=https://www.thepinknews.com/2021/08/24/asmongold-twitch-hate-raids/ |website=[[PinkNews]] |access-date=9 September 2026 |date=24 August 2021}}</ref> As part of his political commentary, Hoyt claimed that "every [[Transgender youth|trans kid]] is a victim of a parent with mental illness".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Taaffe |first=Gideon |date=2025-12-11 |title=Asmongold, one of the largest US streamers on YouTube, has leveled up from gaming to politics |url=https://www.mediamatters.org/asmongold/asmongold-one-largest-us-streamers-youtube-has-leveled-gaming-politics |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=Media Matters for America |language=en}}</ref> Despite Hoyt's claims that trans children have been "[[LGBTQ grooming conspiracy theory|groomed]]" into being trans, he has said he would respect the pronoun choices of his own children.<ref name="Pink News Pronouns">{{cite news |last=Hansford |first=Amelia |date=November 5, 2025 |title=Asmongold stuns right-wing fans by saying he'd respect his trans child's pronouns |url=https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/11/05/asmongold-trans-broken-clock-right-twice-a-day/ |work=[[Pink News]] |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref>

In December 2025, Hoyt endorsed candidate [[James Fishback]]'s campaign for [[2026 Florida gubernatorial election|Governor of Florida]], describing Fishback as "[[based]]" and urging his followers to "vote for people like this."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sommer |first=Will |date=December 18, 2025 |title=Meet the First Groyper Politician |url=https://www.thebulwark.com/p/meet-the-first-groyper-politician-james-fishback |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[The Bulwark (website)|The Bulwark]] |language=en |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref>

[[Media Matters for America]] has been critical of Hoyt's remarks against immigrants and political opposition, highlighting statements he made in which he called for criminal prosecution of both groups in addition to a statement Hoyt made that his goal in his coverage is to "radicalize people as much as possible" by portraying subjects in "the most extreme and negative way" as a means of driving people toward his desired solutions. They also reported that Hoyt has praised white nationalist [[Nick Fuentes]] and anti-Muslim activist [[Tommy Robinson]] for being "willing to put it on the table and risk their platforms," and has described his own role as a bridge between far-right figures and more mainstream audiences.<ref name="MediaMattersJuly2026">{{cite web |title="My goal ... is to radicalize people as much as possible": Asmongold's extreme rhetoric about immigration and ideological opponents |url=https://www.mediamatters.org/asmongold/my-goal-radicalize-people-much-possible-asmongolds-extreme-rhetoric-about-immigration-and |website=Media Matters |date=July 10, 2026 |access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref> 

His remarks have frequently drawn accusations of misogyny, including claims that men are "more naturally attractive" than women, that women are "best" at "selling themselves for money," and that female streamers are essentially equivalent to OnlyFans creators.<ref>{{cite web |title=Asmongold Reveals Insane Take on Men vs Women Attractiveness |url=https://gamerant.com/asmongold-men-women-more-attractive/ |website=GameRant |date=May 31, 2026 |access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Asmongold says female streamers are basically OnlyFans creators |url=https://cybernews.com/news/asmongold-female-streamers-onlyfans/ |website=Cybernews |date=June 1, 2026 |access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Jacob Anthony Chansley was born in 1988 and raised by a single mother, Martha Chansley.<ref name="Euronews-2021" /><ref name="Palmer-2021">{{cite web|date=January 8, 2021|title=Multiple "QAnon Shaman" videos resurface after Jake Angeli leads siege of Capitol|url=https://www.newsweek.com/qanon-shaman-jake-angeli-trump-capitol-1560055|access-date=January 8, 2021|website=[[Newsweek]]|first=Ewan|last=Palmer|archive-date=January 8, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108163458/https://www.newsweek.com/qanon-shaman-jake-angeli-trump-capitol-1560055|url-status=live}}</ref> He attended [[Moon Valley High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]], and [[Glendale Community College (Arizona)|Glendale Community College]], where he completed some coursework in psychology, religion, philosophy and ceramics.<ref>{{cite web|date=January 8, 2021|title=Mom of furry-hatted Capitol rioter from Arizona defends his patriotism|url=https://www.abc15.com/news/state/mom-of-furry-hatted-capitol-rioter-from-arizona-defends-his-patriotism|access-date=January 8, 2021|website=[[KNXV]]|first=Melissa|last=Blasius|archive-date=January 8, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108042241/https://www.abc15.com/news/state/mom-of-furry-hatted-capitol-rioter-from-arizona-defends-his-patriotism|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Kunkle-2021">{{cite news |last1=Kunkle |first1=Fredrick |title=Trump supporter in horns and fur is charged in Capitol riot |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/jacob-chansely-horn-qanon-capitol-riot/2021/01/09/5d3c2c96-52b9-11eb-bda4-615aaefd0555_story.html |access-date=January 12, 2021 |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=January 9, 2021 |archive-date=January 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111054231/https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/jacob-chansely-horn-qanon-capitol-riot/2021/01/09/5d3c2c96-52b9-11eb-bda4-615aaefd0555_story.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Career ==
Chansley enlisted in the [[United States Navy]] on September 26, 2005. After [[Recruit Training Command, Great Lakes, Illinois|basic training]] and training as a supply clerk, he was assigned to the [[aircraft carrier]] [[USS Kitty Hawk (CV-63)|USS ''Kitty Hawk'']] in March 2006. At some point, he refused to take an [[anthrax]] vaccine and was scheduled for discharge from the Navy. On September 29, 2007, he was sent to a Transient Personnel Unit in [[Puget Sound]] in [[Washington (state)|Washington]], and was processed out of the Navy on October 11. After two years and 15 days in uniform, his final rank was [[Storekeeper]] [[Seaman Apprentice]].<ref name="Ziezulewicz-2021">{{cite web |title='QAnon Shaman' charged with storming the Capitol is a Navy veteran |last=Ziezulewicz |first=Geoff |website=[[Navy Times]] |date=January 11, 2021 |url=https://www.navytimes.com/news/your-navy/2021/01/12/qanon-shaman-charged-with-storming-the-capitol-is-a-navy-veteran/ |access-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-date=January 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210119022752/https://www.navytimes.com/news/your-navy/2021/01/12/qanon-shaman-charged-with-storming-the-capitol-is-a-navy-veteran/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=January 12, 2021|title=The 'QAnon shaman' guy got kicked out of the Navy for refusing a vaccine|url=https://taskandpurpose.com/news/qanon-shaman-guy-navy-veteran-vaccine/|access-date=January 13, 2021|website=Task & Purpose|first=James|last=Clark|language=en-US|archive-date=January 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113220555/https://taskandpurpose.com/news/qanon-shaman-guy-navy-veteran-vaccine/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Harkins |first=Gina |url=https://www.military.com/daily-news/2021/01/11/qanon-shaman-arrested-storming-us-capitol-navy-veteran.html |title='QAnon Shaman' Arrested for Storming the US Capitol Is a Navy Veteran |work=[[Military.com]] |date=January 11, 2021 |access-date=January 15, 2021 |archive-date=January 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114081111/https://www.military.com/daily-news/2021/01/11/qanon-shaman-arrested-storming-us-capitol-navy-veteran.html |url-status=live}}</ref> His military awards and decorations include the [[National Defense Service Medal]], the [[Global War on Terrorism Service Medal]], the [[Sea Service Ribbon#Navy and Marine Corps Sea Service Deployment Ribbon|Sea Service Deployment Ribbon]] and the [[Navy and Marine Corps Overseas Service Ribbon]].<ref name="Ziezulewicz-2021" />

Chansley [[self-published]] two books: ''Will & Power: Inside the Living Library (Volume 1)'', published in 2017 under the [[pen name]] Loan Wolf; and ''One Mind at a Time: A Deep State of Illusion'', published in 2020 under the name Jacob Angeli.<ref name="Kunkle-2021" /> He produced and narrated 11 videos espousing various conspiracy theories and uploaded them to the platform [[Rumble (website)|Rumble]] in late 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rumble.com/search/video?q=YellowstoneWolfAZ|title=Search results for: YellowstoneWolfAZ|website=Rumble|date=December 8, 2020 |access-date=January 12, 2021|archive-date=January 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112213935/https://rumble.com/search/video?q=YellowstoneWolfAZ|url-status=live}}</ref>

Chansley had a profile on the ''[[Backstage (magazine)|Backstage]]'' website seeking work as an actor.<ref>{{Cite web|date=January 8, 2021|title=Jake Angeli: What we know about the 'QAnon shaman' who stormed the US Capitol|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-election-2020/jake-angeli-qanon-shaman-stormed-capitol-b1784091.html|access-date=January 12, 2021|website=The Independent|first=Graig|last=Graziosi|language=en|archive-date=January 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113145322/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-election-2020/jake-angeli-qanon-shaman-stormed-capitol-b1784091.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In November 2023, he filed a candidate statement of interest to run as a [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] in the [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona|2024 election]] for [[Arizona's 8th congressional district]],<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://apnews.com/article/capitol-rioter-arizona-congress-chansley-33de9a9f4ff1ea35cd12d9719a2f2987 |title=Capitol rioter plans 2024 run as a Libertarian candidate in Arizona's 8th congressional district |date=November 12, 2023 |work=[[AP News]]}}</ref> but he later failed to submit any petition signatures to get on the ballot.<ref name="Packer-2024">{{cite journal |last1=Packer |first1=George |title=WHAT WILL BECOME OF AMERICAN CIVILIZATION? 4. What's replacing it might be just as scary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/nov/21/climate-denial-far-right-immigration |work=The Guardian |date=November 21, 2021 |access-date=November 21, 2021 |archive-date=November 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211121082038/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/nov/21/climate-denial-far-right-immigration |url-status=live}}</ref> In early 2020 he told ''[[The Arizona Republic]]'' that he began wearing a fur hat and [[face paint]] to attract attention, so that he could then talk about QAnon and "other truths".<ref name="Ruelas-2021a" /><ref name="Matthews-2021">{{cite news |last1=Matthews |first1=David |title=Jamiroquai singer Jay Kay denies being at D.C. riot: 'I wasn't with all those freaks' |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/snyde/ny-jamiroquai-jay-kay-not-at-capitol-riot-dc-20210107-d3iwmdakabd4xmj3p2lasodr5e-story.html |access-date=January 8, 2021 |work=[[New York Daily News]] |date=January 7, 2021 |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108215102/https://www.nydailynews.com/snyde/ny-jamiroquai-jay-kay-not-at-capitol-riot-dc-20210107-d3iwmdakabd4xmj3p2lasodr5e-story.html |url-status=live}}</ref> He appeared at a [[Black Lives Matter]] (BLM) protest in the Phoenix area in order to spread the QAnon conspiracy theory.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Choiniere|first=Alyssa|date=January 7, 2021|title='Jake Angeli', Whose Real Name Is Jacob Chansley, Has Been Arrested|url=https://heavy.com/news/jake-angeli-q-shaman/|access-date=January 11, 2021|website=Heavy.com|language=en-US|archive-date=January 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110125251/https://heavy.com/news/jake-angeli-q-shaman/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the [[2020 United States presidential election]], Chansley's protests focused on challenging the results of the [[2020 United States presidential election in Arizona|vote in Arizona]].<ref name="Ruelas-2021a" /><ref>{{cite news|title=Hundreds gather outside state Capitol to protest Ducey stay-at-home order|url=https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/news/local/phoenix/2020/05/03/coronavirus-arizona-protest-ducey-stay-home-order-outside-captiol/3075637001/|access-date=January 8, 2021|date=May 3, 2020|newspaper=[[The Arizona Republic]]|archive-date=January 11, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111190616/https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/news/local/phoenix/2020/05/03/coronavirus-arizona-protest-ducey-stay-home-order-outside-captiol/3075637001/|url-status=live}}</ref> He camped outside the [[Maricopa County Courthouse]] during the vote counting process,<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Scenes from Election Protests in Maricopa County Arizona|url=https://time.com/5908628/maricopa-county-arizona-protests/|access-date=January 8, 2021|date=November 6, 2020|magazine=Time|first=Paul|last=Moakley|archive-date=December 14, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201214111932/https://time.com/5908628/maricopa-county-arizona-protests/|url-status=live}}</ref> and gave a speech at a rally there on November 7, the day that [[Joe Biden]] was declared president-elect, saying, "This election has not been called! Don't believe that lie! They got their hands caught in the cookie jar and we're going to the [[United States Supreme Court|Supreme Court]]! Trump always looks like he's going to lose. And then he wins."<ref name="Snow-2020" />

=== Participation in the 2021 Capitol attack ===
{{January 6 United States Capitol attack|expanded=List}}
During the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack]], Chansley entered the [[United States Senate|Senate]] floor in the [[United States Capitol|Capitol]] wearing his "shamanic" attire,<ref name="Ruelas-2021a" /><ref name="Matthews-2021" /> including a bison-horned fur [[headdress]] and war paint in red, white and blue, carrying a {{convert|6|ft|m|spell=in|adj=mid|-high}} [[spear]] with an [[American flag]] tied below the spear head.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Barnes |first1=Sophia |title=Capitol Rioter Seen in Horned Hat, Carrying Spear Arrested: US Attorney |url=https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/local/capitol-rioter-seen-in-horned-hat-carrying-spear-arrested-us-attorney/2535850/ |access-date=January 9, 2021 |work=NBC Washington 4 |date=January 9, 2021 |archive-date=January 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109165443/https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/local/capitol-rioter-seen-in-horned-hat-carrying-spear-arrested-us-attorney/2535850/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He was photographed standing on the [[Dais|raised platform]] in front of [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]]'s chair in the Senate chamber, gaining him significant media attention. He later said police had initially blocked the crowd from entry, but had then specifically allowed them entry, at which point he entered.<ref>{{cite news|last=Gabbatt|first=Adam|date=January 7, 2021|title=Faces of extremism: the rioters behind the attack on the US Capitol|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/jan/07/capitol-attack-rioters-jake-angeli-richard-barnett|access-date=January 8, 2021|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=January 8, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108000935/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/jan/07/capitol-attack-rioters-jake-angeli-richard-barnett|url-status=live}}</ref> On March 16, 2021, the U.S. District Court in Washington D.C. released previously unseen video footage of Chansley entering the Capitol building after windows were smashed.<ref name="Ruelas-2021">{{Cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona-breaking/2021/03/16/jake-angeli-jacob-chansley-video-shows-storming-capitol/4716926001/|title=Court releases video of Jake Angeli, who mobbed U.S. Capitol in fur hat and horns|first=Richard|last=Ruelas|newspaper=The Arizona Republic|access-date=March 17, 2021|date=March 16, 2021|archive-date=March 17, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210317192722/https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona-breaking/2021/03/16/jake-angeli-jacob-chansley-video-shows-storming-capitol/4716926001/|url-status=live}}</ref> Several media outlets have noted that outfit resembled that of British acid jazz band [[Jamiroquai]]’s lead singer [[Jay Kay]], which led to Kay jokingly denying his involvement in the riots.<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://ew.com/music/jamiroquai-singer-jay-kay-not-capitol-riot-viking/ | title=Jamiroquai singer Jay Kay says he's not Capitol riot Viking: 'I wasn't with all those freaks' | magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] }}</ref>

Video footage presented by [[Tucker Carlson]] on [[Fox News]] in March 2023 depicted Chansley walking through the Capitol building in the company of police officers who appeared to make no visible effort to stop him. Carlson, who was given exclusive access to the security footage by a top congressional Republican, characterized the officers as "tour guides" for Chansley and noted that none of the officers arrested him.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 8, 2023 |title=Fox News host Tucker Carlson not credible, says White House |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-64883668 |access-date=March 9, 2023 |archive-date=March 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308212312/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-64883668 |url-status=live}}</ref> U.S. Capitol Police Chief [[Tom Manger]] denounced Carlson's segment, calling the show "filled with offensive and misleading conclusions." Manger specifically took issue with Carlson's claim that Capitol Police officers acted as "tour guides" for Chansley. He maintained that Capitol Police officers were badly outnumbered and did their best to use de-escalation tactics to try to talk rioters into leaving the building.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jackman |first=Tom |title=Capitol Police chief blasts Tucker Carlson over 'misleading' Jan. 6 footage |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2023/03/07/capitol-police-tucker-carlson-footage/ |newspaper=The Washington Post |access-date=March 10, 2023 |archive-date=March 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230309154930/https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2023/03/07/capitol-police-tucker-carlson-footage/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Chansley's attorney claimed to have no prior knowledge of the footage, noting that the government is obligated to disclose all evidence{{snd}}especially exculpatory evidence{{snd}}and that here the government failed to do so. Because Chansley pleaded guilty, it remains unclear whether this error could cause court proceedings to be affected. The prosecution at the time he pleaded guilty had said they were still reviewing evidence.<ref>{{Cite news |first1=Hannah |last1=Rabinowitz |first2=Katelyn |last2=Polantz |first3=Holmes |last3=Lybrand |date=March 9, 2023 |title=Tucker Carlson's airing of security footage spills into January 6 criminal court cases |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/03/09/politics/tucker-carlson-january-6-court-cases-us-capitol/index.html |access-date=March 9, 2023 |work=CNN |language=en |archive-date=March 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230309175339/https://www.cnn.com/2023/03/09/politics/tucker-carlson-january-6-court-cases-us-capitol/index.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

Court transcripts reveal Chansley told the [[FBI]] that he had traveled to the Capitol "as a part of a group effort, with other 'patriots' from Arizona, at the request of the President that all 'patriots' come to DC on January 6, 2021".<ref>{{cite news|last=Polantz|first=Katelyn|url=https://www.cnn.com/politics/live-news/capitol-riots-investigation-trump-news-saturday/h_618e29aa580e9031519b7d79449c9b85|title=US Capitol rioter in headdress told FBI he came to Washington based on prompt from Trump|work=CNN|date=January 9, 2021|access-date=January 10, 2021|archive-date=January 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109182335/https://www.cnn.com/politics/live-news/capitol-riots-investigation-trump-news-saturday/h_618e29aa580e9031519b7d79449c9b85|url-status=live}}</ref> Prior to the Capitol being invaded, Chansley called out for the demonstrators to pause and join him in prayer, saying, "Thank you for allowing the United States to be reborn. We love you and we thank you. In [[Christ]]'s holy name, we pray."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jelten |first1=Tom |title=Militant Christian Nationalists Remain A Potent Force, Even After The Capitol Riot |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/01/19/958159202/militant-christian-nationalists-remain-a-potent-force |work=[[NPR]] |date=January 19, 2021 |access-date=February 7, 2021 |archive-date=February 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210218015609/https://www.npr.org/2021/01/19/958159202/militant-christian-nationalists-remain-a-potent-force |url-status=live}}</ref> After the riot, Chansley told reporters, "The fact that we had a bunch of our traitors in office hunker down, put on their [[gas mask]]s and retreat into their underground bunker, I consider that a win."<ref name="Schapiro-2021" />

Chansley was listed as a [[person of interest]] with the [[Washington DC Police]] on January 8.<ref name="Stapleton-2021" /> Interviewed while wanted, Chansley said that he believed he did nothing wrong, telling [[NBC]]: "I walked through an open door, dude."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ruelas |first1=Richard |title=Jake Angeli, Arizona's 'QAnon shaman,' pleads guilty to felony obstruction, could get 5 years |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona-breaking/2021/09/02/jake-angeli-jacob-chansley-qanon-shaman-pleads-guilty-jan-6-capitol-riot/5704512001/ |access-date=June 25, 2024 |work=Arizona Republic |date=September 2, 2021 |quote=[Judge Royce Lamberth of D.C. federal court] cited video that showed Angeli walking into the Capitol through a door while people were climbing through a nearby broken window as evidence he was part of the initial incursion of the building. Lamberth wrote that Angeli 'quite literally spearheaded' the entry into the Capitol.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Ruelas|first=Richard|date=November 17, 2021|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2021/11/17/jake-angeli-jacob-chansley-qanon-shaman-sentenced-role-jan-6-raid/8652784002/|title=Jake Angeli, aka QAnon shaman, sentenced to 41 months in Jan. 6 Capitol riot|work=[[USA Today]]|access-date=June 29, 2026|quote=Angeli gave an interview to NBC News the next day, while travelling back to Arizona, and downplayed his actions. "I walked through an open door, dude", he said.}}</ref> Chansley told [[KPNX]] that he "wasn't worried" about possible charges on January 8.<ref name="Stapleton-2021" /> Chansley had no [[criminal record]] in Arizona before taking part in the riot.<ref name="Stapleton-2021" />

|date=January 20, 2021 |work=[[KSDK]] |archive-date=February 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207004628/https://www.ksdk.com/article/news/local/st-louis-attorneys-statement-on-client-not-being-pardoned-in-capitol-riot/63-32553345-a5f3-4a13-9196-b4251643df56 |url-status=live}}</ref> According to Watkins, Chansley was prepared to testify against Trump in [[Second impeachment of Donald Trump|his second impeachment trial]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-friday-edition-1.5893813/capitol-hill-rioter-qanon-shaman-wants-to-testify-against-trump-says-lawyer-1.5893816 |title=Capitol Hill rioter 'QAnon Shaman' wants to testify against Trump, says lawyer |work=[[CBC Radio]] |date=January 29, 2021 |access-date=January 30, 2021 |archive-date=February 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207004727/https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-friday-edition-1.5893813/capitol-hill-rioter-qanon-shaman-wants-to-testify-against-trump-says-lawyer-1.5893816 |url-status=live}}</ref> However, the trial ended with Trump's acquittal without any witnesses being called.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/world-us-canada-56054136|title=Donald Trump impeachment trial: Ex-president acquitted of inciting insurrection|website=BBC News|date=February 13, 2021 |access-date=February 14, 2021|archive-date=February 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210214225754/https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-us-canada-56054136|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/trump-impeachment-trial-live-updates/2021/02/13/967650922/agreement-reached-to-avoid-witnesses-in-trumps-impeachment-trial|title=Agreement Reached To Avoid Witnesses In Trump's Impeachment Trial|last=Naylor|first=Brian|date=February 13, 2021|work=[[NPR]]|access-date=February 14, 2021|archive-date=February 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210214025801/https://www.npr.org/sections/trump-impeachment-trial-live-updates/2021/02/13/967650922/agreement-reached-to-avoid-witnesses-in-trumps-impeachment-trial|url-status=live}}</ref>

Federal judge [[Royce Lamberth]] ruled on March 8, 2021, that Chansley should not be released from jail, saying his lawyer's arguments were "so frivolous as to insult the Court's intelligence." In a written statement, the judge said the "defendant does not fully appreciate the severity of the allegations against him."<ref>{{cite news |last=Shepherd |first=Katie |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2021/03/09/qanon-shaman-jacob-chansley-jail/ |title='QAnon Shaman' stays in jail as judge slams his arguments: 'So frivolous as to insult the Court's intelligence' |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2021 |archive-date=March 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309123627/https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2021/03/09/qanon-shaman-jacob-chansley-jail/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Chansley pleaded guilty to a single count of [[obstructing an official proceeding]] on September 3, 2021, and agreed to accept the prosecution's recommended sentence of 41 to 51 months in prison as part of the settlement. Earlier, his lawyer said Chansley broke away from QAnon and asked that it no longer be used in terms for him.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/03/nyregion/qanon-shaman-capitol-riot-guilty-plea.html |title=Capitol Rioter Known as QAnon Shaman Pleads Guilty |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |first=Alan |last=Feuer |date=September 3, 2021 |access-date=September 3, 2021 |archive-date=September 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210903181914/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/03/nyregion/qanon-shaman-capitol-riot-guilty-plea.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Judge Lamberth turned down a request for release (Chansley wanted to visit his grandfather while Watkins wanted to provide him with shelter and care for his mental health) on the grounds that there was no convincing evidence that there would not be any risk of escape.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/jacob-chansley-qanon-shaman-jan-6-grandfather-release_n_613c2b41e4b00ff836ece5a2 |title=Judge Refuses To Release 'QAnon Shaman' Jacob Chansley Before Sentencing |work=[[HuffPost]] |first=Mary |last=Papenfuss |date=September 11, 2021 |access-date=September 11, 2021 |archive-date=September 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210925010005/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/jacob-chansley-qanon-shaman-jan-6-grandfather-release_n_613c2b41e4b00ff836ece5a2 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Chansley was sentenced to 41 months in prison on November 17.<ref>{{Cite magazine |first=Joe |last=Walsh |title='QAnon Shaman' Jacob Chansley Sentenced To 41 Months In Prison — One Of The Longest Capitol Riot Sentences So Far |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/joewalsh/2021/11/17/qanon-shaman-jacob-chansley-sentenced-to-41-months-in-prison---one-of-the-longest-capitol-riot-sentences-so-far/ |magazine=[[Forbes]] |date=November 17, 2021}}</ref> He served his sentence at [[Federal Correctional Institution, Safford]] in [[Safford, Arizona]],<ref name="Johnson-2022">{{cite web | last=Johnson | first=Jon | title=QAnon Shaman Jacob Chansley held at FCI-Safford | website=The Gila Herald | date=January 20, 2022 | url=https://gilaherald.com/qanon-shaman-jacob-chansley-held-at-fci-safford/ | access-date=March 9, 2023 | archive-date=January 8, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230108072325/https://gilaherald.com/qanon-shaman-jacob-chansley-held-at-fci-safford/ | url-status=live}}</ref> with an original release date of May 25, 2024.<ref name="InmateIntake">{{cite web |title=Federal inmate tracker {{!}} Inmate Intake |url=https://inmateintake.com/inmates/ |access-date=March 27, 2023 |website=Inmate Intake |id=Use "Lookup Inmate" search form with "Register number": 24866-509 |quote= |archive-date=March 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327132432/https://inmateintake.com/inmates/ |url-status=live}}</ref>  On March 30, 2023, attorney Albert Watkins announced Chansley had just been released from prison 14 months early and moved to a [[halfway house]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.abc15.com/news/state/self-proclaimed-qanon-shaman-jacob-chansley-released-from-prison-family-says |title=Self proclaimed 'QAnon Shaman' Jacob Chansley released from prison, family says |work=[[KNXV-TV]] |date=March 30, 2023 |access-date=March 30, 2023 |archive-date=March 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230330162543/https://www.abc15.com/news/state/self-proclaimed-qanon-shaman-jacob-chansley-released-from-prison-family-says |url-status=live}}</ref> In November 2021, Chansley told the court, "Men of honor admit when they're wrong. Not just publicly but to themselves. I was wrong for entering the Capitol. I have no excuse. No excuse whatsoever. The behavior is indefensible."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kim |first1=Juliana |title=U.S. Capitol rioter the 'QAnon Shaman' is released early from federal prison |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/03/31/1167319814/qanon-shaman-jacob-chansley-capitol-riot-early-release-reentry |access-date=March 3, 2024 |work=NPR |date=March 31, 2023}}</ref>

On January 20, 2025, after beginning his [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|second term in office]], President Trump [[Pardon of January 6 United States Capitol attack defendants|issued pardons]] to Chansley and roughly 1,500 other individuals charged with crimes connected to January 6. Chansley celebrated the pardon on [[X (formerly Twitter)]], stating: "J6ers are getting released [and] justice has come. Everything done in the dark will come to light." He also said he would "buy some motha fuckin guns" to commemorate the pardon.<ref name="Liddell-2025" />

==== Disinformation about affiliation and role ====
{{Broader|Antifa (United States)#Capitol attack (2021)|topic=the conspiracy theory that connects antifa to the Capitol attack}}

After the storming of the Capitol, pro-Trump users on Facebook circulated false rumors that Chansley was not a Trump supporter and right-wing advocate but was instead associated with [[Antifa (United States)|antifa]] and the Black Lives Matter (BLM) movement and had infiltrated the event as an [[agent provocateur]]. Those false reports frequently included a photo of Chansley at a BLM rally in Arizona, cropping out his "Q Sent Me" sign that indicates he was a [[counter-protest]]er rather than a participant at the rally.<ref name="MacGuill-2021">{{cite web|url=https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/jake-angeli-viking-capitol-blm/|title=Was Capitol Rioter in Horns and Furs an Antifa Instigator Who Took Part in BLM Protests?|work=[[Snopes]]|last=MacGuill|first=Dan|date=January 7, 2021|access-date=January 9, 2021|archive-date=November 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211110005153/https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/jake-angeli-viking-capitol-blm/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In a January 6 tweet from his [[Twitter]] account, @USAwolfpack, Chansley contradicted speculations made by Trump campaign lawyer [[Lin Wood]]: "Mr. Wood. I am not antifa or blm. I'm a Qanon & digital soldier. My name is Jake & I marched with the police & fought against BLM & ANTIFA in PHX."<ref>[https://twitter.com/USAwolfpack/status/1346989136310398977 USAwolfpack tweet] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109030658/https://twitter.com/USAwolfpack/status/1346989136310398977 |date=January 9, 2021}}, January 6, 2021.</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Palmer |first1=Ewan |title='QAnon Shaman' Who Stormed Capitol Denies He Is Antifa as Conspiracy Theorists Turn on Him |url=https://www.newsweek.com/qshaman-washington-antifa-protest-qanon-1559599 |access-date=January 8, 2021 |work=[[Newsweek]] |date=January 7, 2021 |archive-date=January 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210107235629/https://www.newsweek.com/qshaman-washington-antifa-protest-qanon-1559599 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Snopes]] investigated the statement, concluding that he did attend a BLM rally, that he is not affiliated with antifa, and was an active Trump supporter.<ref name="MacGuill-2021" />

There was also disinformation propagated which falsely claimed Chansley colluded with [[Nancy Pelosi]]'s son-in-law, [[Michiel Vos]], seen in a photo with him outside the Capitol. Snopes wrote that Vos is a reporter with the Dutch [[free-to-air]] television channel [[RTL Nederland]], and the image is from a story on the protests which Vos wrote for the Dutch news program ''[[RTL Boulevard]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/pelosi-angeli-collude-antifa/|title=Did 'Antifa' Jake Angeli Collude With Nancy Pelosi's Son-in-Law?|work=[[Snopes]]|last=MacGuill|first=Dan|date=January 7, 2021|access-date=January 9, 2021|archive-date=November 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211110005929/https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/pelosi-angeli-collude-antifa/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Views ==
{{Trumpism sidebar|people}}
[[File:Jake Angeli (Qanon Shaman), seen holding a Qanon sign (cropped).jpg|thumb|Chansley in 2020]]
Chansley has stated his unfounded belief that televisions and radios emit "very specific frequencies that are inaudible," that "affect the [[brain waves]] of your brain".<ref name="Kunkle-2021" /> He has also spoken about the [[Bilderberg meeting#Conspiracy theories|Bilderberg conspiracy theory]] and said that [[Masonic conspiracy theories#Alleged occult influences on popular culture|Freemasons designed Washington, D.C.]], according to "[[ley lines]]" (that crisscross one another at sacred sites of civilizational importance, such as temples, pyramids, the buildings on the National Mall,<ref name="Packer-2024"/> amplify the [[Earth's magnetic field]],<ref name="Kunkle-2021" /> and which have been debunked by archaeologists and statisticians).<ref>{{cite book |title=Pagan Britain |last=Hutton |first=Ronald |year=2013 |publisher=Yale University Press |location=New Haven and London |isbn=978-0-300-197716 |page=135 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Carroll |first=Robert Todd |title=Ley Lines |website=The Skeptic's Dictionary |url=http://www.skepdic.com/leylines.html |date=December 3, 2015 |access-date=September 16, 2019 }}</ref> During a 2020 interview on [[ORF (broadcaster)|ORF]], Chansley declared that "in order to beat this evil [[occultic]] force you need a light occultic force ... [you need] a force that is of the side of God, of love ... almost like on the side of the angels ... as opposed to the demons."<ref name="Crossley-2021" /> In reflecting on the Capitol storming, Chansley said that "What we did on January 6 in many ways was an evolution in consciousness, because as we marched down the street along these ley lines shouting 'USA' or shouting things like 'freedom'... we were actually affecting the quantum realm."<ref name="Kunkle-2021" />

Prosecutors have alleged that Chansley believes he is an [[Extraterrestrial life|alien]] or higher being and is destined to ascend to another reality;<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/capitol-riot-charges-1.5874440 |title=U.S. federal officials say more than 100 people in custody so far in Capitol riot investigation |date=January 15, 2021 |work=[[CBC News]] |access-date=January 15, 2021 |archive-date=January 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115084135/https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/capitol-riot-charges-1.5874440 |url-status=live}}</ref> he purports to be a [[bodhisattva]] who remains on this plane of reality to lead other conscious beings to ascend this realm.<ref>''[[The David Pakman Show]]'', November 30, 2023</ref> When asked about her son in the wake of the January 2021 attack on the Capitol, his mother, Martha Chansley, said to [[KNXV-TV]], "he's fine," adding that "it takes a lot of courage to be a patriot".<ref name="Palmer-2021" />

In an interview with journalist [[George Packer]] after his release from prison, Chansley expressed great respect for [[Donald Trump]], who, he insisted, had declassified three U.S. patents: “a zero-point-energy engine, infinite free clean energy; a room-temperature superconductor that allows a zero-point-energy engine to function without overheating; and what’s called a TR3B—it’s a triangular-shaped antigravity or inertia-propulsion craft. And when you combine all these things together, you get a whole new socioeconomic-geopolitical system.”<ref name="Packer-2024"/> He also described the Q poster of [[QAnon]] as "a successful psychological operation that disseminated the truth about corruption in our government.”<ref name="Packer-2024"/>

In July 2025, due to Trump's support for funding Israel during the [[Gaza genocide]] and his refusal to release the [[Epstein files]] after promising he would release them,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Clark  |first=Emily |date=July 18, 2025 |title=With the Epstein files, Trump finally hits a line MAGA are unwilling to follow him over |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-07-18/donald-trump-maga-demand-release-of-epstein-fles/105538654 |access-date=July 24, 2025 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> Chansley rescinded his support for Trump.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 23, 2025 |title=Trump Just Lost One of His Most Famous Followers: the QAnon Shaman |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-just-lost-one-most-192027826.html |access-date=July 24, 2025 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sherratt |first=Madeline |date=July 24, 2025 |title=Even the 'QAnon Shaman' has turned on Trump |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/qanon-shaman-trump-epstein-jan-6-b2795134.html |access-date=July 24, 2025 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

'''Myha'la Herrold''' ({{IPAc-en|m|aɪ|ˈ|h|ɑː|l|ə}}<ref>{{cite web |last=Morales |first=Wilson |date=November 6, 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e2bsPsfeEFA&t=8s |title=Myha'la Herrold talks HBO new series 'Industry' |work=BlackFilmandTV.com |via=YouTube |access-date=January 18, 2022 |archive-date=August 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220820071436/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e2bsPsfeEFA&t=8s |url-status=live}}</ref>; born April 6, 1996), known [[mononymously]] as '''Myha'la''', is an American actress. She portrays [[Harper Stern]] in the British television drama ''[[Industry (TV series)|Industry]]'' and had roles in the films ''[[Bodies Bodies Bodies]]'' (2022) and ''[[Leave the World Behind (film)|Leave the World Behind]]'' (2023).

==Early life and education==
Myha'la was born and grew up in [[San Jose, California]].<ref name=pizarro2017/> Her mother, Susan (of English, French and German descent) ran a salon. Her father is Jamaican.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Myha'la Herrold is making the industry work for her |first=Charlie |last=Brinkhurst Cuff |date=August 17, 2022 |magazine=[[gal-dem]] |url=https://gal-dem.com/myhala-herrold-is-making-the-industry-work-for-her/ |access-date=August 21, 2022 |archive-date=August 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220821045507/https://gal-dem.com/myhala-herrold-is-making-the-industry-work-for-her/ |url-status=live}}</ref> She graduated from [[Archbishop Mitty High ==== Public discussion of racial bias in game shows ====
Myha'la's elimination from the second series of [[The Celebrity Traitors series 2|''The Celebrity Traitors'']] in October 2026<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-08 |title=Faithful Myha’la banished from Celebrity Traitors |url=https://uk.news.yahoo.com/faithful-myha-la-banished-celebrity-200600660.html |access-date=2026-10-14 |website=Yahoo News UK |language=en-GB}}</ref> prompted discussion about the potential influence of racial bias on the game. After entrepreneur Chantel Sachanna argued on Instagram that Myha'la had been banished because of her race, the actress offered a more nuanced assessment. She suggested that differences in cultural background and expression might lead other contestants to misinterpret her behavior, adding that she had anticipated this possibility before joining the program.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kanter |first=Jake |date=2026-10-13 |title='Industry' Star Myha'la Claims "Racial Bias" Baked Into 'The Traitors' |url=https://deadline.com/2026/10/industry-myhala-unconscious-racial-bias-the-traitors-1237155474/ |access-date=2026-10-14 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref> Nevertheless, Myha'la considered her own conduct a significant factor in the suspicions against her and disputed the suggestion that her fellow contestants had deliberately targeted her on racial grounds. She also highlighted the value of examining unconscious bias in competitive situations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kanter |first=Jake |date=2026-10-13 |title='Industry' Star Myha'la Claims "Racial Bias" Baked Into 'The Traitors' |url=https://deadline.com/2026/10/industry-myhala-unconscious-racial-bias-the-traitors-1237155474/ |access-date=2026-10-14 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[WWE Performance Center]] |debut = June 24, 2017 }} '''Theresa Lee Schuessler''' (born September 25, 1994) is an American [[professional wrestler]]. {{As of|since=n|lc=n|2022}}, she is signed to [[WWE]], where she performs on the [[SmackDown (WWE brand)|SmackDown]] [[WWE brand extension|brand]] under the [[ring name]] '''Fallon Henley''' and is a member of the [[Fatal Influence]] [[Stable (professional wrestling)|stable]]. She is a former [[List of NXT Women's North American Champions|one-time]] [[NXT Women's North American Champion]], a one-time [[WWE Women's Speed Champion]], a [[List of WWE Women's Tag Team Champions|one-time]] [[WWE Women's Tag Team Champions|WWE Women's Tag Team Champion]], and a [[List of NXT Women's Tag Team Champions|one-time]] [[NXT Women's Tag Team Champion]]. Schuessler, under the ring name '''Tesha Price''', previously performed for various promotions, such as [[All Elite Wrestling]] (AEW), [[Shine Wrestling]], and [[World Xtreme Wrestling]] (WXW). == Early life == Theresa lee Schuessler{{cite web|url=https://www.wwe.com/shows/wwenxt/article/wwe-welcomes-newest-class-of-recruits-to-the-wwe-performance-center|title=WWE welcomes newest class of recruits to the WWE Performance Center|date=March 17, 2022|access-date=June 7, 2025|publisher=[[WWE]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603091133/https://www.wwe.com/shows/wwenxt/article/wwe-welcomes-newest-class-of-recruits-to-the-wwe-performance-center|archive-date=June 3, 2025|url-status=live}} was born in [[Tampa, Florida]], but moved with her family at the age of one to [[Chelsea, Michigan]] owing to her father's work as a pilot. Schuessler graduated from [[Chelsea High School (Michigan)|Chelsea High School]] in 2012 and left when she was 17 years old for college. She attended the [[University of South Florida]] and graduated with a Bachelors in Criminology and a Business certificate.{{cite web|url=https://www.guardiannewspapersmi.com/uploads/1/2/5/8/125836507/chelsea_guardian_12_31_20_final.pdf|title=Chelsea's Tesha Price Dreaming Big in Professional Wrestling|publisher=Chelsea Guardian|date=December 31, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241220174409/https://www.guardiannewspapersmi.com/uploads/1/2/5/8/125836507/chelsea_guardian_12_31_20_final.pdf|archive-date=December 20, 2024|url-status=live}} Schuessler would pursue a wrestling career in 2015, while finishing her senior year. == Professional wrestling career == === Early career (2017–2021) === Schuessler made her [[professional wrestling]] debut at an event held by [[World Xtreme Wrestling]] (WXW) on June 24, 2017, under the [[ring name]] '''Tesha Price'''.{{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=20006|title=Fallon Henley's Cagematch bio|website=cagematch.net|access-date=June 24, 2017}} On December 16, Price made her [[Shine Wrestling]] debut at [[Shine Wrestling events|Shine 47]], competing in a [[Battle royal (professional wrestling)|battle royal]] to determine the number one contender for the [[Shine Championship]], which was won by [[Rain (wrestler)|Rain]]. Later that night, she also competed in a [[four way match]] against Dynamite DiDi, Kikyo, and Robyn Reid, which would be won by DiDi. Price made her [[All Elite Wrestling]] (AEW) debut on the November 6, 2020 episode of ''[[AEW Dark]]'' in a match against [[Big Swole]], which she lost.{{cite web |title=AEW DARK 11/6/20 Results |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/results/aew-dark-11620-results-live-coverage-and-discussion-7pm-est |website=fightful.com |date=November 6, 2020 }} She made her ''[[AEW Dynamite]]'' debut on December 9, where she lost to [[Abadon (wrestler)|Abadon]].{{cite web |date=December 10, 2020 |title=AEW DYNAMITE Results for December 9, 2020 |url=https://www.allelitewrestling.com/post/aew-dynamite-results-for-december-9-2020 |website=allelitewrestling.com}} She went on to have 21 matches in AEW from 2020 to 2021.{{cite web|url=https://aewresults.com/wrestler/tesha-price/|title=Tesha Price - AEW Record|website=aewresults.com|access-date=June 7, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240414041259/https://aewresults.com/wrestler/tesha-price/|archive-date=April 14, 2024|url-status=live}} On December 15, 2021, it was announced she would no longer take independent bookings. === WWE (2018–present) === ==== Early appearances (2018–2022) ==== Schuessler appeared on the July 25, 2018 episode of ''[[WWE NXT|NXT]]'' under the ring name Tenilla Price, losing to [[Lacey Evans]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wwe.com/shows/wwenxt/2018-07-25|title=WWE NXT: July 25, 2018|date=July 25, 2018|work=[[WWE]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215205754/https://www.wwe.com/shows/wwenxt/2018-07-25|archive-date=February 15, 2025|url-status=live}} On August 8, now back under the ring name Tesha Price, she lost to [[Britt Baker]] in a [[dark match]] held during the [[Mae Young Classic (2018)|second annual Mae Young Classic]].
