'''Élie N'Zeyi''' (born 17 October 1997) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder (association football)|midfielder]] for Italian [[Serie D]] club [[ASD Polisportiva Calcio Budoni|Budoni]].

==Club career==
===FK Pohronie===
N'Zeyi was featured for [[FK Pohronie|Pohronie]] in winter friendly games and went on to be signed by the [[Slovakia|Slovak]] [[Slovak Super Liga|Fortuna Liga]] club.<ref>{{Cite web|title=V poslednom prípravnom zápase pred jarnou časťou sme porazili Ružomberok|url=https://www.fkpohronie.sk/v-poslednom-pripravnom-zapase-pred-jarnou-castou-sme-porazili-ruzomberok/?f=|access-date=2021-03-12|website=www.fkpohronie.sk|language=slovak}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Tlačovka pred štartom sezóny. Sledujte naživo cez stream|url=https://www.fkpohronie.sk/tlacovka-pred-startom-sezony.-sledujte-nazivo-cez-stream/?f=|access-date=2021-03-12|website=www.fkpohronie.sk|language=slovak}}</ref>

N'Zeyi was nominated in late February for a league fixture against [[AS Trenčín]] but remained unused.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pohronie vs. Trenčín - 27 February 2021 - Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2021/02/27/slovakia/super-liga/fk-pohronie/fk-as-trencin/3311921/|access-date=2021-03-12|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref> N'Zeyi made his [[Slovak Super Liga|Fortuna Liga]] debut during an [[Štadión FK Senica|away]] fixture on 6 March 2021 against [[FK Senica|Senica]]. He came on in the 89th minute to replace [[Martin Adamec]] and seal the defence. Pohronie was in a narrow 1–0 lead, thanks to a first-half goal by [[Patrik Blahút]]. Senica's late pressure was, however, converted into a last-minute equaliser set by a header from [[Marin Ljubičić (footballer, born 1988)|Marin Ljubičić]]. The match ended in said tie.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Zo Senice odchádzame s bodom. O víťazstvo sme prišli až v závere|url=https://www.fkpohronie.sk/zo-senice-odchadzame-s-bodom.-o-vitazstvo-sme-prisli-az-v-zavere/?f=|access-date=2021-03-12|website=www.fkpohronie.sk|language=slovak}}</ref>

===Finn Harps===
On 11 February 2022, N'Zeyi signed for [[Finn Harps F.C.|Finn Harps]] in the [[League of Ireland Premier Division]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://finnharps.ie/harps-add-midfielder-elie-gael-nzeyi-kibonge/ | title=Harps add midfielder Élie-Gaël N'Zeyi Kibonge – Finn Harps FC }}</ref>

N'Zeyi made his debut for the club on 25 February 2022 in a 0–0 draw away to [[University College Dublin A.F.C.|UCD]] at the [[UCD Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=UCD vs. Finn Harps - 25 February 2022 - Soccerway |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/02/25/ireland-republic/premier-league/university-college-dublin-football-club/finn-harps-football-club/3712457/ |access-date=2022-02-28 |website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref>

'''Benny Díaz Jáuregui''' (born December 15, 1998) is an American professional [[Association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Liga MX]] club [[FC Juárez|Juárez]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=FC Juarez Facebook page |url=https://www.facebook.com/reel/2154441508234195}}</ref> in the United States, Díaz began his career with [[Cimarrones de Sonora]] before joining [[Liga MX]] club [[Querétaro F.C.|Querétaro]].<ref name="Tijuana">{{cite news |title=BENNY DÍAZ SE INCORPORA AL CLUB TIJUANA |url=http://www.xolos.com.mx/noticias/xoloitzcuintles/6212/benny-d-az-se-incorpora-al-club-tijuana.html |access-date=April 4, 2021 |work=[[Club Tijuana]] |archive-date=June 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200619072021/http://xolos.com.mx/noticias/xoloitzcuintles/6212/benny-d-az-se-incorpora-al-club-tijuana.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Prior to the [[2020–21 Liga MX season|2020–21]] season, Díaz signed with [[Club Tijuana|Tijuana]].<ref name="Tijuana"/> He made his professional debut for the club on April 3, 2021, against [[Atlas F.C.|Atlas]], coming on as a 60th-minute substitute as Tijuana were defeated 1–0, the goal being scored prior to Díaz coming on.<ref>{{cite web |title=Atlas 1–0 Tijuana |url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2021/04/04/mexico/primera-division/club-atlas-de-guadalajara/club-tijuana-xoloitzcuintles-de-caliente/3433346/ |website=Soccerway}}</ref>

On January 18, 2023, Díaz joined [[El Paso Locomotive FC|El Paso Locomotive]] on a loan deal through the [[2023 USL Championship season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Locomotive FC acquires goalkeeper Benny Diaz on loan |url=https://www.uslchampionship.com/news_article/show/1255878 |website=USLChampionship.com |date=January 18, 2023 |publisher=[[USL Championship]] |access-date=18 January 2023}}</ref>

'''Alef Mangueira Severino Pereira''' (born 29 November 1994), known as '''Alef Manga''', is a Brazilian [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Clube do Remo|Remo]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Santos, São Paulo|Santos]], [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]], Alef Manga began his career at a [[futsal]] club in his hometown called Saldanha da Gama, at the age of five. In 2007, aged 12, he was invited to play for the [[Santos FC Futsal|futsal team]] of [[Santos FC|Santos]], and later moved to football. However, he was released in 2011 and subsequently represented [[Jabaquara Atlético Clube|Jabaquara]] and [[São Vicente Atlético Clube|São Vicente]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://interativos.globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/materia/xxxxxx-alef-manga|title=O sonho de Alef Manga|trans-title=The dream of Alef Manga|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|GloboEsporte.com]]|language=pt-BR|date=10 April 2021|accessdate=28 April 2021}}</ref>

After finishing his formation, Alef Manga made his senior debut with [[Campeonato Paulista Segunda Divisão]] side [[Bandeirante Esporte Clube|Bandeirante]]; at that time, he was known as ''Dodô''. He returned to Jabaquara for the 2016 season, and moved to the [[Paraná (state)|Paraná state]] in 2017 to join [[Cascavel Clube Recreativo|Cascavel CR]].

Alef Manga was the top scorer of the second division of the [[Campeonato Paranaense]] for Cascavel, and was also the top scorer of the year's [[Taça FPF]], while playing for [[Maringá Futebol Clube|Maringá]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/pr/blogs/especial-blog/boleiros-e-barangas/post/maringa-marchiori-manga.html|title=Maringá, Marchiori e Manga|trans-title=Maringá, Marchiori and Manga|publisher=Boleiros e Barangas|language=pt-BR|date=5 November 2017|accessdate=28 April 2021}}</ref> He moved to [[Futebol Clube Cascavel|FC Cascavel]] for the 2018 Paranaense, but was loaned back to Maringá on 28 March of that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.catve.com/2021/index.php?p=noticia&id_editoria=3&id_noticia=211972&topo=topo_cinza|title=Futebol: Alef Manga do FCC é emprestado ao Maringá|trans-title=Football: Alef Manga from ''FCC'' is loaned to Maringá|publisher=Catve.com|language=pt-BR|date=28 March 2018|accessdate=28 April 2021|archive-date=30 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210430162616/https://www.catve.com/2021/index.php?p=noticia&id_editoria=3&id_noticia=211972&topo=topo_cinza|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Alef Manga was released by Maringá in May 2018, after only two matches,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.futebolinterior.com.br/futebol/Brasileiro/Serie-D/2018/noticias/2018-05/serie-d-maringa-dispensa-alef-manga-ex-jabaquara-e-bandeirante-sp|title=Série D: Maringá dispensa Alef Manga, ex-atacante de Jabaquara e Bandeirante-SP|trans-title=Série D: Maringá release Alef Manga, former Jabaquara and Bandeirante-SP forward|publisher=Futebol Interior|language=pt-BR|date=28 May 2018|accessdate=28 April 2021}}</ref> and agreed to a move abroad in August, joining [[U.D. Oliveirense|Oliveirense]] of the Portuguese [[LigaPro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fccascavel.com.br/noticias/do-fc-cascavel-para-portugal-atacante-alef-manga-vai-jogar-em-gramados-lusitanos|title=Do FC Cascavel para Portugal: atacante Alef Manga vai jogar em gramados lusitanos|trans-title=From FC Cascavel to Portugal: forward Alef Manga will play in Portuguese fields|publisher=FC Cascavel|language=pt-BR|date=30 August 2018|accessdate=28 April 2021|archive-date=8 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108044648/https://fccascavel.com.br/noticias/do-fc-cascavel-para-portugal-atacante-alef-manga-vai-jogar-em-gramados-lusitanos|url-status=dead}}</ref> After struggling with injuries, he returned to Brazil in 2019, and subsequently joined [[Associação Atlética Coruripe|Coruripe]].

Alef Manga moved to [[Agremiação Sportiva Arapiraquense|ASA]] in April 2019,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asadearapiraca.com.br/noticia/1601-novo-reforco-alef-manga-ja-se-sente-em-casa-no-gramado-do-asa|title=Novo reforço {{!}} Alef Manga já se sente em casa no gramado do ASA|trans-title=New addition {{!}} Alef Manga is already at home in ASA's field|publisher=Agremiação Sportiva Arapiraquense|language=pt-BR|date=26 April 2019|accessdate=28 April 2021|archive-date=8 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108044648/https://www.asadearapiraca.com.br/noticia/1601-novo-reforco-alef-manga-ja-se-sente-em-casa-no-gramado-do-asa|url-status=dead}}</ref> but left the club in June after their elimination from the [[2020 Campeonato Brasileiro Série D|2020 Série D]]. In July, he agreed to a deal with [[Associação Portuguesa de Desportos|Portuguesa]] for the year's [[Copa Paulista]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://netlusa.com.br/2019/07/16/portuguesa-acerta-com-dois-reforcos-para-o-ataque/|title=Portuguesa acerta com dois reforços para o ataque|trans-title=Portuguesa sign two additions for the attack|publisher=NetLusa|language=pt-BR|date=16 July 2019|accessdate=28 April 2021}}</ref> but left on 2 August without making a single appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://netlusa.com.br/2019/08/02/alef-manga-e-mais-um-a-deixar-a-portuguesa-sem-estrear/|title=Alef Manga é mais um a deixar a Portuguesa sem estrear|trans-title=Alef Manga is another one to leave Portuguesa without debuting|publisher=NetLusa|language=pt-BR|date=2 August 2019|accessdate=28 April 2021}}</ref>

On 9 December 2019, Alef Manga agreed to join [[Resende Futebol Clube|Resende]] for the [[2020 Campeonato Carioca]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/rj/sul-do-rio-costa-verde/futebol/campeonato-carioca/noticia/resende-fecha-com-atacante-alef-manga-para-o-carioca-2020.ghtml|title=Resende fecha com atacante Alef Manga para o Carioca 2020|trans-title=Resende sign with forward Alef Manga for the 2020 Carioca|publisher=GloboEsporte.com|language=pt-BR|date=9 December 2019|accessdate=28 April 2021}}</ref> He then returned to Coruripe the following July, but moved to [[Volta Redonda Futebol Clube|Volta Redonda]] on 24 September 2020, as a replacement to [[Saulo Rodrigues da Silva|Saulo Mineiro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/rj/sul-do-rio-costa-verde/futebol/noticia/voltaco-anuncia-contratacao-do-atacante-alef-manga.ghtml|title=Voltaço anuncia contratação do atacante Alef Manga|trans-title=''Voltaço'' announce the signing of forward Alef Manga|publisher=GloboEsporte.com|language=pt-BR|date=24 September 2020|accessdate=28 April 2021}}</ref>

After impressing with ''Voltaço'' in the [[2020 Campeonato Brasileiro Série C|2020 Série C]], Alef Manga signed a permanent two-year deal with the club on 7 January 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/rj/sul-do-rio-costa-verde/futebol/noticia/voltaco-renova-contrato-do-atacante-alef-manga-por-mais-dois-anos.ghtml|title=Voltaço renova contrato do atacante Alef Manga por mais dois anos|trans-title=''Voltaço'' renew contract of forward Alef Manga for two more years|publisher=GloboEsporte.com|language=pt-BR|date=7 January 2021|accessdate=28 April 2021}}</ref> He went on to score nine goals in the [[2021 Campeonato Carioca|2021 Carioca]] with the club.

===Goiás===
Alef Manga moved to [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série B|Série B]] side [[Goiás Esporte Clube|Goiás]] on loan in May 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goiasec.com.br/alef-manga-eu-vim-para-ajudar-e-fazer-gols/|title=Alef Manga: "Eu vim para ajudar e fazer gols"|trans-title=Alef Manga: "I came here to help and score goals"|publisher=Goiás EC|language=pt-BR|date=11 May 2021|accessdate=9 December 2021|archive-date=9 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209195514/https://www.goiasec.com.br/alef-manga-eu-vim-para-ajudar-e-fazer-gols/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Regularly used, he contributed with ten goals in Goiás' [[2021 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|promotion]] to the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]].

===Coritiba===
[[File:Alef Manga - Brasileirão Série A- Bragantino 4 x 2 Coritiba.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Manga with [[Coritiba Foot Ball Club|Coritiba]] in 2022]]
On 30 December 2021, Alef Manga joined [[Coritiba Foot Ball Club|Coritiba]], also promoted to the top tier, on a one-year loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://coritiba.com.br/artigo/38464/contratacao_para_o_elenco_2022|title=Contratação para o elenco 2022|trans-title=Signing for the 2022 squad|publisher=Coritiba FBC|language=pt-BR|date=30 December 2021|accessdate=1 January 2022}}</ref> On 10 November of the following year, after being an undisputed starter for most of [[2022 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|the campaign]], he signed a permanent two-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/pr/blogs/blog-da-nadja/post/2022/11/10/pele-neymar-manga-fica-coritiba-crava-permanencia-do-atacante.ghtml|title=Coritiba acerta a permanência de Alef Manga por mais duas temporadas|trans-title=Coritiba agree the permanence of Alef Manga for two more seasons|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=10 November 2022|accessdate=11 November 2022}}</ref>

On 13 May 2023, Alef Manga's contract with Coritiba was suspended, as a result of his involvement in the [[2023 Brazilian football match-fixing scandal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.terra.com.br/esportes/coritiba/coritiba-suspende-contrato-de-alef-manga-citado-em-investigacao-sobre-esquema-de-apostas-manipuladas,0cde3eec4cbaa6e9e6384c3ddc8c56a7utxcbnz8.html|title=Coritiba suspende contrato de Alef Manga, citado em investigação sobre esquema de apostas manipuladas|trans-title=Coritiba suspend contract of Alef Manga, cited in investigation over fixed betting schemes|publisher=Terra|language=pt-BR|date=13 May 2023|accessdate=15 May 2023}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=1 August 2023 |title=Brazilian player involved in match-fixing scandal transfers to Cyprus |url=https://www.ekathimerini.com/sports/1216857/brazilian-player-involved-in-match-fixing-scandal-transfers-to-cyprus/ |access-date=16 August 2023 |website=Kathimerini}}</ref> On 28 July, he was loaned to Cypriot side [[Pafos FC|Pafos]] for one year;<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coritiba.com.br/Artigo/39817/comunicado_oficial|title=Comunicado oficial|trans-title=Official announcement|publisher=Coritiba FBC|language=pt-BR|date=28 July 2023|accessdate=28 July 2023}}</ref> while the player was not allowed to play in official competitions in Brazil as long as he stood trial, the ban did not extend to any foreign leagues.<ref name=":0" />

'''Hannah Einbinder''' ({{ipac-en|'|aɪ|n|.|b|aɪ|n|d|ər}} {{respell|EYEN|byne|dər}};<ref>{{cite av media |people=Einbinder, Hannah |date=June 21, 2026 |title=Hannah Einbinder's Closet Picks |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FDm1avEBSBM&t=15s |work=[[The Criterion Collection|Criterion]] |access-date=August 7, 2026 |time=0:15 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> born May 21, 1995) is an American actress and stand-up comedian. She is best known for her starring role as struggling comedy writer Ava Daniels in the [[HBO Max]] comedy-drama series ''[[Hacks]]'' (2021–2026), for which she received [[#Awards and nominations|various accolades]] including a [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series|Primetime Emmy Award]] and [[Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series|Critics' Choice Television Award]], as well as nominations for four [[Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actress – Series, Miniseries or Television Film|Golden Globes]]. Einbinder had her first starring roles in a film in the 2026 comedy ''[[Seekers of Infinite Love]]'' and the horror drama ''[[Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma]]''.

== Early life and education ==
Einbinder is the daughter of original ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' cast member [[Laraine Newman]] and writer/director Chad Einbinder.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosemberg |first=Jasmin |date=2024-05-31 |title='Hacks' Star Hannah Einbinder Doesn't Want to Be Categorized |url=https://lamag.com/tv/hannah-einbinder-hacks-max-pride |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=LAmag - Culture, Food, Fashion, News & Los Angeles |language=en}}</ref> She grew up in Los Angeles in a Jewish family.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Zinoman|first=Jason|date=May 12, 2021|title=Hannah Einbinder: Portrait of a Young Comic on the Cusp|language=en-US|location=New York|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/12/arts/television/hannah-einbinder-hacks.html|access-date=May 16, 2021|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hollywood Star Hannah Einbinder Talks Zionism, Jewish Identity, and Palestinian Liberation |url=https://zeteo.com/p/beyond-israelism-simone-zimmerman-hannah-einbinder |website=Zeteo |access-date=10 October 2025}}</ref>

As a teenager, Einbinder was a competitive cheerleader.<ref name="Bustle-2022">{{Cite web |date=2022-09-06 |title=Hannah Einbinder Lets Down Her Armor |url=https://www.bustle.com/entertainment/hannah-einbinder-hbo-max-hacks-emmys |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=Bustle |language=en}}</ref> She graduated from [[Beverly Hills High School]]<ref name="Frick-2021">{{Cite web |last=Frick |first=Evelyn |date=2021-07-23 |title=18 Things to Know About Hannah Einbinder |url=https://www.heyalma.com/18-things-to-know-about-hannah-einbinder/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=Hey Alma |language=en-US}}</ref> and went on to study broadcast journalism at [[Chapman University]] before earning a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in television writing and production.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hannah Einbinder at Improv|url=https://improv.com/comic/hannah+einbinder/|access-date=May 16, 2021|website=Improv|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Bustle-2022" /> At Chapman, Einbinder joined the school's improv team and had her first experience with stand-up comedy when she opened for [[Nicole Byer]] for a campus show.<ref name="Bustle-2022" /><ref name="Frick-2021" />

== Career ==
In 2019, Einbinder appeared in the [[Just for Laughs]] festival's New Faces showcase and was named by [[National Public Radio]] as one of the 10 standout comedians to watch.<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Faces Emerge At The World's Biggest Comedy Festival| url= https://www.npr.org/2019/07/30/746330491/new-faces-shine-at-the-worlds-biggest-comedy-festival| access-date=May 16, 2021|website=NPR.org| date= July 30, 2019|language=en | publisher=[[National Public Radio]]| last1= Limbong| first1= Andrew}}</ref> She was also named one of [[Vulture (website)|''Vulture'']]'s best new up-and-coming comedians to watch in 2019; she was recognized for "her refreshingly absurdist charm."<ref>{{Cite web|last2=Clark|first=Jake | last=Kroeger | first2= Anne Victoria|date=October 29, 2019|title=The Comedians You Should and Will Know of 2019| url= https://www.vulture.com/2019/10/best-new-up-and-coming-comedians-to-watch-in-2019.html| access-date= May 16, 2021|website=Vulture|language=en-us}}</ref> The same year, she was among the "New Faces of Comedy" at Just for Laughs.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.unitedtalent.com/talent/comedy-touring/hannah-einbinder |access-date=2024-01-15| title= Hannah Einbinder | website = unitedtalent.com}}</ref>

In March 2020, she made her national television debut on ''[[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert]]''<ref>{{Citation|title=Hannah Einbinder: This Is What Happens When Your Parents Wish For A Boy| date=March 7, 2020 | url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5i6dUdMoX3w|language=en | via= YouTube |access-date= May 16, 2021}}</ref> and at the time was the youngest person to do a stand-up set on the show.{{fact|date=September 2026}}

Starting in 2021, she co-starred as Ava Daniels in ''[[Hacks]]'' on [[HBO Max]], together with [[Jean Smart]] and [[Carl Clemons-Hopkins]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Otterson|first=Joe|date=February 8, 2021|title=Jean Smart Comedy Series at HBO Max Adds 10 to Cast, Including Hannah Einbinder and Carl Clemons-Hopkins| url= https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/jean-smart-comedy-series-hbo-max-cast-1234903468/|access-date=May 16, 2021|website=Variety|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=D’addario|first=Daniel|date=June 15, 2021|title= Why 'Hacks' Wouldn't Work Without Ava as Deborah Vance's Prickly Foil| url= https://variety.com/2021/tv/columns/hannah-einbinder-ava-hacks-1234997394/ |access-date=June 20, 2021|website=Variety|language=en-US}}</ref> The show received a total of 15 [[Emmy]] nominations, including acting nominations for Einbinder, Smart, and Clemons-Hopkins.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last= Canfield|first= David|date=July 14, 2021 |title= How ''Hacks'' Became an Even Bigger Emmy Power Player Than Expected| url= https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2021/07/hacks-emmy-nominations-hannah-einbinder
 |access-date=July 23, 2021|magazine=Vanity Fair|language=en-US}}</ref>

She was on [[Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]'s List of "10 Comics to Watch for 2021".<ref>{{Cite web | last=Ferme | first=Antonio | last2=Gilchrist  | first2=Todd  | last3=Miller  | first3=Stuart  | last4=Plunkett  | first4=Paul  | last5=Shanfeld | first5=Ethan |date=2021-07-27 |title=Variety's 10 Comics to Watch for 2021 |url=https://variety.com/lists/varietys-10-comics-to-watch-for-2021/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> She continued to perform stand-up comedy and toured nationally during the summer of 2022.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dodes |first1=Rachel |title=Into the Real With Hannah Einbinder |url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a39994178/hannah-einbinder-hacks/ |publisher=Esquire |date=May 16, 2022}}</ref> [[Max (streaming service)|Max]] released her debut stand-up special in June 2024, ''Hannah Einbinder: Everything Must Go.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zuckerman |first=Esther |date=2024-06-07 |title=With 'Everything Must Go,' Hannah Einbinder returns to her first passion: stand-up |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/tv/story/2024-06-07/hannah-einbinder-everything-must-go-hacks |access-date=2024-09-29 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

In May 2025, it was announced that she would star alongside [[Gillian Anderson]] in [[Jane Schoenbrun]]'s [[slasher film]], ''[[Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma]]''. Einbinder played a lead role in the [[Mubi (streaming service)|Mubi]] and [[Plan B Entertainment|Plan B]] production.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grobar |first=Matt |date=2025-05-09 |title=Hannah Einbinder & Gillian Anderson Board Jane Schoenbrun's 'Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma' For Mubi And Plan B |url=https://deadline.com/2025/05/jane-schoenbrun-teenage-sex-and-death-at-camp-miasma-cast-1236390856/ |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ritman |first=Alex |date=2025-05-09 |title=Hannah Einbinder, Gillian Anderson to Lead Slasher 'Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma' From 'I Saw the TV Glow' Director and Mubi |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/global/hannah-einbinder-gillian-anderson-slasher-jane-schoenbrun-1236391951/ |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Activism ==
In March 2025, Einbinder spoke about several issues while accepting the [[Human Rights Campaign|HRC Visibility Award]]. In her speech, she voiced her concerns about [[climate change]], condemning the "architects of humanity's slow extinction and the destruction of planet Earth." She also denounced the detention of [[detention of Mahmoud Khalil|pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil]], [[Israeli war crimes in the Gaza war|the Israeli government's actions]] in the [[Gaza genocide]], and [[United States support for Israel in the Gaza war|the United States government's support for Israel]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Collins |first=Rance |date=March 23, 2025 |title=Hannah Einbinder and Janelle Monáe Denounce Donald Trump’s Politics at Human Rights Campaign Dinner: ‘Bullies Only Win When We Let Them Think They Can’ |url=https://variety.com/2025/scene/news/hannah-einbinder-janelle-monae-human-rights-campaign-dinner-1236345943/ |access-date=September 15, 2025 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Factora |first=James |date=March 24, 2025 |title=Hannah Einbinder Did Not Hold Back in HRC Speech Condemning Big Oil, Advocating for Palestinians |url=https://www.them.us/story/hannah-einbinder-hrc-speech-condemning-big-oil-advocating-for-palestinians |access-date=September 15, 2025 |website=[[Them (magazine)|Them]]}}</ref>

In May 2025, Einbinder signed on to a letter criticizing the film industry's "passivity" during the [[Gaza genocide]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ritman |first=Alex |date=May 13, 2025 |title=Mark Ruffalo, Guy Pearce, Melissa Barrera and Ralph Fiennes Among 350+ Figures to Sign Letter About Killing of Palestinian Protagonist of Cannes-Bound Doc: ‘We Are Ashamed’ of Industry ‘Passivity’ (EXCLUSIVE) |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/global/letter-about-killing-of-fatma-hassona-1236391687/ |access-date=September 15, 2025 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> In September 2025, she signed the [[Film Workers for Palestine]] pledge, a campaign in which film professionals commit not to work with Israeli film institutions implicated in genocide and [[Israeli apartheid|apartheid]] against Palestinians.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gardner |first1=Chris |date=September 8, 2025 |title=Ayo Edebiri, Olivia Colman, Mark Ruffalo and Yorgos Lanthimos Back Boycott of Israeli Film Institutions |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/ayo-edebiri-mark-ruffalo-boycott-israeli-film-institutions-1236364989/ |website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Film Workers for Palestine |url=https://filmworkersforpalestine.org/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Film Workers for Palestine |language=en}}</ref>

acceptance speech with the words, "Go [[Philadelphia Eagles|Birds]], fuck [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|ICE]], and free Palestine!"<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lindsay September 2025 |language=en-AU |date=16 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=Julia |last2=Wenger |first2=Stephanie |title=Hannah Einbinder Gets Bleeped at Emmys 2025 After |access-date=September 17, 2025 |work=[[Haaretz]]}}</ref>

In October 2025, Einbinder was interviewed for [[Zeteo]] by [[Simone Zimmerman]], one of the subjects in the documentary ''[[Israelism (film)|Israelism]]''.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X-eLWZLs8Q8 |title=Why Hannah Einbinder Said ‘FREE PALESTINE’ — And What Came Next |date=2025-10-26 |last=Zeteo |access-date=2025-11-15 |via=YouTube}}</ref> She also signed a pledge to boycott ''[[The New York Times]]'' over its alleged [[anti-Palestinian]] bias in its [[List of The New York Times controversies#Gaza war coverage|coverage of the Gaza war]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dayan |first1=Linda |title='Genocide Is Not an Opinion': A-listers Boycott The New York Times Over 'anti-Palestinian Bias' |url=https://www.haaretz.com/us-news/2025-10-28/ty-article/.premium/genocide-is-not-an-opinion-a-listers-boycott-the-times-over-anti-palestinian-bias/0000019a-2aa5-ddf1-a1db-fefd1e130000 |access-date=October 28, 2025 |work=[[Haaretz]] |date=October 28, 2025}}</ref> In the same interview, Einbinder expressed opposition to [[Zionism]], specifically [[Liberal Zionism]] which she claimed allowed Zionists to not "reckon with the necessary elements for the ideology to thrive". She also called Zionism a "[[Settler colonialism|settler-colonialist]] ideology" that used [[Israeli apartheid|apartheid]] as a "vehicle" to maintain a Jewish majority <ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/shorts/spFoy0uOqSU |title=Hannah Einbinder rejects "liberal Zionism" in Zeteo interview |language=en |access-date=2026-09-24 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>. 

In January 2026, after the [[killing of Renée Good]] in [[Minneapolis]], Einbinder posted an [[Instagram]] comment calling on artists and creatives to use their platforms to condemn [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|ICE]]. In the same post Einbinder wrote, "The [[imperial boomerang]] has come back home. What we FUND and allow to happen to Palestinians by the hands of the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] who TRAIN ICE will happen to our people here in America. They poisoned [[Flint Michigan]] and got away with it so they knew they could put Al data centers in poor communities and poison their water too. [[Hawaii]] burned and real estate developers snatched up the land from generational locals and they got away with it. So when LOS ANGELES burned the developers knew they could do the same here. And if this sadist [[Nazi]] murderer JONATHAN ROSS who killed RENEE NICOLE GOOD for consciously observing an ICE raid gets away with it? None of us are safe".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garner |first=Glenn |date=2026-01-10 |title=Hannah Einbinder Calls To Abolish ICE After Renee Good Killing: “None Of Us Are Safe” |url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/hannah-einbinder-abolish-ice-renee-good-killing-1236678374/ |access-date=2026-01-12 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Roberto Óscar Albuquerque''' (born November 4, 1993) is an American [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for Spanish club [[Caudal Deportivo|Caudal]].

==Career==
===Youth===
Albuquerque played club soccer with Chicago Magic PSG between 2009 and 2012. He also played high school soccer at [[Crystal Lake South High School]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://kcroos.com/sports/mens-soccer/roster/roberto-albuquerque/1607|title=Roberto Albuquerque - 2015 - Men's Soccer|website=University of Missouri-Kansas City}}</ref>

===College===
In 2012, Albuquerque attended the [[University of Missouri–Kansas City]] to play [[College soccer in the United States|college soccer]]. With the Roos, Albuquerque made 63 appearances and scored 4 goals over four seasons.<ref name="auto"/>

===Professional===
Albuquerque started his professional career in 2018 in Spain, playing with fourth-tier [[Tercera División]] side [[CD Lealtad|Lealtad]]. He then spent a season with [[CD Mensajero|Mensajero]], before moving to third-tier side [[Real Avilés CF|Real Avilés]]. On June 19, 2021, Albuquerque returned to the United States, joining [[USL Championship]] side [[Rio Grande Valley FC]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rgvfc.com/news_article/show/1170435-defender-robert-albuquerque-signs-with-rgv-fc|title=DEFENDER ROBERT ALBUQUERQUE SIGNS WITH RGV FC|first=Toros|last=Communications|date=June 19, 2021|website=Rio Grande Valley FC|access-date=June 20, 2021|archive-date=June 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628074438/https://www.rgvfc.com/news_article/show/1170435-defender-robert-albuquerque-signs-with-rgv-fc|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut the same day, starting against [[San Antonio FC]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uslchampionship.com/sanantoniofc-riograndevalleyfc-2199540|title=San Antonio FC vs. Rio Grande Valley FC- June 19, 2021 | USLChampionship.com|website=www.uslchampionship.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is the son of Oscar Albuquerque and Lina Storti. He has two siblings, a twin sister and brother. His father played 15 years professionally in the [[Major Indoor Soccer League (1978–1992)|MISL]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Roberto Albuquerque - 2015 - Men's Soccer |url=https://kcroos.com/sports/mens-soccer/roster/roberto-albuquerque/1607 |website=Kansas City Roos |access-date=3 October 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Kenia Guadalupe Flores Osuna''' (born 15 July 1999), known professionally as '''Kenia Os''', is a Mexican singer and social media personality. She was a content creator on [[YouTube]] with a team of creators where she amassed millions of subscribers, before continuing on her own.<ref>{{Cite web |first= |date=February 12, 2022 |title=Kenia Os |language=es}}</ref> She signed with Lizos Music in 2018, releasing her debut single "Por Siempre".<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 20, 2019 |title=Kenia Os combina faceta de youtuber con música |url=https://pulsoslp.com.mx/camerino/kenia-os-combina-faceta-de-youtuber-con-musica/896877 |url-status=live |website=Notimex |language=es}}</ref> After a period as an independent artist, she signed with [[Sony Music Mexico]] and released her debut studio album, ''Cambios de Luna'' (2022),<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 11, 2022 |title=Kenia os lanzará 'Cambios de luna': su primer álbum |url=https://www.milenio.com/espectaculos/musica/kenia-os-lanzara-su-primer-album-cambios-de-luna |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220313090416/https://www.milenio.com/espectaculos/musica/kenia-os-lanzara-su-primer-album-cambios-de-luna |archive-date=March 13, 2022 |access-date=May 9, 2022 |website=[[Milenio]] |language=es}}</ref> followed by the successful albums ''K23'' (2023) and ''[[Pink Aura]]'' (2024).<ref>{{Cite web |last=GUERRERO |first=PATRICIA |date=2024-04-25 |title=“Es el álbum donde me siento más completa como artista”: Kenia Os sobre Pink Aura |url=https://es.rollingstone.com/es-el-album-donde-me-siento-mas-completa-como-artista-kenia-os-sobre-pink-aura/ |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=Rolling Stone en Español |language=es}}</ref>

She has expanded her career into television, co-hosting the [[2021 MTV MIAW Awards]] and appearing on streaming shows such as [[HBO Max]]'s ''Bake Off Celebrity: Mexico''.<ref name=":22">{{Cite web |last=Villa |first=Lucas |date=June 9, 2021 |title=Karol G, Bad Bunny And Danna Paola Lead 2021 MTV MIAW Nominations |url=https://wearemitu.com/latidomusic/mtv-miaw-2021-nominations/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220502162711/https://wearemitu.com/latidomusic/mtv-miaw-2021-nominations/ |archive-date=May 2, 2022 |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=Mitú |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite web |author=Forbes Staff |date=July 2, 2021 |title=Esta es la primera producción original mexicana que llegará a HBO Max |url=https://www.forbes.com.mx/forbes-life/entretenimiento-hbo-max-el-gran-pastelero-bake-off-mexico-estreno/amp/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220502162711/https://www.forbes.com.mx/forbes-life/entretenimiento-hbo-max-el-gran-pastelero-bake-off-mexico-estreno/amp/ |archive-date=May 2, 2022 |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=[[Forbes|Forbes Mexico]] |language=es}}</ref> Her accolades include seven [[MTV MIAW Awards]], an [[MTV Europe Music Award]], and a [[Heat Latin Music Awards|Heat Latin Music Award]], in addition to a nomination for a [[Latin Grammy Award for Best Long Form Music Video]].

== Career ==
In 2015, she created her first [[YouTube|YouTube channel]], later joining the Jukilop group.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Vargas |first=Diana |date=January 6, 2022 |title=Te decimos cómo se hizo famosa Kenia Os y cuál es su nombre real |url=https://www.explica.me/entretenimiento/Te-decimos-como-se-hizo-famosa-Kenia-Os-y-cual-es-su-nombre-real-20220106-0006.html |journal=Explica.me |access-date=January 2, 2024 |archive-date=October 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001101949/https://www.explica.me/entretenimiento/Te-decimos-como-se-hizo-famosa-Kenia-Os-y-cual-es-su-nombre-real-20220106-0006.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2018, she left the group following disagreements in her contract. Due to a previous contract, Os's social networks were deleted because they no longer belonged to her. '''Ekain Zenitagoia Arana''' (born 29 April 1994), simply known as '''Ekain''', is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Real Murcia CF|Murcia]].

==Club career==
Ekain was born in [[Durango, Biscay|Durango]], [[Biscay]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], and finished his formation with hometown side [[SCD Durango]]. He made his senior debut with {{ill|Iurretako KT|eu|Iurretako Kirol Taldea}} in 2013, in the regional leagues, before returning to ''Cultu'' in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD03/PUB/2015/08/21/EMD20150821024MDV.pdf|title=Suplen las numerosas ‘fugas’ con gente de casa|trans-title=They replace the numerous "exodus" with home-grown people|publisher=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=21 August 2015|accessdate=10 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deia.eus/deportes/futbol/2018/05/31/futbol-debe/651704.html|title="El fútbol nos debe una"|trans-title="Football owe us one"|publisher=[[Deia (newspaper)|Deia]]|language=es|date=31 May 2018|accessdate=10 August 2021}}</ref>

Ekain scored a career-best 18 goals for Durango during the [[2017–18 Tercera División|2017–18 season]], as his club returned to [[Segunda División B]] after 12 years. He scored a further eight times in [[2018–19 Segunda División B|the following campaign]], but could not prevent his team's relegation.

On 19 June 2019, Ekain signed for [[SD Amorebieta]] in the third division.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sdamorebieta.eus/?p=9679&lang=es|title=Ekain Zenitagoia, primer fichaje para la 2019–20|trans-title=Ekain Zenitagoia, first signing for the 2019–20|publisher=SD Amorebieta|language=es|date=19 June 2019|accessdate=10 August 2021|archive-date=13 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813200259/http://sdamorebieta.eus/?p=9679&lang=es|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 13 August 2020, after scoring nine goals, he moved to fellow league team [[UD Ibiza]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ibizaud.com/en/ekain-is-an-ibiza-player/|title=Ekain is an Ibiza player|publisher=UD Ibiza|date=13 August 2020|accessdate=10 August 2021|archive-date=23 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210523203554/https://www.ibizaud.com/en/ekain-is-an-ibiza-player/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Mainly used as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]], Ekain scored Ibiza's goal in a 1–0 win over [[UCAM Murcia CF]] on 23 May 2021, which sealed the club's [[2020–21 Segunda División B|first-ever promotion]] to [[Segunda División]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.diariodeibiza.es/deporte-base/2021/05/29/vez-veo-gol-penalti-ascenso-52378338.html|title=Ekain Zenitagoia: "Cada vez que veo el gol del penalti del ascenso se me pone la piel de gallina"|trans-title=Ekain Zenitagoia: "Each time that I see the penalty goal of promotion I get goosebumps"|publisher=Diario de Ibiza|language=es|date=29 May 2021|accessdate=10 August 2021}}</ref> He made his professional debut at the age of 27 on 13 August, starting in a 0–0 away draw against [[Real Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/zaragoza-vs-ibiza/cronica/2021/08/14/6116d20e268e3e4d628b45ff.html|title=El Zaragoza decepciona y empata ante un valiente Ibiza|trans-title=Zaragoza disappoint and draw against a valiant Ibiza|publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=13 August 2021|accessdate=13 August 2021}}</ref>

On 15 June 2023, after Ibiza's [[2022–23 Segunda División|relegation]], Ekain signed a two-year contract with [[Racing de Santander]] also in the second division.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realracingclub.es/noticias/ekain-zenitagoia-segundo-fichaje-racinguista-para-la-nueva-temporada|title=Ekain, segundo refuerzo del Racing para la temporada 2023/24|trans-title=Ekain, second addition fo Racing for the 2023/24 season|publisher=Racing Santander|language=es|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=2 July 2023}}</ref>

On 19 July 2025, Ekain signed with [[Real Murcia CF|Murcia]] in [[Primera Federación]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Real Murcia CF|url=https://www.realmurcia.es/ekain-un-atacante-versatil-y-experimentado-para-el-real-murcia-2025-26/|title=Ekain, un atacante versátil y experimentado para el Real Murcia 2025/26|date=19 July 2025|access-date=19 September 2025|language=es}}</ref>

'''Herman Nils Johansson''' (born 16 October 1997) is a Swedish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] for [[MLS]] club [[FC Dallas]] and the [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden national team]].

==Club career==
Herman Johansson started his senior career in the main football club in his hometown of Örnsköldsvik, Friska Viljor FC, while also working as a pupil assistant in a local school.
In December 2020, after a spell with Sandvikens IF, Johansson was recruited by [[Mjällby AIF]], where he signed a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fotbollskanalen.se/allsvenskan/mjallby-varvar-mittfaltare-fran-ettan-hog-utvecklingspotential/|title=Mjällby värvar mittfältare från ettan: "Hög utvecklingspotential"|trans-title=Mjällby recruits midfielder from one: "High development potential"|language=sv|date=11 December 2020|author=Fredrik Andersson|website=fotbollskanalen.se|access-date=23 March 2022}}</ref>

In December 2025, Johansson was presented as a new player for [[FC Dallas]], signing a contract that extends through the 2028–29 season with an option for the 2029–30 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcdallas.com/news/fc-dallas-signs-swedish-international-herman-johansson-from-mjallby-aif|title=FC Dallas Signs Swedish International Herman Johansson from Mjällby AIF|date=30 December 2025|website=www.fcdallas.com|access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
In November 2025, Johansson received his first call up for [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] to a [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification|2026 World Cup qualification]] fixture against [[Slovenia men's national football team|Slovenia]], following an injury from [[Emil Holm (footballer)|Emil Holm]]. He made his debut against Slovenia on 18 November 2025, replacing [[Mattias Svanberg]] in the 65th minute of a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Herman Johansson kallas in|url=https://www.svenskfotboll.se/nyheter/landslag/2025/11/johansson-ersatter-holm/|access-date=16 November 2025 |website=www.svenskfotboll.se |language=sv}}</ref>

On 30 May 2026, Johansson was called up for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], replacing injured [[Emil Holm (footballer)|Emil Holm]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.svenskfotboll.se/nyheter/landslag/2026/05/johansson-ersatter-holm/ |title=Herman Johansson ersätter Emil Holm |trans-title=Herman Johansson replaces Emil Holm |publisher=[[Swedish Football Association]] |date=May 30, 2026 |access-date=May 30, 2026 |language=sv}}</ref>

== Career ==
Jacobs began streaming on [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]] in 2017, playing ''[[Roblox]]'' under the name GamerBoyKarl.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Alexander |date=March 7, 2022 |title='More organic': YouTuber Karl Jacobs on why creators should prioritize working with like-minded sponsors |url=https://digiday.com/marketing/sponsorships-have-to-be-more-organic-youtuber-karl-jacobs-on-why-creators-should-prioritize-working-with-like-minded-sponsors/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220412205903/https://digiday.com/marketing/sponsorships-have-to-be-more-organic-youtuber-karl-jacobs-on-why-creators-should-prioritize-working-with-like-minded-sponsors/ |archive-date=April 12, 2022 |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Digiday]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Basbas |first=Franchesca Judine |date=August 20, 2021 |title=10 streamers you need to watch: Valkyrae, Disguised Toast, TommyInnit, Kyedae, and more |url=https://www.bandwagon.asia/articles/10-streamers-you-need-to-watch-valkyrae-disguised-toast-tommyinnit-karl-jacobs-faker-kyedae-valorant-among-us-minecraft-twitch-youtube-facebook-list-2021 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220416011046/https://www.bandwagon.asia/articles/10-streamers-you-need-to-watch-valkyrae-disguised-toast-tommyinnit-karl-jacobs-faker-kyedae-valorant-among-us-minecraft-twitch-youtube-facebook-list-2021 |archive-date=April 16, 2022 |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=Bandwagon |location=Asia |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, he was hired as a [[video editor]] for YouTuber MrBro. Jacobs then became a cameraman for MrBro's brother, YouTuber [[MrBeast]],{{When|date=January 2023}} before transitioning into a member of MrBeast's on-screen cast.{{When|date=January 2023}}<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Asarch |first=Steven |date=March 29, 2022 |title=Karl Jacobs reveals how a Mr. Beast fluke made him a Minecraft icon |url=https://www.inverse.com/gaming/karl-jacobs-interview-minecraft-mr-beast |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220416011130/https://www.inverse.com/gaming/karl-jacobs-interview-minecraft-mr-beast |archive-date=April 16, 2022 |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Inverse (website)|Inverse]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Fay |first=Kacee |date=September 21, 2022 |title=Who is Karl Jacobs? Everything to know about the dynamic Minecraft, MrBeast star |url=https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/who-is-karl-jacobs-everything-to-know-about-the-dynamic-minecraft-mrbeast-star |access-date=September 22, 2022 |website=Dot Esports |language=en-US}}</ref> During a video for MrBeast Gaming, Jacobs met ''Minecraft'' YouTuber [[Dream (YouTuber)|Dream]], and was later invited to join his server, the [[Dream SMP]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Asarch |first=Steven |date=May 3, 2021 |title=One of YouTube's top Minecraft streamers apologized for past support of a creator known for his "toxic" history |url=https://www.insider.com/karl-jacobs-ice-poseidon-twitter-drama-minecraft-streamer-apologized-2021-5 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706002136/https://www.insider.com/karl-jacobs-ice-poseidon-twitter-drama-minecraft-streamer-apologized-2021-5 |archive-date=July 6, 2022 |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Insider Inc.|Insider]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

In December 2020, Jacobs created the online [[anthology series]] ''Tales from the SMP'', which explores the story of characters in the Dream SMP by following Jacobs's time-travelling character to various times and locations throughout the server.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fay |first=Kacee |date=February 11, 2022 |title=How to watch Tales From the SMP: The Maze |url=https://dotesports.com/news/how-to-watch-tales-from-the-smp-the-maze |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220416011046/https://dotesports.com/news/how-to-watch-tales-from-the-smp-the-maze |archive-date=April 16, 2022 |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Gamurs|Dot Esports]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The series has featured internet personalities such as Dream and [[Corpse Husband]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Destito |first=Deanna |date=August 2, 2022 |title=Karl Jacobs and Dark Horse team up for TIME TRAVELER TALES |url=https://www.comicsbeat.com/karl-jacobs-dark-horse-time-traveler-tales/ |access-date=August 18, 2022 |website=[[Comics Beat]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The season two pilot, titled "The Maze", premiered on February 11, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fay |first=Kacee |date=February 11, 2022 |title=All streamers participating in Tales From the SMP: The Maze |url=https://dotesports.com/news/all-streamers-participating-in-tales-from-the-smp-the-maze |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220416011047/https://dotesports.com/news/all-streamers-participating-in-tales-from-the-smp-the-maze |archive-date=April 16, 2022 |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Gamurs|Dot Esports]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In August 2022, Jacobs announced that stories from his series ''Tales from the SMP'' would be adapted as a series of comic books titled ''Time Traveler Tales'' for [[Dark Horse Comics]]. The series is written by Dave Scheidt and illustrated by Kelly and Nichole Matthews.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Michael |first=Cale |date=August 1, 2022 |title=Karl Jacobs partners with Dark Horse to publish new comic series |url=https://dotesports.com/streaming/news/karl-jacobs-partners-with-dark-horse-to-publish-new-comic-series |access-date=August 11, 2022 |website=[[Gamurs|Dot Esports]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hale |first=James |date=August 2, 2022 |title=Karl Jacobs is turning his Dream SMP adventures into a Dark Horse comic series |url=https://www.tubefilter.com/2022/08/02/karl-jacobs-time-traveler-tales-from-the-smp-dark-horse/ |access-date=August 11, 2022 |website=[[Tubefilter]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The series was released in five issues between December 2023 and April 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gritz |first=Ben |date=November 3, 2023 |title=Be Ready for Popular Streamer Karl Jacob's Time Traveler Tales! |url=https://prhcomics.com/2023/11/03/be-ready-for-popular-streamer-karl-jacobs-time-traveler-tales/ |access-date= November 9, 2024 |website=[[Penguin Random House|PRH Comics]]}}</ref> A collected trade paperback edition, published by Dark Horse Books, was released on August 13, 2024, compiling ''Time Traveler Tales'' #1–#5.<ref name="PRHCollected2024">{{Cite web |title=Time Traveler Tales |url=https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/745722/time-traveler-tales-by-created-by-karl-jacobs-written-by-dave-scheidt-illustrated-by-kelly-and-nichole-matthews-lettered-by-joamette-gil/ |website=Penguin Random House |publisher=Dark Horse Books |date=August 13, 2024 |access-date=December 27, 2025}}</ref>

{{Short description|American singer-songwriter}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2026}} {{Infobox musical artist | name = Fousheé | image = | caption = | birth_name = Britanny Fousheé | birth_date = | birth_place = [[Bridgewater, New Jersey]], U.S. | occupation = Singer-songwriter | genre = {{Hlist|[[Contemporary R&B|R&B]]{{Cite web |date=2020-12-17 |title=INTERVIEW: Fousheé on latest track 'single af' |url=http://www.womeninpop.com/news-home/interview-foushee-single-af |access-date=September 3, 2023 |website=Women In Pop |language=en-AU}}{{Cite web |last=Willis|first=Collin |date=2021-07-29|title=Fousheé Gets Applause For New "clap for him" Music Video|url=https://musicdaily.com/foushee-gets-applause-for-new-clap-for-him-music-video/|access-date=September 6, 2023|website=Music Daily|language=en-US}}|[[Soul music|soul]]{{Cite web|last=González|first=Jesús|date=2021-01-19|title=Fousheé: La artista que llevó el soul a TikTok gracias a una rola viral|trans-title= Fousheé: The artist who takes the soul music to TikTok thanks to a viral song|language=es-MX|url=https://www.sopitas.com/musica/foushee-artista-llevo-soul-tiktok-rola-viral-deep-end-the-voice/|access-date=2023-09-03|website=Sopitas.com}}}} | instrument = {{Hlist|Vocals|guitar}} | years_active = 2019–present | label = {{Hlist|[[RCA Records|RCA]]|Trackmasters}} | website = {{URL|fousheeofficial.com}}}} '''Britanny Fousheé''' (born 1998) is an American singer-songwriter. She came to wide notice when the vocals for her song "Deep End" were used on a hit song by rapper [[Sleepy Hallow]] in 2020. She released her [[RCA Records]] second [[extended play]] ''[[Time Machine (EP)|Time Machine]]'' on June 4, 2021, and has collaborated with multiple artists including [[Vince Staples]],{{Citation |title=Vince Staples & Fousheé – TAKE ME HOME |url=https://genius.com/Vince-staples-and-foushee-take-me-home-lyrics |access-date=2022-11-20}} [[Lil Wayne]], [[James Blake (musician)|James Blake]], [[Steve Lacy]], [[Lil Yachty]] and [[Lil Uzi Vert]].{{Cite magazine |date=February 17, 2022 |title=Fousheé Made One of 2022's Biggest Hits. Next, She Wants to Transcend Time |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/foushee-bad-habit-steve-lacy-interview-1234679066/ |access-date=September 3, 2023 |magazine=Rolling Stone}} She released her debut album, ''[[Softcore (album)|Softcore]]'', on November 17, 2022.{{Cite web |date=2022-11-18 |title=8 Albums Out This Week You Should Listen to Now |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/8-new-albums-you-should-listen-to-now-weyes-blood-roddy-ricch-foushee/ |access-date=2022-11-20 |website=Pitchfork |language=en-US}} ==Background and early life== Fousheé was born and raised in [[New Jersey]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-radar/foushee-deep-end-single-af-interview-2020-2818884 |title= Fousheé: "Black women have been the workhorses of the music industry since time began" |website=NME |last=O'Reilly |first=Caitlin |date=18 November 2020 |accessdate=3 September 2021}} Her Jamaican mother was a drummer for PEP, an all-woman 1980s Jamaican reggae band. Fousheé wrote her first song when she was five.{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/foushee-hip-hop-r-b-rookie-of-the-month-march-2021/ |title= Billboard's Hip-Hop and R&B Rookie of the Month for March: Fousheé |magazine=Billboard |last=Mitchell |first=Gail |date=11 March 2021 |accessdate=2 September 2021}} In her younger years she studied voice, media, classical music, background arranging, guitar, and piano{{Cite web |url=https://divinemagazine.biz/alt-soul-singer-foushee-releases-stirring-debut-ep-speak-up/ |title= Alt-Soul Singer Fousheé Releases Stirring Debut EP 'Speak Up' |website=Divine Magazine |date=4 June 2018 |accessdate=6 September 2021}} and performed with groups she had formed with her childhood friends. She attended [[Bridgewater-Raritan High School]]Olivier, Bobby. [https://www.nj.com/entertainment/2021/03/nj-singer-went-viral-but-didnt-know-it-then-she-had-to-prove-the-voice-was-hers.html "N.J. singer went viral but didn’t know it. Then she had to prove the voice was hers."], NJ Advance Media for [[NJ.com]], March 18, 2021, July 18, 2022.Accessed October 17, 2022. "The artist born Britanny Fousheé, who grew up in Somerset and Middlesex counties and graduated from Bridgewater-Raritan High School, explains that her few viral 'Deep End' lines weren’t even part of a full song when she wrote them." and continued her musical activities into college.{{Cite web |url=https://www.okayplayer.com/music/foushee-time-machine-interview.html |title= Fousheé's Plan to Break Thru the Alt World Begins With 'Time Machine' |website=okayplayer |last=Mowatt |first=Robyn |accessdate=3 September 2021}} == Career == Fousheé released her debut EP ''Speak Up'' in May 2018. In fall 2018 she competed on [[The Voice (American season 15)|season 15 of The Voice]] making it up to the battle rounds with [[Adam Levine]] as her coach.{{cite web | title=FOUSHEÉ: The Voice contestant | website=NBC | date=2023-05-23 | url=https://www.nbc.com/the-voice/credits/contestant/season-15/foushee | access-date=2023-08-09}}{{cite web | title='The Voice' recap: The battles sound more like duets | website=EW.com | date=2018-10-23 | url=https://ew.com/recap/the-voice-season-15-episode-9/ | access-date=2023-08-09}} In 2019 she moved to Los Angeles. === 2020: "Deep End" === Fousheé was invited to contribute vocal samples to Splice, a royalty-free music database. American rapper [[Sleepy Hallow]] found her "Deep End" track and used it in his 2020 single "[[Deep End Freestyle]]". His track ended up going viral on TikTok and had an associated dance challenge which drove up its popularity; Fousheé hadn't known about the trend and wasn't credited on the song for some time.{{Cite web |url=https://gal-dem.com/foushee-deep-end-interview-tiktok-2021/ |title=Meet Fousheé, the 'Deep End' singer who wants to keep you guessing |website=gal-dem |last=Simpson |first=Annique |date=13 May 2021 |accessdate=2 September 2021 |archive-date=18 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210918112226/https://gal-dem.com/foushee-deep-end-interview-tiktok-2021/ |url-status=dead }}{{Cite web |url=https://vmagazine.com/article/meet-alt-rbs-most-promising-voice-foushee/ |title= MEET ALT-R&B'S MOST PROMISING VOICE: FOUSHEÉ |website=V Magazine |last=Bujnosek |first=Bailey |date=11 December 2021 |accessdate=2 September 2021}}{{Cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/foushee-time-machine/ |title= time machine |website=Pitchfork |last=Torres |first=Eric |date=11 June 2021 |accessdate=2 September 2021}} The Sleepy Hallow track, "Deep End Freestyle", was certified platinum by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]] in August 2020.{{Cite web|title=SLEEPY HALLOW – DEEP END FREESTYLE (FEAT. FOUSHEÉ)|url=http://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?share=21656&t=t|access-date=August 15, 2020|website=RIAA}} In the same year, Fousheé released her own version of the song, simply titled "Deep End". The song reached the No. 10 spot on Billboard's March 27 Alternative Airplay chart. With that feat, she became the first Black woman to hit the Top 10 for that chart since [[Tracy Chapman]] with her song "[[Crossroads (Tracy Chapman song)|Crossroads]]" in 1989.{{Cite web |url=https://uproxx.com/music/foushee-deep-end-alternative-chart-black-women-history/ |title= Fousheé's Breakout Hit 'Deep End' Just Made History For Black Women On The Alternative Charts |website=Uproxx |last=Rossignol |first=Derrick |date=25 March 2021 |accessdate=2 September 2022}} === 2020–present: Solo career and collaborations === Fousheé signed to [[RCA Records]] in June 2020. She also had the video for her track "By One" premiered by ''Essence'' in October of the same year.{{Cite web |url=https://www.essence.com/entertainment/premiere-foushee-new-video-by-one/ |title= Premiere: Rising Alt-Soul Star Fousheé Shares New Video For "By One" |website=Essence |last=Scott |first=Sydney |date=24 October 2020 |accessdate=6 September 2022}} She was named ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'''s R&B/hip-hop rookie for the month of March 2021. Her RCA debut EP, ''[[Time Machine (EP)|Time Machine]]'', was released on June 4, 2021, under Trackmasters Entertainment. She was also named [[Apple Music|Apple]]'s "Up Next Artist" for that same month and was the cover feature of ''Wonderland'' ''Magazine'''s Summer 2021 issue.{{Cite web |url=https://respect-mag.com/2021/06/foushee-releases-new-project-time-machine/ |title=Foushee Releases New Project 'Time Machine' |website=Respect |last=Rashed |first=Ayana |date=6 June 2021 |accessdate=2 September 2022 |archive-date=20 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221020010719/https://respect-mag.com/2021/06/foushee-releases-new-project-time-machine/ |url-status=dead }}{{Cite web |url=https://www.wonderlandmagazine.com/2021/06/08/foushee-time-machine-summer-21-issue/ |title= FOUSHEÉ: The singer talks her debut project "Time Machine" and defying expectations in our Summer 21 issue. |website=Wonderland |last=Baker |first=Scarlett |date=8 June 2021 |accessdate=5 September 2022}} In 2021, Fousheé collaborated with French rappers [[Laylow]] and [[Nekfeu]] on the song "Spécial" on Laylow's album "L'étrange histoire de Mr. Anderson".{{Citation|title=Laylow — SPECIAL (feat. Nekfeu & Fousheé)|url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/l%C3%A9trange-histoire-de-mr-anderson/1575206577|access-date=September 16, 2021|language=en-US|website=Apple Music}} It was around the same time that she started collaborating with mainstream artists including [[Lil Wayne]] and [[Vince Staples]].{{Cite web |url=https://americansongwriter.com/genre-bending-singer-foushee-releases-track-and-visual-for-gold-fronts-feat-lil-wayne/ |title= Genre-Bending Singer Fousheé Releases Track and Visual for "gold fronts" Feat. Lil Wayne |website=American Songwriter |last=Williams |first=Gracie |date= 30 March 2021 |accessdate=6 September 2022}} In August, she performed the song "Take Me Home" on [[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon]] with the latter.{{Cite web |url=https://www.complex.com/music/vince-staples-performs-take-me-home-foushee |title= Vince Staples Performs Soothing Rendition of "Take Me Home" f/ Fousheé |website=Complex |last=Rose |first=Jordan |date=19 August 2021 |accessdate=5 September 2022}} In the fall, she toured with [[James Blake (musician)|James Blake]] at venues including the [[Chicago Theatre]] and [[Radio City Music Hall]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.timeout.com/chicago/music/james-blake-foushee |title= James Blake + Fousheé |website=Timeout |date=29 September 2021 |accessdate=2 September 2022}}{{Cite web |url=https://donyc.com/events/2021/10/9/james-blake-friends-that-break-your-heart-tour-tickets |title= James Blake, Fousheé |website=DoNYC |date=9 October 2021 |accessdate=5 September 2022}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.vogue.co.uk/arts-and-lifestyle/article/foushee-personality-test |title= Angel Numbers & Frank Ocean: Inside The Mind Of Fousheé |website=Vogue (UK) |last=Mukhtar |first=Amel |date=3 September 2021 |accessdate=2 September 2022}} The track "Clap for Him" from ''Time Machine'' also featured [[Lil Yachty]]; he appeared in the track's music video as well.{{Cite web |url=https://uproxx.com/music/foushee-lil-yachty-clap-for-him-video/ |title= Fousheé And Lil Yachty's 'Clap For Him' Video Counts Someone Else's Blessings |website=Uproxx |last=Williams |first=Aaron |date=16 July 2021 |accessdate=3 September 2022}}{{Cite web |title=Fousheé releases new music video for "Clap For Him" featuring Lil Yachty |url=https://www.rcarecords.com/news/foushee-releases-new-music-video-for-clap-for-him-ft-lil-yachty/ |access-date=September 2, 2023 |website=[[RCA Records]] (News) |language=en-US}} In 2022, she collaborated with [[Steve Lacy]] and not only co-wrote but contributed background vocals for the songs "Sunshine" and "[[Bad Habit (Steve Lacy song)|Bad Habit]]," both of which were lead singles for his second studio album ''[[Gemini Rights]]''.{{Cite web |url=https://www.thefader.com/2022/07/13/steve-lacy-foushee-sunshine-gemini-rights |title= Steve Lacy shares Fousheé collaboration "Sunshine" |website=The Fader |last=Renshaw |first=David |date=13 July 2022 |accessdate=5 September 2022}} "Bad Habit" made it to the number one spot on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming both of the artists' first number one entry on the chart. She also appeared on [[Ravyn Lenae]]'s debut album ''[[Hypnos (album)|Hypnos]]'' the same year.{{Cite web |url=https://www.complex.com/music/ravyn-lenae-debut-album-hypnos-stream |title= Listen to Ravyn Lenae's Debut Album 'Hypnos' f/ Smino, Steve Lacy, and More |website=Complex |last=Price |first=Joe |date=20 May 2022 |accessdate=5 September 2022}} In the leadup to her debut album, she appeared in a feature article by ''Flaunt'' in which she was pictured in [[Prada]], [[LOEWE (fashion brand)|Loewe]], [[Louis Vuitton]], and [[Dolce & Gabbana]].{{Cite web |url=https://flaunt.com/content/foushee-first-time-offenders |title= FOUSHEÉ: THESE WALLS WERE MEANT FOR BREAKING THROUGH |website=Flaunt |last=Castillo |first=Bree |date=2 September 2022 |accessdate=10 October 2022}} Her debut album ''[[Softcore (album)|Softcore]]'' was released on November 17, 2022. '''Jani Cristina Dai Zhao''' (born October 19, 1992) is a Portuguese actress of Chinese descent. She is best known for playing Stingray in ''[[Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom]]''<ref name="RM">{{cite web|title=A menina dos macaenses|url=http://www.revistamacau.com/2011/12/04/a-menina-dos-macaenses/|website=Revista MACAU|date=2011-04-12}}[''en: The girl from Macao'']</ref>

== Biography ==
Born in Portugal, she is the daughter of an American father of Chinese descent and a [[Macau|Macanese]] Chinese mother. She moved shortly afterwards to [[China]], then to the United States and then back to Portugal when she was six years old. She began her modeling career at a young age in Portugal, turning to acting. She began her acting career in the children's soap opera ''[[Floribella]]'' in the role of the hippie Ashie in 2006. In 2008 she was part of the cast of Rebelde Way where she played the student Hoshi. Between 2009 and 2010 she participated in ''Sentimentos''. Between 2010 and 2011 she was in ''[[Morangos com Açúcar]]'' where she played the role of Sandra and worked on the [[SIC K]] program, ''Pronto a Vestir''. She resides in [[Lisbon]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jani Zhao regressa à SIC (com vídeo)|url=http://www.atelevisao.com/sic/jani-zhao-regressa-a-sic-com-video/|website=A Televisão|date=2012-05-20}} ''[en: Jani Zhao returns to SIC (with video)]''</ref>

In 2015, Jani Zhao participated in the Angolan telenovela ''Jikulumessu'' on Angolan Public Television ([[TPA 2]]), written by Coréon Dú.

In 2018, she participated in the TVI telenovela ''[[Jogo Duplo]]'' as one of the antagonists. She played the character Susana Wang, an assassin for a Macanese triad working under the orders of a Portuguese-Chinese criminal, Manuel Qiang. This role brought her recognition because, along with her colleague Anna Eremin, she performed homosexual romantic scenes, thus drawing attention to this theme and its importance.<ref name=":19">{{cite web|title=Aquaman e o Reino Perdido|website=SAPO Mag|url=https://mag.sapo.pt/filmes/aquaman-and-the-lost-kingdom|accessdate=2023-05-29|language=pt}}</ref>

In 2023, she played the fearless Stingray in the film ''[[Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom]]''.<ref name="CastSep2021">{{Cite magazine |last=Kit |first=Borys |date=September 24, 2021 |title=''Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom'' Casts Indya Moore, Jani Zhao and Vincent Regan (Exclusive) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/aquaman-and-the-lost-kingdom-cast-1235020425/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924230528/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/aquaman-and-the-lost-kingdom-cast-1235020425/ |archive-date=September 24, 2021 |access-date=September 24, 2021 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> In 2026, she starred as [[FP-25]] member and theatre actress Rosa in the political thriller ''[[Projecto Global]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/488609/|website=[[Cineuropa]]|first=Olivia|last=Popp|date=4 February 2026|title=Review: Projecto Global|access-date=6 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Julien Nguyen''' is a Vietnamese American artist.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hess |first=Liam |date=2020-09-28 |title=The Renaissance-Inspired Painter Behind This Season’s Buzziest Print |url=https://www.vogue.com/article/julien-nguyen-ottolinger-artist-collaboration |access-date=2024-11-12 |website=Vogue |language=en-US}}</ref> He is known for Renaissance-inspired, meticulously rendered figurative works that fuse art-historical motifs with science fiction, gaming and contemporary portraiture. He lives and works in Los Angeles and participated in the 2017 Whitney Biennial. His work is held by institutions including the Whitney Museum of American Art.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julien Nguyen {{!}} Matthew Marks Gallery |url=https://matthewmarks.com/artists/julien-nguyen |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=Julien Nguyen {{!}} Matthew Marks Gallery}}</ref>

== Biography ==
=== Early life and education ===

Julien Nguyen was born in 1990 in [[Fairfax, Virginia]] to Vietnamese parents who had emigrated to America after the [[fall of Saigon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spielberger |first=Daniel |date=2021-11-25 |title=Artist Julien Nguyen Is Painting Immersive, Cryptic Dreamscapes |url=https://vietcetera.com/onboardy/artist-julien-nguyen-is-painting-immersive-cryptic-dreamscapes |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=Vietcetera |language=vi}}</ref> As a teenager, Nguyen was more interested in video games than traditional art, citing formative influences such as [[Civilization III|''Civilization III'']], [[Age of Empires|''Age of Empires'']] and [[StarCraft (video game)|''StarCraft'']].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julien Nguyen 20th Century & Contemporary Art Evening Sale in association with Yongle |url=http://phillips.com/detail/julien-nguyen/HK010322/6 |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=phillips.com |language=en}}</ref> This early immersion in strategy and speculative worlds later fed into his pictorial vocabulary of art history meeting digital iconography. Nguyen went on to pursue formal art training. He earned a [[Bachelor of Fine Arts]] (BFA) from the [[Rhode Island School of Design]] (RISD) in 2012. Afterward, he continued his studies at [[Städelschule]] in [[Frankfurt|Frankfurt]] in Germany, where he completed the postgraduate Meisterschule (Master School) in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julien Nguyen |url=https://www.sothebys.com/en/artists/julien-nguyen |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=Sothebys.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Work ==
Nguyen is primarily a painter, working in oil and tempera on panel. His work is noted for its highly precise, virtuosic technique, which deliberately recalls the finish and compositional mastery of 15th-century painters like Fra Angelico and Caravaggio.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julien Nguyen {{!}} February 08, 2019 {{!}} Contemporary Arts Center |url=https://www.contemporaryartscenter.org/visit/exhibitions/2019/02/julien-nguyen |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=www.contemporaryartscenter.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

Nguyen's paintings combine references to Renaissance and early Christian art with elements drawn from contemporary culture, science fiction, and digital media. His compositions frequently adapt motifs from artists such as [[Piero della Francesca]], Giotto, and Leonardo da Vinci, reinterpreting them through a modern lens informed by anime, video games and speculative fiction.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zack Hatfield on Julien Nguyen |url=https://www.artforum.com/features/zack-hatfield-on-julien-nguyen-242333 |website=Artforum |date=2021 |access-date=16 October 2025}}</ref>
Nguyen's technical approach is rooted in traditional materials—oil and tempera on panel, occasionally on copper—while his subject matter often involves friends and collaborators presented in allegorical or devotional settings. Critics have observed that his paintings merge "the sacred and the secular", reflecting both the precision of Renaissance painting and the introspection of portrait photography.<ref>{{cite web |title=Julien Nguyen: Pictures of the Floating World |url=https://brooklynrail.org/2021/07/artseen/Julien-Nguyen-Pictures-of-the-Floating-World |website=The Brooklyn Rail |date=July 2021 |access-date=16 October 2025}}</ref>
Recurring themes in Nguyen's work include spiritual devotion, intimacy and technology. His figures are often rendered with elongated proportions and subdued color, suggesting detachment or transcendence.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Gospel According to Julien Nguyen |url=https://www.frieze.com/article/gospel-according-julien-nguyen |website=Frieze |date=2018 |access-date=16 October 2025}}</ref> The artist has described his imagery as influenced by strategy games such as ''Civilization III'' and ''StarCraft'', noting their structural and historical world-building as parallel to the construction of pictorial space.<ref>{{cite web |title=Julien Nguyen |url=https://www.phillips.com/detail/julien-nguyen/HK010322/6 |website=Phillips |access-date=16 October 2025}}</ref>
Nguyen's practice has been characterized by critics as balancing restraint and intensity. [[Artforum]] described his paintings as "meticulously composed devotional images that collapse medieval reverence into the anxieties of the present", while Frieze called them "unsettling hybrids of human and technological beauty".<ref>{{cite web |title=Zack Hatfield on Julien Nguyen |url=https://www.artforum.com/features/zack-hatfield-on-julien-nguyen-242333 |website=Artforum |date=2021 |access-date=16 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Gospel According to Julien Nguyen |url=https://www.frieze.com/article/gospel-according-julien-nguyen |website=Frieze |date=2018 |access-date=16 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Moffitt |first=Evan |date=2021-09-21 |title=The Hedonistic Fever Dream of Julien Nguyen’s Twinks |url=https://www.frieze.com/article/hedonistic-fever-dream-julien-nguyens-twinks |access-date=2025-10-17 |work=Frieze |language=en |issue=222 |issn=0962-0672}}</ref>

== Major exhibitions ==
His work was included in the 2017 [[Whitney Biennial]] at the [[Whitney Museum|Whitney Museum of American Art]] in New York.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Juxtapoz Magazine - Julien Nguyen @ Matthew Marks, NYC |url=https://www.juxtapoz.com/news/painting/julien-nguyen-matthew-marks-nyc/?utm_source=mutualart&utm_medium=referral |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=www.juxtapoz.com |language=en-gb}}</ref>
He has had one-person exhibitions at institutions and galleries, including:
* [[Matthew Marks Gallery]], New York and Los Angeles <ref>{{Cite web |title=Julien Nguyen {{!}} Biography |url=https://www.mutualart.com/Artist/Julien-Nguyen/D9DC23684D33DFF2/Biography |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=www.mutualart.com |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Swiss Institute Contemporary Art New York|Swiss Institute]], New York<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julien Nguyen: Works for Sale, Upcoming Auctions & Past Results |url=https://www.phillips.com/artist/24110/julien-nguyen |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=Phillips |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Kunstverein München]], Munich<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julien Nguyen: Works for Sale, Upcoming Auctions & Past Results |url=https://www.phillips.com/artist/24110/julien-nguyen |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=Phillips |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Contemporary Arts Center|Contemporary Arts Center (CAC)]], Cincinnati
* Modern Art London, London

{{small|Suspended since November 27, 2023{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君逮捕の宮崎市議会、改正議員報酬条例を可決 |url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20231127-7YQQIE4TANNI5LXFBEEPT6NNBQ/ |website=[[Sankei Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=27 November 2023}}}} | office2 = Toda City Councilor | term_start2 = February 6, 2021 | term_end2 = March 4, 2022{{efn|name=Void|He is technically [[void ab initio|not elected by law]]}} | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1986|8|14}} | birth_place = [[Miyazaki, Miyazaki]], Japan | party = Super Crazy-kun Party | children = 1 | nickname = Super Crazy-kun | module = {{Infobox criminal | child = yes | criminal_charges = non-consensual sexual intercourse resulting in injury | convictions = May 21, 2024 | penalty = 4 years and 6 months | imprisoned = {{ill|Saga Juvenile Prison|ja|佐賀少年刑務所}} }} | footnotes = }} {{Nihongo|'''Makoto Nishimoto'''|西本 誠|Nishimoto Makoto|born August 14, 1986|lead=yes}}, also known as {{Nihongo|"'''Super Crazy-kun'''"|スーパークレイジー君|Sūpā Kureijī-kun}} is a former Japanese politician.
