He was then elected as city councilor of [[Miyazaki City]] in 2023. He resigned after being arrested for sexually assaulting a female acquaintance in September 2023. He was charged with sexual assault in May 2024. ==Early life== Nishimoto was born on August 14, 1986, in [[Miyazaki, Miyazaki|Miyazaki city, Miyazaki Prefecture]].{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君、出身地・宮崎県知事選出馬へ「若い人が立候補していない。投票率上がれば」 - 社会 : 日刊スポーツ |url=https://www.nikkansports.com/general/nikkan/news/202210310001344.html |website=[[Nikkan Sports]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja|date=November 1, 2022}} His father is part of a {{Transliteration|ja|[[yakuza]]}} gang and his mother left him when he was one year old. Nishimoto grew up with his grandmother. He joined a {{Transliteration|ja|[[bōsōzoku]]}} gang and was sent to [[juvenile detention centers]] three times during his third year of middle school. In an interview with the ''[[Tokyo Shimbun]]'', he stated that during his third detention, he was unable to see his grandmother before she died, which caused his change of heart.{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君 独占取材 「3カ月の居住実態なく当選無効」決めた市選管とは「徹底的に闘う」：東京新聞デジタル |url=https://www.tokyo-np.co.jp/article/98289 |website=[[The Tokyo Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=April 15, 2021}} ==Political career== ===Tokyo gubernatorial election=== Nishimoto moved to [[Tokyo]] at the age of twenty-one and worked as a club employee and caregiver in [[Ginza]]. He also worked as a singer and performed in live concerts. He ran for the [[2020 Tokyo gubernatorial election]] because he wanted to "raise his profile". He ran under his nickname, "Super Crazy-kun", but it was rejected. Nishimoto was then allowed to run under his real name. He lost the election, garnering only 11,887 votes.{{cite web |title=「スーパークレイジー君」議員に当選証書 スーツで出席：朝日新聞 |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP22340NP21UTNB00J.html |website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=2 February 2021}}{{cite web |title=金髪に特攻服「スーパークレイジー君」 異色の市議誕生 埼玉・戸田（1/2ページ） |url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20210201-ZNI6RH7NQVLKNNLLW3BEUB3HCI/ |website=[[Sankei Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=2 February 2021}} ===Toda City councillor (2021–2022)=== In 2021, Nishimoto attempted to run for city councillor for [[Toda, Saitama|Toda City, Saitama Prefecture]], where he ran again using his nickname "Super Crazy-kun" and was approved by the city election commission. He campaigned while wearing a {{Transliteration|ja|[[kamikaze]]}} uniform. He won by garnering 912 votes and placing 26th out of the 36 seats within the city council. He was addressed as "{{Nihongo|Super Crazy Councillor|スーパークレイジー君議員|Sūpākureijī-kun giin}}" during the preliminary session.{{cite web |title=「破天荒議員に」スーパークレイジー君氏、中身勝負 - 社会 : 日刊スポーツ |url=https://www.nikkansports.com/general/nikkan/news/202102080000969.html |website=[[Nikkan Sports]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=February 8, 2021}} The Toda City Election Commission later received various complaints from citizens claiming that he did not live in the city for more than three months as required by the Japanese Public Offices Election Law. Nishimoto denied the claims, stating in various interviews that he moved to an apartment in the city in late September 2020, changing his residency from Tokyo's [[Chuo-ku, Tokyo|Chūō ward]] to Toda City on October 5, 2020 in order to run for the election.{{cite web |title=「スーパークレイジー君」当選無効に不服申し立て 埼玉・戸田 |url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20210413-C4JIRBWOBNKDDLXDE3JVICCWZ4/ |website=[[Sankei Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=13 April 2021}}{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君市議の「当選無効求める」...市選管が異議申し出を受理 |url=https://www.yomiuri.co.jp/election/local/20210217-OYT1T50074/ |website=[[Yomiuri Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=17 February 2021}} On April 9, the city election commission revoked his election, stating that the apartment where he resided since September 2020 was still in someone else's name, failing to prove that he actually lives in Toda City.{{cite press release |url=https://www.city.toda.saitama.jp/uploaded/attachment/45316.pdf |website=Toda City Election Commission|title=【⼾⽥市議会議員⼀般選挙】当選の効⼒に関する異議の申出に対する決定について |access-date=25 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210409092547/https://www.city.toda.saitama.jp/uploaded/attachment/45316.pdf|archive-date=April 9, 2021|url-status=dead}}{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君議員への不適切言動で市職員停職：朝日新聞 |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP3V6VVDP3VUTNB01K.html?iref=ogimage_rek |website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]] |language=ja |date=26 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230429143657/https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASP3V6VVDP3VUTNB01K.html?iref=ogimage_rek|archive-date=April 29, 2023|url-status=dead}} Nishimoto responded in an interview with ''[[Sankei Shimbun]]'' that he lived in the house in Tokyo where his wife and child live, but "he slept in Toda City". He filed a lawsuit against the Toda City Election Commission on April 13 at the Saitama Prefectural Election Commission,{{cite web |title=「スーパークレイジー君」の当選無効 埼玉・戸田市選管 |url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20210409-ZXFJRF62UJMLTFRTJRS5QQSHEE/ |website=[[Sankei Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=9 April 2021}} but it was later dismissed in July. He then appealed to the [[Tokyo High Court]] to have the ruling overturned in the same month, but the lawsuit also was dismissed.{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君の当選無効認める 高裁「住んでいた事実ない」：朝日新聞 |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASPBH73N6PBHUTIL04Z.html |website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=15 October 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Fukatsu |first1=Hibiki |last2=Nakamura |first2=Tomotaka |title=クレイジー市議当選は「無効」 埼玉県選管 |url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20210712-CLH4QUIP5BOYZIKDKOFVGGYEIE/ |website=[[Sankei Shimbun]] |language=ja |date=12 July 2021}}{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君、埼玉県選管も当選無効判断 戸田市議選 |url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/20210712/k00/00m/010/038000c |website=[[Mainichi Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=July 12, 2021}} Nishimoto then announced that he would file an appeal in the [[Supreme Court of Japan]] on October 15, but the appeal was rejected on March 4, 2022.{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君議員の請求棄却「覚悟あったが悔しい」最高裁に上告へ - 社会 : 日刊スポーツ |url=https://www.nikkansports.com/general/nikkan/news/202110150000724.html |website=[[Nikkan Sports]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |date=15 October 2021}}{{cite web |title=当選無効の市議スーパークレイジー君「タダ働きでいいからやらせてほしかった」 |url=https://news.tbs.co.jp/newseye/tbs_newseye6005903.html |website=[[Japan News Network]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307154429/https://news.tbs.co.jp/newseye/tbs_newseye6005903.html |archive-date=March 7, 2022 |date=March 4, 2022 |url-status=dead}} On March 9, the Toda City Election Commission officially revoked his win.{{cite web |title=「クレイジー君」市議当選無効、公明新人の繰り上げ決定 |url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220309-LVKAEBBITZOQPHHMCWC62YWA3Y/ |website=[[Sankei Shimbun]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=9 March 2022}} ===Mayoral election and Miyazaki gubernatorial election=== Nishimoto decided to run for mayor of Toda City after learning the incumbent mayor Fumihito Sugawara was running uncontested. He lost the election by a wide margin, garnering only 2,529 votes against his opponent's 37,092 votes.{{cite web |title=戸田市長選落選のスーパークレイジー君氏「フルボッコにされた」夏の参院選出馬も再検討意向 - 社会 : 日刊スポーツ |url=https://www.nikkansports.com/general/nikkan/news/202203200001233.html |website=[[Nikkan Sports]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=March 20, 2022}}{{cite web |title=戸田市長選にスーパークレイジー君が立候補 菅原文仁氏は再選めざす：朝日新聞デジタル |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASQ3F3TN8Q3CUTNB006.html |website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]] |date=March 13, 2022}} In April 2022 he enrolled at [[Nihon University]] in the Faculty of Law, Department of Politics and Economics. He stated that he decided not to run for the [[Japanese House of Councillors]].{{cite web |title=スーパークレイジー君が参院選不出馬を表明 4月から日大法学部で「政治」を学ぶ |url=https://www.tokyo-sports.co.jp/articles/-/184755 |website=[[Tokyo Sports]] |access-date=25 April 2025 |language=ja |date=1 June 2022}} In November 2022, Nishimoto announced that he would run for governor of [[Miyazaki Prefecture]]. office over vaccine scandal|website=[[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]]|date=17 April 2021|access-date=11 October 2025|archive-date=16 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250816103208/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/17/perus-vizcarra-banned-from-public-office-over-vaccine-scandal|url-status=live}} Jerí held office as a member of the centrist [[We Are Peru]] party. On 26 July 2025, he was elected as [[President of the Congress of the Republic of Peru|President of the Congress of the Republic]] for the 2025–2026 annual session period with the votes of [[Free Peru]], [[Popular Force]], [[Alliance for Progress (Peru)|Alliance for Progress]], [[Popular Action (Peru)|Acción Popular]], [[Go on Country – Social Integration Party (2017)|Avanza País]], and [[We Are Peru]].{{cite web |last=Loo |first=Wendy Milla |date=26 July 2025 |title=José Jerí, new president of Congress [PROFILE] |url=https://rpp.pe/politica/congreso/jose-jeri-nuevo-presidente-del-congreso-perfil-noticia-1648008 |access-date=26 July 2025 |website=rpp.pe |language=es |archive-date=11 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011132217/https://rpp.pe/politica/congreso/jose-jeri-nuevo-presidente-del-congreso-perfil-noticia-1648008 |url-status=live }} After the unanimous [[Impeachment of Dina Boluarte|impeachment and removal]] of Boluarte on 10 October 2025 amidst the [[2025 Peruvian protests]], Jerí assumed the presidency in his capacity as head of the legislative branch.{{cite news |last1=Aquino |first1=Marco |last2=Morland |first2=Sarah |date=10 October 2025 |title=Peru Congress ousts president, successor vows 'war on crime' |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-lawmakers-make-fresh-push-remove-unpopular-president-office-2025-10-09/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=10 October 2025}} In his inaugural speech, Jerí pledged to "install and lead a government of transition, empathy, and national reconciliation", and said that the nation "must declare war on crime".{{cite web |last=Ortiz |first=Andy |date=10 October 2025 |url=https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2025/10/10/latinoamerica/quien-es-jose-jeri-inesperado-nuevo-presidente-peru-orix |title=¿Quién es José Jerí, el inesperado nuevo presidente de Perú? |trans-title=Who is José Jerí, the unexpected new president of Peru? |work=[[CNN en Español]] |access-date=10 October 2025 |language=es |archive-date=10 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010163724/https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2025/10/10/latinoamerica/quien-es-jose-jeri-inesperado-nuevo-presidente-peru-orix |url-status=live }} The Peruvian Congress approved the censuring of Jerí from the position of president of Peru under a vote of no confidence on 12 February 2026. Unlike impeachment, which requires a supermajority of 26 in the 120-member legislature, censuring strips him of his title as head of Congress with a simple majority. His interim status was then used to remove him from the presidency.{{cite web |date=18 February 2026|title=Peru Congress ousts president because of China-linked secret meetings|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/world/south-america/peru-congress-ousts-president-china-linked-secret-meetings-rcna259489|access-date=18 February 2026|website=NBC News|quote=While the current head of Congress, Fernando Rospigliosi, would be constitutionally next in the line of succession, he has declined to assume the presidency. As such, legislators will have to elect a new head of Congress who will then automatically assume the presidency.}} Jerí became the sixth president removed by Congress after [[Guillermo Billinghurst]] (1914), [[Alberto Fujimori]] (2001), [[Martín Vizcarra]] (2020), [[Pedro Castillo]] (2022), and Boluarte (2025). He was the fourth president to be removed in the 2020s.{{cite web |date=17 February 2026 |title=Peru Ousts President, Again |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/17/world/americas/peru-president-jose-jeri-impeachment.html |access-date=17 February 2026 |publisher=[[The New York Times]]}}{{cite web |date=17 February 2026 |title=Peru's congress votes to oust President Jeri |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/china/perus-congress-votes-oust-president-jeri-2026-02-17/ |access-date=17 February 2026 |publisher=Reuters}} == Early life and education == José Jerí was born on 13 November 1986, in the [[Jesús María District, Lima|Jesús María District]], located in the city of [[Lima]]. He graduated from the [[Federico Villarreal National University]] (UNFV), where he earned his bachelor's degree in law in 2014. The following year, he earned his law degree from the [[Inca Garcilaso de la Vega University]]. He held various positions in the [[Department of Ancash|Ancash Regional Government]] from 2020 to 2021, also serving as Secretary General. He was an advisor to the [[We Are Peru]] caucus in the [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Congress of the Republic]] in 2020.{{cite web |date=20 December 2020 |title=View of the Candidate's Resume |url=https://plataformahistorico.jne.gob.pe/ListaDeCandidatos/ResumenHDV |access-date=25 July 2024 |website=JNE – Electoral Platform }}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} == Political career == Since 2013, he has been affiliated with the political party [[We Are Peru]]. As a member, he served as youth secretary and alternate legal representative. He is currently the party's first vice president since September 2021.{{cite web |title=José Jerí Oré – Party History |url=https://infogob.jne.gob.pe/Politico/FichaPolitico/jose-enrique-jeri-ore_historial-partidario_ug@eTICaAcoc6+@0ElOxMA==@I |access-date=25 July 2024 |website=Infogob |archive-date=11 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231211041341/https://infogob.jne.gob.pe/Politico/FichaPolitico/jose-enrique-jeri-ore_historial-partidario_ug@eTICaAcoc6+@0ElOxMA==@I |url-status=live }} His first political participation took place in the 2013 Lima municipal elections as a candidate for the [[Lima|Lima Municipality]] council with the backing of {{ill|Fernando Andrade (Peruvian politician)|lt=Fernando Andrade|es|Fernando Andrade}}, though Jerí was not elected. He ran again unsuccessfully in the 2014 elections.{{cite web |title=José Jerí Oré – Electoral Processes |url=https://infogob.jne.gob.pe/Politico/FichaPolitico/jose-enrique-jeri-ore_procesos-electorales_ug@eTICaAcoc6+@0ElOxMA==@I |access-date=25 July 2024 |website=Infogob |archive-date=11 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011120957/https://infogob.jne.gob.pe/Politico/FichaPolitico/jose-enrique-jeri-ore_procesos-electorales_ug@eTICaAcoc6+@0ElOxMA==@I |url-status=live }} From November 2015 to April 2016, he was a delegate and member of the [[Alliance for the Progress of Peru]] coalition led by [[César Acuña]] because the party he belonged to, [[We Are Peru]], was a member of said [[electoral alliance]].{{citation needed|date=February 2026}} === Congressman of the Republic === [[File:146° ANIVERSARIO DEL COMBATE DE ANGAMOS - 54841571190.jpg|thumb|right|Jerí as member of Congress (October 2025)]] In the [[2021 Peruvian general election|2021 parliamentary elections]], José Jerí ran for the [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Congress of the Republic]] on behalf of [[We Are Peru]] in the [[Lima|Lima Metropolitan electoral list]] of, running as number 3 on the candidate list. Despite obtaining only 11,654 preferential votes, Jerí managed to be elected as a [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|congressman of the republic]] for the [[2021 Peruvian general election|2021–2026 parliamentary term]] due to the [[Vacunagate|disqualification]] of winning candidate [[Martín Vizcarra]], a former president who obtained 208,387 preferential votes in the election, from holding any public office.{{cite news |access-date=25 July 2024 |date=26 May 2021 |title=2021 Elections: Who is José Jeri, who will enter Congress after Martín Vizcarra's disqualification? |url=https://rpp.pe/politica/elecciones/elecciones-2021-quien-es-jose-jeri-quien-entrara-al-congreso-tras-la-inhabilitacion-de-martin-vizcarra-el-poder-en-tus-manos-noticia-1337387 |website=RPP Noticias |archive-date=25 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725073916/https://rpp.pe/politica/elecciones/elecciones-2021-quien-es-jose-jeri-quien-entrara-al-congreso-tras-la-inhabilitacion-de-martin-vizcarra-el-poder-en-tus-manos-noticia-1337387 |url-status=live }} In July 2021, he ran for president of Congress for the 2021–2022 term, but was unsuccessful.{{cite web |date=26 July 2021 |title=Congress: List 3 was excluded from the election of the Board of Directors |url=https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-congreso-lista-3-quedo-fuera-de-eleccion-mesa-directiva-854913.aspx |access-date=10 August 2023 |website=Andina |language=es |archive-date=11 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011132655/https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-congreso-lista-3-quedo-fuera-de-eleccion-mesa-directiva-854913.aspx |url-status=live }} During the [[Third impeachment of Pedro Castillo|third presidential impeachment process against Pedro Castillo]], Jerí voted in favour of declaring [[Vacancy due to moral incapacity|moral incapacity]] of [[Pedro Castillo]]. The vacancy was approved by 101 parliamentarians on 7 December 2022.{{Citation needed|date=February 2026}} In February 2022, during the third wave of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]], Jerí was photographed entering a bar in the [[Miraflores District, Lima|Miraflores]] district with a young woman who worked as an assistant in his congressional office, to celebrate the birthday of Claudia Llanos Vidal, an official from the municipality of [[La Molina District|La Molina]]. According to reports, Jerí was seen drinking with guests and disregarding social-distancing rules despite a decree from the Presidency of the Council of Ministers enforcing restrictions due to the pandemic.{{cite web |date=8 February 2022 |title=El "after office" del congresista José Jerí |trans-title=The 'after office' of Congressman José Jerí |url=https://elfoco.pe/2022/02/lo-ultimo/el-after-office-del-congresista-jose-jeri/ |access-date=27 July 2025 |website=El Foco |language=es}}{{cite web |work=La República |date=9 February 2022 |title=Captan a congresista José Jerí celebrando en bar sin respetar protocolos ante la COVID-19 |trans-title=Congressman José Jerí caught celebrating in a bar without following COVID-19 protocols |url=https://larepublica.pe/politica/2022/02/09/captan-a-congresista-jose-jeri-celebrando-en-bar-sin-respetar-protocolos-ante-la-covid-19-somos-peru |access-date=10 October 2025 |language=es |archive-date=1 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220801164535/https://larepublica.pe/politica/2022/02/09/captan-a-congresista-jose-jeri-celebrando-en-bar-sin-respetar-protocolos-ante-la-covid-19-somos-peru/ |url-status=live }} He served as president of the Budget Committee during the 2023–2024 legislative year. He served as spokesperson for the [[We Are Peru]] party. He was one of the congressmen who supported the dismissal of the fiscal investigations into [[Dina Boluarte]].{{cite web |date=26 July 2025 |title=José Jerí, new president of Congress, shielded Dina Boluarte from accusations of deaths in protests |url=https://radioondaazul.com/jose-jeri-nuevo-presidente-del-congreso-blindo-a-dina-boluarte-de-denuncia-por-muertes-en-protestas/ |access-date=30 July 2025 |website=Radio Onda Azul |language=es |archive-date=11 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011145628/https://radioondaazul.com/jose-jeri-nuevo-presidente-del-congreso-blindo-a-dina-boluarte-de-denuncia-por-muertes-en-protestas/ |url-status=live }} In January 2025, Jerí was formally accused of [[sexual assault]] following a [[New Year's Eve]] party in [[Canta]]. The alleged incident took place at the Santa Rosa Casa Club in [[Quives]] on 29 December 2024, where Jerí was with a group of friends. Among the guests was Marco Antonio Cardoza Hurtado, who had arrived with a 31-year-old woman (the complainant) and another person. According to the complainant, she lost consciousness that afternoon and later woke up with pain in her intimate parts. The complaint identified both Jerí and Cardoza as suspects.{{cite web |work=Perú 21 |date=14 January 2025 |title=La copa rota del congresista de Somos Perú José Jerí |trans-title=The broken glass of Somos Perú congressman José Jerí |url=https://peru21.pe/investigacion/la-copa-rota-del-congresista-de-somos-peru-jose-jeri/ |access-date=27 July 2025 |language=es |archive-date=18 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118200709/https://peru21.pe/investigacion/la-copa-rota-del-congresista-de-somos-peru-jose-jeri/ |url-status=live }}{{cite web |last=Giraldo |first=Clara |date=10 January 2025 |title=José Jerí, denunciado por presunta violación sexual: lo que se sabe del caso y la investigación de la Fiscalía |trans-title=José Jerí, accused of alleged sexual assault: what is known about the case and the Prosecutor's Office investigation |url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/2025/01/10/jose-jeri-denunciado-por-presunta-violacion-sexual-lo-que-se-sabe-del-caso-y-la-investigacion-de-la-fiscalia/ |access-date=10 October 2025 |website=infobae |language=es |archive-date=11 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011134431/https://www.infobae.com/peru/2025/01/10/jose-jeri-denunciado-por-presunta-violacion-sexual-lo-que-se-sabe-del-caso-y-la-investigacion-de-la-fiscalia/ |url-status=live }} The Civil Court of [[Canta]] admitted the complaint, issued protective measures for the alleged victim, and ordered Jerí to undergo psychological treatment for impulsive and [[pathological]] [[sexual behavior]]. Despite being temporarily suspended by his party, he reportedly failed to comply with the court order for more than five months. As a result, Attorney General [[Delia Espinoza]] filed a separate complaint for disobedience to authority, citing Article 368 of the Criminal Code.{{cite web |work=Perú 21 |date=25 July 2025 |title=Los pasivos de José Jerí en su camino a la presidencia Congreso |trans-title=José Jerí's liabilities on his path to the presidency of Congress |url=https://peru21.pe/politica/los-pasivos-de-jose-jeri-en-su-camino-la-presidencia-congreso/ |access-date=27 July 2025 |language=es |archive-date=26 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250726134035/https://peru21.pe/politica/los-pasivos-de-jose-jeri-en-su-camino-la-presidencia-congreso/ |url-status=live }} ==== President of Congress ==== On 26 July 2025, he was elected as [[President of the Congress of the Republic of Peru|President of the Congress of the Republic]] for the 2025–2026 annual session period with the votes of [[Free Peru]], [[Popular Force]], [[Alliance for Progress (Peru)|Alliance for Progress]], [[Popular Action (Peru)|Acción Popular]], [[Go on Country – Social Integration Party (2017)|Avanza País]] and [[We Are Peru]]. Following his controversial election as President of Congress due to his background, Jerí stated in an interview with the Peruvian newspaper [[El Comercio (Peru)|El Comercio]] in August that he would refrain from assuming the presidency of the executive branch, according to the constitutional line of succession, in the event that [[Dina Boluarte|Boluarte]] were removed from office by Congress. He expressed the following for such a scenario (translated from Spanish):{{cite web|url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/2025/10/10/jose-jeri-dijo-que-se-negaria-a-asumir-la-presidencia-pero-juramento-luego-de-la-vacancia-de-dina-boluarte/|title=José Jerí said he would refuse to assume the presidency but was sworn in after Dina Boluarte's removal|access-date=17 October 2025|last=Oré Arroyo|first=Carlos|date=10 October 2025|website=Infobae|language=es-ES|archive-date=10 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010181241/https://www.infobae.com/peru/2025/10/10/jose-jeri-dijo-que-se-negaria-a-asumir-la-presidencia-pero-juramento-luego-de-la-vacancia-de-dina-boluarte/|url-status=live}}{{cite news|title=José Jerí: "No me han facultado para poner dictámenes de la noche a la mañana"|url=https://elcomercio.pe/politica/congreso/jose-jeri-presidente-del-congreso-no-me-han-facultado-para-poner-dictamenes-de-la-noche-a-la-manana-entrevista-noticia/|newspaper=El Comercio|date=25 August 2025|access-date=19 October 2025|issn=1605-3052|language=es-PE|first=Milagros|last=Leiva|archive-date=24 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251024180504/https://elcomercio.pe/politica/congreso/jose-jeri-presidente-del-congreso-no-me-han-facultado-para-poner-dictamenes-de-la-noche-a-la-manana-entrevista-noticia/|url-status=live}} {{Blockquote|"I was elected to be President of Congress. I'm not going to say I'm unaware of the procedures of constitutional succession, right? But from my perspective, the presidency should be constitutionally renewed on July 28, 2026. If that scenario you mention were to occur, I would personally refrain from assuming it."}}Shortly after being named president of Congress, the television program ''Milagros Leiva, entrevista'' reported an alleged case of [[illicit enrichment]] involving Jerí, noting a sharp increase in his declared assets. In 2021 he declared ownership of two vehicles worth S/ 97,000 [[Peruvian sol|soles]], but by 2024 he reportedly owned properties valued at more than one million soles.{{cite web |last=Quilca Catacora |first=Mariana |date=26 July 2025 |title=José Jerí es el nuevo presidente del Congreso: perfil, antecedentes y denuncias |trans-title=José Jerí is the new president of Congress: profile, background, and accusations |url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/2025/07/26/jose-jeri-es-el-nuevo-presidente-del-congreso-perfil-antecedentes-y-denuncias/ |access-date=26 July 2025 |website=Infobae |language=es |archive-date=30 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250730101439/https://www.infobae.com/peru/2025/07/26/jose-jeri-es-el-nuevo-presidente-del-congreso-perfil-antecedentes-y-denuncias/ |url-status=live }}{{cite web |last=Quilca Catacora |first=Mariana |date=25 July 2025 |title=José Jerí es el nuevo presidente del Congreso: cuestionamientos de los nuevos integrantes de la Mesa Directiva |trans-title=José Jerí is the new president of Congress: objections from the new members of the Board of Directors |url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/2025/07/25/continua-el-dominio-fujicerronista-en-el-congreso-cuestionamientos-a-los-perfiles-que-podrian-integrar-la-mesa-directiva/ |access-date=10 October 2025 |website=Infobae |language=es-ES}} The investigative television program ''[[Panorama (Peruvian TV program)|Panorama]]'' also alleged that Jerí had received a [[Bribery|bribe]] of S/ 150,000 ''soles'' from a businesswoman named Blanca Ríos. The alleged payment took place in November 2023, when Jerí chaired the congressional budget committee, in connection with the approval of public works projects under the portfolio of the [[Ministry of Economy and Finance (Peru)|Ministry of Economy and Finance]]. According to Ríos's testimony, the payment was made to secure funding for an [[irrigation]] project in the [[Cajamarca region]]. The case also implicated congresswoman [[Ana Zegarra]], spokesperson for the We Are Peru party, and Nahum Hidalgo, an advisor to the ''Somos Perú'' parliamentary group. Jerí denied the accusation, stating he had no connection with the person involved and declared that he would cooperate with all investigations.{{cite web |last=Quilca Catacora |first=Mariana |date=26 |language=es-ES |archive-date=10 October 2025 |url-status=live }} He became the eighth individual to serve as president since the resignation of [[Pedro Pablo Kuczynski]] in 2018, a span of just over seven years.{{cite web |last=Mandujano |first=Edgar |date=10 October 2025 |title=Dina Boluarte, vacada: 8 presidentes en 9 años – Caretas Política |url=https://caretas.pe/politica/dina-boluarte-vacada-8-presidentes-en-9-anos/ |access-date=10 October 2025 |website=Caretas |language=es |archive-date=11 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011012448/https://caretas.pe/politica/dina-boluarte-vacada-8-presidentes-en-9-anos/ |url-status=live }} Shortly after being named president, Jerí's social media history was ridiculed for previously [[misogynistic]] posts and he was observed unfollowing [[pornographic]] accounts on [[Instagram]].{{Cite news |last=Alarcón |first=Daniel |date=2026-06-04 |title=Peru's Politics Are a Disaster, but Does It Matter? |url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/the-lede/perus-politics-are-a-disaster-but-does-it-matter |access-date=2026-06-22 |work=[[The New Yorker]] |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}} In his inaugural speech, Jerí pledged to "install and lead a government of transition, empathy, and national reconciliation", and said that the nation "must declare war on crime". Despite the removal of President Dina Boluarte, the [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Congress of the Republic]] rejected a motion of censure against prime minister [[Eduardo Arana Ysa]], meaning that the Boluarte cabinet carried over into the presidency of José Jerí. [[File:XVI GABINETE BINACIONAL ECUADOR-PERÚ 2025. QUITO, 12 DE DICIEMBRE DE 2025. - 54979923416.jpg|thumb|Jerí with Ecuadorian President [[Daniel Noboa]] on 12 December 2025]] Protests against Jerí grew due to allegations of sexual assault.{{cite web |last=Mendivelso |first=Sergio Andrés Gamboa |date=15 October 2025 |title=Reportan heridos por enfrentamientos en medio de manifestaciones en contra del Congreso y Presidencia interina de José Jerí en Lima, Perú |trans-title=Injuries reported from clashes amid demonstrations against Congress and interim presidency of José Jerí in Lima, Peru |url=https://www.eltiempo.com/mundo/latinoamerica/reportan-heridos-por-enfrentamientos-en-medio-de-manifestaciones-en-contra-del-congreso-y-presidencia-interina-de-jose-jeri-en-lima-peru-3500163 |access-date=16 October 2025 |website=El Tiempo |language=es}} He refused to resign, stating "My responsibility is to maintain the stability of the country."{{cite news |author=Caretas |date=16 October 2025 |title=Defensoría: Protestas en Lima dejan un muerto y 102 personas heridas |trans-title=Ombudsman: Protests in Lima leave one dead and 102 injured |url=https://caretas.pe/nacional/defensoria-protestas-en-lima-dejan-un-muerto-y-102-personas-heridas/ |access-date=16 October 2025 |work=Caretas |language=es |archive-date=26 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251026234252/https://caretas.pe/nacional/defensoria-protestas-en-lima-dejan-un-muerto-y-102-personas-heridas/ |url-status=live }} On 15 October, massive demonstrations in major cities across the country denounced the explosion of crime and "corrupt elites", demanding the resignation of the president and Congress. In Lima, the protest ended in violence. One protester was killed by a plainclothes police officer and around 100 people were injured. The government declared a [[state of emergency]] on 21 October, officially to combat crime but, according to its critics, to prevent the protests from continuing.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/oct/25/peru-youth-protesters-state-of-emergency-gen-z|title='We'll march as many times as necessary': Peru's youth protesters defy state of emergency|first=Dan|last=Collyns|date=25 October 2025|via=The Guardian}}{{cite web |url=https://apnews.com/article/peru-violence-emergency-president-jose-jeri-675366bbbfa89e00b4a4e8ea763f03b5 |title=Peru's president declares state of emergency in capital as it tries to stem surging violence |website=[[AP News]] |access-date=23 October 2025 |date=23 October 2025 |archive-date=22 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251022230423/https://apnews.com/article/peru-violence-emergency-president-jose-jeri-675366bbbfa89e00b4a4e8ea763f03b5 |url-status=live }} On 28 November, Jerí declared a state of emergency in areas along the [[Chile–Peru border]] in response to an influx of migrants exiting Chile,{{cite web |title=Peru to declare state of emergency to block Chile border crossings |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/28/peru-to-declare-state-of-emergency-to-block-chile-border-crossings |date=28 November 2025 |access-date=1 December 2025 |website=[[Al Jazeera]]}} predominantly [[Venezuelan refugee crisis|Venezuelans]]. Large numbers of Venezuelans attempted to leave Chile and enter Peru following threats of mass expulsion from Chilean President-elect [[José Antonio Kast]].{{cite news |title=Peru's president to declare border state of emergency to prevent entry of undocumented migrants |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/perus-president-declare-border-state-emergency-prevent-entry-undocumented-2025-11-28/ |work=Reuters |date=28 November 2025}} === Censure === {{Main|Censure of José Jerí}} On 14 February 2026, it was announced that Jerí was under investigation for [[illicit enrichment]] for a second time. He was accused of [[influence peddling]] after the revelation of secretive meetings with Chinese businessmen outside of any official framework.{{cite web|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/14/peru-to-debate-removal-of-president-jose-jeri-four-months-into-his-term|title=Peru to debate removal of President Jose Jeri four months into his term|publisher=Al Jazeera|access-date=17 February 2026|date=17 February 2026}} Three days later, on 17 February, Jerí was removed from the presidency by the Peruvian Congress in a 75–24 vote, with 3 abstentions, following a motion of censure approved weeks before the general elections.{{cite web |date=17 February 2026 |title=Peru's President José Jerí ousted, marking eighth change in leader in less than a decade |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/02/17/americas/peru-president-jose-jeri-ousted-intl-latam |access-date=17 February 2026 |publisher=CNN}} He was removed as President of Congress after he failed to disclose meetings with Chinese businessmen who were under government scrutiny. He was only president for four months.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/17/world/americas/peru-president-jose-jeri-impeachment.html|title=Peru Ousts President, Again|publisher=[[The New York Times]]|date=17 February 2026|access-date=17 February 2026}} [[José María Balcázar]] was sworn in as his successor.{{cite web |last=Elliot; Siniawski |first=Lucinda; Natalia |title=Peru installs Jose Balcazar as interim president after Jeri ousted in political upheaval |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-congress-elects-jose-balcazar-new-interim-president-2026-02-19/ musician
[[Music executive|Producteur]] | genre = {{hlist|Singer|[[Electronic music]]}} | instrument = {{hlist|Voice|Keyboard}} | years_active = Since 2015 | label = [[Initial Artist Services]] | website = {{url|https://herve.store}} }} '''Hervé Le Sourd''', known as '''Hervé''' (born February 19, 1991) is a French singer-songwriter, musician, and producer. He is [[Autodidacticism|self-taught]] and draws inspiration from various musical styles: [[britpop]], [[jungle music|jungle]], [[drum and bass]].{{Cite web|author=Anna|title=Hervé, le poète des temps modernes|url=https://www.masculin.com/culture/433730-herve-chanteur-francais/|website=Masculin.com|date=8 April 2021|access-date=17 April 2021}} His debut album ''Hyper'', released in 2020, won the {{ill|lt=Male Revelation of the Year|Victoire de la révélation masculine|fr}} award at the [[Victoires de la Musique]] in 2021. == Biography == === Youth === Hervé{{Cite web|author=Jonathan Trullard|title=Il est partout avec son premier album ''Hyper'', Hervé la nouvelle voix sensible de la chanson française|url=https://www.francetvinfo.fr/culture/musique/il-est-partout-avec-son-premier-album-hyper-herve-la-nouvelle-voix-sensible-de-la-chanson-francaise_4037939.html|website=[[France Info (radio network)]]|date=10 July 2020 |access-date=14 December 2020}} was born in February 1991 in [[Saint-Cyr-l'École]]. He was raised by his single mother in [[Fontenay-le-Fleury]].{{Cite news|author1=Odile de Plas|title=Hyper|work=[[Télérama]]|date=24 June 2020|issn=0040-2699|pages=44–45}} He first dreamed of becoming a professional footballer. He grew up listening to the songs of [[Alain Bashung]], [[Jacques Higelin]], and the group [[Daft Punk]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.lapresse.ca/arts/musique/2021-03-15/la-revelation-herve.php|title=La révélation Hervé|author=Marissa Groguhé|date=15 March 2021|website=lapresse.ca}} === Career === ==== 2015–2018: Beginnings in the group Postaal ==== In 2015, Hervé began his career in the Franco-British [[Musical ensemble|duo]] Postaal with Englishman Dennis Brown. Their debut single, ''Freedom'', helped the duo gain attention.{{Cite web|language=fr-FR |first=Laura |last=Aronica |title=LE SON DU WEEK-END by BETC Pop : Postaal, "Freedom" |url=https://www.clique.tv/le-son-du-week-end-by-betc-pop-postaal-freedom/ |date=11 July 2015|access-date=15 May 2024}} [[File:Festival des Vieilles Charrues 2021 - Hervé - 03.jpg|thumb|On tour with their first album]] Their first album was released in 2018, and Hervé toured with [[Eddy de Pretto]] for the opening acts of his tour to launch his solo career. That same year, in collaboration with [[Yodelice]], he co-wrote three tracks (''{{ill|lt=Pardonne-moi|Pardonne-moi (chanson de Johnny Hallyday)|fr}}'', ''Je ne suis qu'un homme'', and ''Un enfant du siècle'') for the posthumous album ''{{ill|Mon pays c'est l'amour|fr}}'' by [[Johnny Hallyday]].{{Cite web|author=Philippe Grelard|title=Le Breton Hervé se fait un nom sur la scène electro|url=https://www.letelegramme.fr/musique/herve-se-fait-un-nom-sur-la-scene-electro-22-06-2020-12569926.php|website=[[Le Télégramme]]|date=23 June 2020|access-date=17 April 2021}} ==== 2019–2021: Solo career and debut album ''Hyper'' ==== In May 2019, he released his first EP, ''Mélancolie F.C.'' In June 2020, his first solo album ''Hyper'' was released.{{Cite web|author=Éric Bureau|title=Musique : ''Hyper'' emballé par Hervé et son premier album|url=https://www.leparisien.fr/culture-loisirs/musique/musique-hyper-emballe-par-herve-et-son-premier-album-18-06-2020-8338032.php|website=[[Le Parisien]]|date=18 June 2020|access-date=14 December 2020}} The album is described by ''Télérama'' as "a powerful generational uppercut."{{Cite web|language=fr |title=Avec "Hyper", Hervé décroche un puissant uppercut générationnel |url=https://www.telerama.fr/musique/avec-hyper-herve-decroche-un-puissant-uppercut-generationnel-6659235.php |date=25 June 2020|access-date=15 May 2024}} In February 2021, he won the Male Revelation award at the [[Victoires de la Musique]].{{Cite web|author1=E.Cornet|author2=J.Ababsa|author3=T.Mongellaz, S.Lacombe|title=Victoires de la musique : Clou et Hervé, deux révélations inspirées par le confinement|url=https://www.francetvinfo.fr/culture/musique/victoires-de-la-musique/victoires-de-la-musique-clou-et-herve-deux-revelations-inspirees-par-le-confinement_4294809.html|website=[[France Info (radio network)]]|date=12 February 2021|access-date=17 April 2021}}{{Cite web|author1=Eric Bureau|author2=Emmanuel Marolle|title=Victoires de la musique : Hervé et Yseult, deux révélations du confinement récompensées|url=https://www.leparisien.fr/culture-loisirs/musique/victoires-de-la-musique-herve-et-yseult-deux-revelations-du-confinement-recompensees-12-02-2021-8424653.php|website=[[Le Parisien]]|date=12 February 2021|access-date=17 April 2021}} ==== Since 2022 ==== In 2022, his six-month ''Hyper Tour'' was nominated for the Victoires de la Musique. In 2023, Hervé announced the release of his second album ''Intérieur vie'', which coincides with the birth of his first child.{{Cite web|language=fr-FR |title=Cette sensation française de la musique va avoir son 1er enfant : répercussion forte sur sa carrière |url=https://fr.news.yahoo.com/sensation-fran%C3%A7aise-musique-va-avoir-075700480.html |date=5 September 2023|access-date=15 May 2024}} In 2024, Hervé released his third album, ''Adrénaline''. Due to a manufacturing error, the album contained music from the artist [[Luis Fonsi]] instead of his own.{{Cite web|language=fr-FR |title=Hervé remplacé par Luis Fonsi sur son nouvel album ? {{!}} Les Inrocks |url=https://www.lesinrocks.com/musique/herve-remplace-par-luis-fonsi-sur-son-nouvel-album-620407-31-05-2024/ |website=www.lesinrocks.com|date=31 May 2024|access-date=13 February 2025}} == Participation == Since 2019, he has been the patron of the association Les éveillés in support of exiles. Since November 2023, he has been the patron of the {{ill|Festival ODP Talence|fr}}, benefiting the orphans of French firefighters.{{Cite web|url=https://www.talence.fr/le-festival-odp-talence-au-coeur-du-parc-peixotto/|title=Le Festival ODP Talence au cœur du Parc Peixotto|date=26 November 2024}} == Discography == === Studio albums === {{Hidden|titlealign=left|fw1=normal| [[2020 in music|2020]]: ''Hyper'' (Romance Musique)| # Le premier jour du reste de ma nuit # Trésor # Cœur poids plume # Maelström # Si bien du mal # Fureur de vivre # Paréo parade # Addenda # La peur des mots # Des airs de toi # Bel air }} {{Hidden|titlealign=left|fw1=normal| [[2023 in music|2023]]: ''Intérieur vie'' (Romance Musique)| # D'où je viens # Autour de moi # Tout ira mieux demain # Si tu savais # 25ème heure # Chelou # Pulsions # Rester # La lettre # Dans la peau # Mémoire }} {{Hidden|titlealign=left|fw1=normal| [[2024 in music|2024]]: ''Adrénaline'' (Mélancolie F.C. / Romance Musique)| # Encore # Sémaphore # Comme tout le monde # Moins une # Adrénaline # Tube de l’été # Séquelle # Odeur # CLASHHH! # Rien de personnel }} Upon its release, this last album was mistakenly pressed with [[reggaeton]] tracks by [[Luis Fonsi]]. === Re-releases === {{Hidden|titlealign=left|fw1=normal| [[2021 in music|2021]]: ''Hyper – Prolongations'' (Romance Musique)| # Le premier jour du reste de ma nuit # Trésor # Cœur poids plume # Maelström # Si bien du mal # Fureur de vivre # Paréo parade # Addenda # La peur des mots # Des airs de toi # Bel air # Monde meilleur # Permis de construire # Si elle me revient pas # Rodéo # L'an zéro }} === EPs === {{Hidden|titlealign=left|fw1=normal| [[2019 in music|2019]]: ''Mélancolie F.C.'' Suezawa is affiliated with [[Starto Entertainment]]. == Biography == Due to the influence of his mother, who is a fan of [[SMAP]], he developed an admiration for [[Takuya Kimura]].「なにもんGO! VOL.4 末澤誠也」『[[Myōjō|Myojo]]』January 2017 issue, [[Shueisha]], November 22, 2016, p. 84. A friend of Suezawa's mother sent his resume to [[Johnny & Associates]], predecessor of Starto Entertainment.「関西ジャニーズJr.ごっつええやん!! Vol.17 末澤誠也」、『産経新聞夕刊 関西版』[[Sankei Shimbun]] Evening Edition Kansai Edition, June 24, 2017 issue, [[Sankei Shimbun]], June 24, 2017, Entertainment section, p.4. After passing the audition, he joined the agency on April 3, 2009. He then began his activities with the name 'Kansai's Johnny's Jr.' After entering university, he didn't have much stage opportunity for 2 years. There was a period when he could only work a few times a year as backup dancers at dome shows or other evets that were understaffed. At that time, while practicing daily with a dance club, he decided to quit Kansai's Johnny's Jr. at the end of 2014 to find a job in the fashion industry, which he told his family. {{Infobox musical artist | name = Rincon Sapiência | image = Rincon Sapiencia 3.jpg | caption = Rincon Sapiência in 2010 | birth_name = Danilo Albert Ambrosio | alias = Manicongo | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1985|9|9|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[São Paulo]], Brazil | death_date = | death_place = | origin = | instrument = | occupation = {{flatlist| * Rapper * poet * singer * composer * multi-instrumentalist }} | genre = {{Flatlist| *[[Rap music|Rap]] *[[Hip hop]] }} | years_active = 2000—present | label = | website = }} '''Danilo Albert Ambrosio''' (born 9 September 1985), better known by his artistic names '''Rincon Sapiência''' or '''Manicongo''', is a Brazilian rapper and poet. He began his career in 2000, and gained success in 2009 with the single "Elegância".{{Cite web |last=Antunes |first=Pedro |date=14 December 2018 |title=Com Rincon Sapiência, Amanda Magalhães quer a liberdade de ser "brega de amor" em Fazer Valer; assista |url=https://rollingstone.uol.com.br/noticia/com-rincon-sapiencia-amanda-magalhaes-quer-liberdade-de-ser-brega-de-amor-em-fazer-valer-assista/ |access-date=27 November 2025|website=[[Rolling Stone Brasil]] |publisher=Grupo Perfil}} == Career == Rincon Sapiência began his career in 2000 as part of the band Munições da 38, where he performed under the names Rincon X and MC Shato.{{Cite web |title=Rincon Sapiência vulgo Manicongo em Música do MySpace – Transmissão gratuita de MP3s, Fotos & Vídeos |url=http://www.myspace.com/rinconzl |access-date=27 November 2025|work=myspace.com}} Still, he worked as part of the groups Ébanos, 2º Assalto, Plano B, Equilíbrio Insano and Porte Verbal, performing with the latter in their album ''As Coisas Vão Melhorar...'', released by Salmus Produções in 2003. In 2005, he became a member of the label Plano Áudio, made by rapper Kamau, and was part of the band ''Simples'', during which he released his first solo song, "Aventureiro", that was included in the album ''Escuta Aí''. Beginning after that, he would perform shows throughout [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]] state and other states. Along with rapping, Rincon developed poetry workshops, hip hop events, and other social activities. In 2005, he participated in the [[World Social Forum]], where he rapped freestyle on an open mic and won the improvised championship that took place at the event.{{Cite web |title=Central Hip-Hop - 2010 - Bocada Forte - Nós Trabalhamos Pelo Hip-Hop Brasileiro |url=http://centralhiphop.uol.com.br/site/?id=441&url=colunas_detalhes.php |access-date=27 November 2025 |publisher=centralhiphop.uol.com.br }}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} He also took part in the group Audácia, which also included Cafuris, RG, Rocha, and Raphão. In 2009, he participated in the [[TV Cultura]] program Manos e Minas together with [[Projota]] and [[Rashid (rapper)|Rashid]].{{Cite web |title=Projota, Rashid e Rincon Sapiência no Manos e Minas {{!}} Noticiário Periférico |date=5 June 2009 |url=http://www.noticiario-periferico.com/2009/06/projota-rashid-e-rincon-sapiencia-no.html |access-date=27 November 2025|publisher=www.noticiario-periferico.com}} A month after, in July 2009, he released "Elegância", which was accompanied by a music video in March 2010 that was shown on [[MTV Brasil]].{{Cite web |title=Estreia no MTV Lab Coletivo: Rincon Sapiência - Elegância MTV Brasil |url=http://mtv.uol.com.br/coletivo/blog/estreia-no-mtv-lab-coletivo-rincon-sapiencia-elegancia |access-date=27 November 2025 |publisher=mtv.uol.com.br }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} This single became part of his first promotional album, titled ''Promotrampo Volume 1''. He was nominated for the [[2010 MTV Video Music Brazil]] in the Rap category.{{Cite web |title=MTV divulga os indicados ao VMB 2010 - Yahoo! Notícias |url=http://br.noticias.yahoo.com/s/16072010/48/entretenimento-mtv-divulga-indicados-vmb-2010.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100723161347/http://br.noticias.yahoo.com/s/16072010/48/entretenimento-mtv-divulga-indicados-vmb-2010.html |archive-date=2010-07-23 |access-date=27 November 2025 |publisher=br.noticias.yahoo.com}} He took part in the [[NX Zero]] album ''Projeto Paralelo'' where he appeared on the track "Tarde Pra Desistir", one of four rare tracks. In 2016, Rincon released his single, titled "Ponta de Lança - Verso Livre". Rincon also participated in Poetas no Topo 3.1 - Prólogo, a series of videos that brought together 38 MC's from 8 states. His solo album ''Galanga Livre'' was honored as the best Brazilian album in 2017 by ''[[Rolling Stone Brasil]]''.{{Cite web |date=2017 |title=Melhores Discos Nacionais de 2017 |url=https://rollingstone.uol.com.br/galeria/melhores-discos-nacionais-de-2017/ |access-date=27 November 2025|website=[[Rolling Stone Brasil]] |publisher=[[Grupo Spring de Comunicação]]}} With both Galanga Livre and Ponta de Lança, his works have appeared in academic works putting forth the possibilities of the dialogue of rap as Afro-Brazilian literature.{{Cite web |title=Plataforma Sucupira |url=https://sucupira-legado.capes.gov.br/sucupira/public/consultas/coleta/trabalhoConclusao/viewTrabalhoConclusao.jsf?popup=true&id_trabalho=11733919 |access-date=27 November 2025|website=sucupira-legado.capes.gov.br}} Blackness and the reeducation of ethnic-racial relations have been part of his musical career.{{Cite web |title=Plataforma Sucupira |url=https://sucupira-legado.capes.gov.br/sucupira/public/consultas/coleta/trabalhoConclusao/viewTrabalhoConclusao.jsf?popup=true&id_trabalho=7702791 |access-date=27 November 2025|website=sucupira-legado.capes.gov.br}} In 2018, Rincon joined various legendary and respected rappers in the Brazilian rap scene, such as [[Emicida]], [[Mano Brown]], [[Rael (rapper)|Rael]], [[Djonga]], and BK in the single O céu é o limite. Along with works with [[Drik Barbosa]] and Rubel, Rincon started an artistic partnership with [[Iza (singer)|IZA]], including the single "Ginga"; and with [[Alice Caymmi]] on the track "Inimigos" on her album ''[[Alice (Alice Caymmi album)|Alice]]''. In 2019, he released his second studio album, titled ''Mundo Manicongo: Dramas, Danças e Afroreps'', premiering the single Mundo Manicongo on the YouTube channel COLORS.{{Cite web |title=Plataforma Sucupira |url=https://sucupira-legado.capes.gov.br/sucupira/public/consultas/coleta/trabalhoConclusao/viewTrabalhoConclusao.jsf?popup=true&id_trabalho=13798982 |access-date=27 November 2025 |website=sucupira-legado.capes.gov.br}} == Personal life == Rincon was born on 9 September 1985 in [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]]. '''Michel Dias Costa''' (born 21 March 1988), better known as '''Rashid''', is a Brazilian rapper, author, producer, and businessman. He became known in the [[São Paulo]] rap scene for hits such as  “Bilhete 2.0” (2017) and “Sobrou silêncio” (2020),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.popmatters.com/rashid-brazilian-rap-interview-2025|title=Rashid Brings Brazilian Rap to Lincoln Center|last=Ribeiro|first=Ana Clara|publisher=PopMatters|date=31 July 2025|access-date=6 January 2026}}</ref> and for his collaborations with other prominent Brazilian rappers such as [[Emicida]], [[Rael (rapper)|Rael]], and [[Rincon Sapiência]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://musicapave.com/artigos/emicida-e-seus-10-anos-de-triunfo/ |title=Emicida e seus “10 Anos de Triunfo” : Música Pavê |access-date=6 January 2026|website=musicapave.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gregório|first=Rafael|title=Cada vez mais MPB, rapper Rael da Rima se apresenta em SP |url=http://guia.folha.uol.com.br/shows/1216612-cada-vez-mais-mpb-rapper-rael-da-rima-se-apresenta-em-sp.shtml |access-date=6 January 2026|publisher=UOL}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Projota, Rashid e Rincon Sapiência no Manos e Minas {{!}} Noticiário Periférico |date=5 June 2009 |url=http://www.noticiario-periferico.com/2009/06/projota-rashid-e-rincon-sapiencia-no.html |access-date=6 January 2026|publisher=www.noticiario-periferico.com}}</ref>

His album ''Crise'' was elected the 39th best Brazilian album of 2018 by ''[[Rolling Stone Brasil]]''<ref name="rsbmelhores18">{{Cite web |last=Antunes |first=Pedro |date=21 December 2018 |title=Rolling Stone Brasil: os 50 melhores discos nacionais de 2018 |url=https://rollingstone.uol.com.br/noticia/rolling-stone-brasil-os-50-melhores-discos-nacionais-de-2018/ |access-date=5 January 2026|website=Rolling Stone Brasil |publisher=Grupo Perfil}}</ref> and one of the 25 best Brazilian albums of the first half of 2018 by the [[São Paulo Art Critics Association]].<ref name="apcamelhores18">{{Cite web |last=Antunes |first=Pedro |date=30 November 2018 |title=Baco Exu do Blues, Gilberto Gil, Duda Beat: os 25 melhores discos brasileiros do segundo semestre de 2018, segundo a APCA |url=https://rollingstone.uol.com.br/noticia/baco-exu-do-blues-gilberto-gil-carne-doce-duda-beat-apca-escolhe-os-25-melhores-discos-brasileiros-do-segundo-semestre-2018/ |access-date=5 January 2026|website=Rolling Stone Brasil |publisher=Grupo Perfil}}</ref>

He is also the author of the 2018 book ''Ideias que rimam mais que palavras - Vol. 1'', which explores his music and explains the meaning behind his music. He has toured extensively for the book.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://revistatrip.uol.com.br/trip/rapper-rashid-lanca-o-livro-ideias-que-rimam-mais-que-palavras-vol1|title=Rashid dando a letra|last=Ito|first=Carol|publisher=Revista Trip|date=3 July 2018|access-date=5 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Jeong Jae-won''' ({{Korean|hangul=정재원}}; born January 26, 1989), known professionally as '''Jukjae''' ({{Korean|hangul=적재|labels=no}}), is a South Korean singer, songwriter and guitarist. He is affiliated with Abyss Company.

==Career==
Jeong graduated from [[Seoul Institute of the Arts]] with a bachelor's degree in practical music in 2008 and began his musical career as a guitarist.

On November 10, 2014, Jukjae debuted with his first studio album, ''One Word'' (한마디).<ref>{{Cite web |title=싱어송라이터로 거듭나다! 정재원이 전하는 앨범 이야기 |url=http://www.melon.com/musicstory/detail.htm?mstorySeq=1927&startIndex= |website=멜론 |accessdate=2022-02-07 |language=ko}}</ref> He also wrote the lyrics, composed the music, arranged, produced, sang, and played guitar on this album under the name Jeong Jaewon. The following year, on April 23, 2015, he released the digital single "사랑한대".

On March 9, 2017, Jukjae released his first EP, ''FINE''. The title song, "Let's Go See the Stars," is one of Jukjae's signature songs, and became a hot topic after being covered by actor [[Park Bo-gum]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=パク・ボゴム、「スケッチブック」初出演…"デビュー前、シンガーソングライターが夢だった"|url=https://kt.wowkorea.jp/news-read/44205.html|website=wowKorea|date=2020-03-20|accessdate=2020-12-17|publisher=}}</ref>

On June 29, 2019, he held his first solo concert in about three years, "One Step Further" (한걸음, 더), at the Seogang Merry Hall Grand Theater.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Bxgs-mllnee/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link|title=Jukjae|website=Instagram|date=May 16, 2019}}</ref>

On September 1, 2020, Jukjae signed an exclusive contract with his agency, Antenna.<ref>{{Cite web|title=シンガーソングライターのJukjae、ユ･ヒヨル設立の「Antenna」と専属契約…「長年の信頼を基に成立」|url=https://www.kbsworld.ne.jp/entertainment/view?blcSn=55404&rowNum=3|website=kbsworld|accessdate=2020-11-19|publisher=|date=2020-09-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-09-01 |title=적재, 안테나와 전속계약 체결…안테나 "적극 서포터 예정"[공식] |url=https://sports.chosun.com/news/ntype.htm?id=202009020100007620000164&servicedate=20200901 |access-date=2023-08-14 |website=[[Sports Chosun]]|language=ko}}</ref> On November 9, he released his second studio album, ''The LIGHTS'', their first in about eight years.<ref>{{Cite web|title=チョクジェ、タイトル曲「Lights」MV公開…ペク・イェリンがフィーチャリングとして参加 |url=https://kstyle.com/article.ksn?articleNo=2205187 |website=Kstyle |access-date=2022-12-03}}</ref> On November 12, he released his second EP, ''2006''. Jukjae described it as "an album that contains songs that best express my true colors."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=チョクジェ、ニューミニアルバム「2006」を発売…親友のIUに感謝のコメントも“本当に必要な話をたくさんしてくれる”|url=https://kstyle.com/article.ksn?articleNo=2156130|website=Kstyle|accessdate=2020-12-17|publisher=|date=2020-11-12}}</ref> On December 4, he won the Best Session Award (Other Category) at the [[Melon Music Awards]] 2020.<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iLIEpay8BPA|title=[MMA 2020] 사전시상 세션상 - 김현아, 신석철, 적재, 최훈, 홍소진|date=December 4, 2020|website=YouTube}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=BTS（防弾少年団）が驚異の6冠！「MMA 2020」で感激のコメント…MONSTA X＆IZ*ONE＆THE BOYZらも続々登場（総合）|url=https://kstyle.com/article.ksn?articleNo=2157476|website=Kstyle|accessdate=2020-12-17|publisher=|date=2020-12-05}}</ref>

On June 30, 2023, Jukjae's exclusive contract with Antenna ended.<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Kevin |date=2023-06-05 |title=Singer Jukjae Departs Antenna - JazmineMedia |url=https://www.jazminemedia.com/news/singer-jukjae-departs-antenna/, |access-date=2023-08-14 |language=en-us}}</ref> On July 3, he signed an exclusive contract with Abyss Company.

In December 2025, [[Fender (company)|Fender]] Music Korea released the JUKJAE Stratocaster Baggy, the first signature guitar by a Korean artist.<ref>{{Cite web|title=フェンダー、韓国人アーティスト初のシグネイチャーギター発表 韓国語で「白い服」を意味する一本|url=https://www.oricon.co.jp/news/2424499/full/|website=オリコンニュース（ORICON NEWS）|access-date=2025-12-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.guitarworld.com/gear/electric-guitars/fender-launches-jukjae-signature-guitar|title=“The beginning of new relationships between Fender and Korean artists”: Fender unveils its first-ever signature guitar with a South Korean artist – and it’s a streamlined Strat with a trick up its sleeve|publisher=Guitar World|date=December 15, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In an interview, Jukjae said, "When we think of a band, we often think of the vocalist and the supporting musicians separately, but I want to be a musician who shows what it means to have both instruments and voices working in harmony and to make the most of both."<ref>{{Cite web|title=2015년 주목해야 할 싱어송라이터 기대주, 정재원|url=http://www.melon.com/musicstory/detail.htm?mstorySeq=2387|website=멜론|accessdate=2021-09-24|language=ko|date=2015-04-23}}</ref>

In addition to his singing career, Jukjae is also actively involved in music, arranging and playing guitar for albums and concerts by fellow musicians such as [[IU (entertainer)|IU]], [[Akdong Musician]], [[Jung Eun-ji]], [[Taeyeon]], [[Ha Sung-woon]], and [[Lim Han-byul]]. He was particularly active as the guitarist for the so-called "IU team" during IU's live sessions. Jukjae's activities as part of the IU team came to an end with the IU special episode of "Yoo Hee-yeol's Sketchbook," which aired on KBS2 on September 18, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CFSK36ID97u/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link|title=Jukjae|website=Instagram|date=September 19, 2020}}</ref>

In July 2025, Jukjae announced his marriage to Heo Sung-yeon, the older sister of [[Kara (South Korean group)|Kara]] member [[Hur Young-ji|Youngji]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=歌手Jukjae、KARAヨンジの実姉ホ・ソンヨンと結婚 「生涯を約束する相手ができた」|url=https://ekr.chosunonline.com/site/data/html_dir/2025/07/01/2025070180190.html|website=ekr.chosunonline.com|date=2025-07-01|access-date=2025-12-29|language=ja|last=エンタメコリア}}</ref> The wedding took place in October of the same year.<ref>{{Cite web|title=JUKJAE＆ホ・ソンヨン、本日（3日）非公開結婚…妹ホ・ヨンジ（KARA）“クールに見送る”|url=https://korepo.com/archives/1594588|website=K-POP、韓国エンタメニュース、取材レポートならコレポ！|access-date=2025-12-29|language=ja}}</ref>

'''Adonnecy Joshua "AJ" Bramah''' (born May 11, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Hanoi Buffaloes]] of the [[Vietnam Basketball Association]] (VBA). He previously played [[college basketball]] for the [[Sheridan College|Sheridan Bruins]], [[Robert Morris Colonials men's basketball|Robert Morris Colonials]], and the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada Wolf Pack]].

==College career==

===Sheridan College===

As a freshman for [[Sheridan College]], Bramah averaged 14 PPG, and 10.1 RPG. His career high was on a win against [[Williston State College]], dropping 26 points in a 95–77 win.

===Robert Morris===

For the Generals, Bramah led them in the [[Northern Conference]] tournament, averaging 17.3 PPG, and 7 RPG. In his first season, Bramah received All-Team NEC honours.

==Professional career==

On April 21, 2022, Bramah was drafted 1st overall pick in the 2022 [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto|LNB]] Draft by the [[Indios de San Francisco de Macorís]].<ref>{{Cite web |author=Chris Murray |date=21 April 2022 |title=Ex-Nevada basketball player AJ Bramah the first overall pick in pro league draft
|url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/ex-nevada-basketball-player-aj-bramah-first-overall-pick-in-pro-league-draft|access-date=12 March 2026|website=nevadasportsnet.com |language=en}}</ref>

On February 1, 2025, [[Pacific Caesar]] of the [[Indonesian Basketball League]] signed Bramah, replacing former forward, Alioune Tew.<ref>{{Cite web |author=IBLIndonesia |date=1 February 2025 |title=AJ Bramah, Pemain Muda Pengganti Alioune Tew di Tim Pacific|url=https://iblindonesia.com/news/aj-bramah-pemain-muda-pengganti-alioune-tew-di-tim-pacific|access-date=12 March 2026|website=iblindonesia.com |language=id}}</ref> In his debut match against [[Satria Muda Pertamina]] on February 7, 2025, Bramah dropped 31 points and 12 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web |author=IBLIndonesia |date=7 February 2025 |title=Dengan 31 Poin, AJ Bramah Langsung Tancapkan Kuku di IBL|url=https://iblindonesia.com/news/dengan-31-poin-aj-bramah-langsung-tancapkan-kuku-di-ibl|access-date=12 March 2026|website=iblindonesia.com |language=id}}</ref>

'''Gary Eugene Redus II''' (born June 23, 1989) is an American basketball coach who is currently the head coach of the [[Rutgers University–New Brunswick|Rutgers University]] [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights women's basketball|women's basketball team]].<ref name="Rutgers hiring">{{cite web |title=Rutgers Tabs Gary Redus II To Lead Women’s Basketball Program |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2026/3/9/womens-basketball-rutgers-tabs-gary-redus-ii-to-lead-womens-basketball-program |website=Rutgers University Athletics |access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref>

== Playing career ==
Redus played his freshman year of college basketball at [[Marion Military Institute]] before transferring to [[Centenary Gentlemen basketball|Centenary College]] in Louisiana for his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gary Inks Redus and Tubner as Recruiting Continues |url=https://www.gocentenary.com/sports/mbkb/2007-08/releases/4962.0.html |website=Centenary Athletics |access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref> He transferred to [[South Alabama Jaguars men's basketball|South Alabama]] after his sophomore season, citing wanting to be closer to his family and due to Centenary's program being placed on probation.<ref name="USA profile piece">{{cite web |title=FROM HARDBALL TO ROUNDBALL: “G” REDUS TAKES A DIFFERENT PATH TO STARDOM |url=https://usajaguars.com/story.aspx?filename=MBB_0214114711&file_date=2/14/2011 |website=University of South Alabama Athletics |access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref>

Redus played professionally in China, the Middle East, and South America before injuries cut his professional career short.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Broussard |first1=Justin |title=Gary Redus II and his path to the LSU Women's Basketball program |url=https://www.lsudaily.com/post/gary-redus-ii-and-his-path-to-the-lsu-women-s-basketball-program |website=LSU Daily |access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref>

== Coaching career ==
Redus began his coaching career at [[West Georgia Wolves women's basketball|West Georgia]], during which he earned a master's degree. He was also an assistant at [[Delta State Lady Statesmen basketball|Delta State]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores women's basketball|Vanderbilt]], and [[SMU Mustangs women's basketball|SMU]] before joining LSU as an assistant coach.

=== LSU ===
Redus was named an assistant coach at [[LSU Tigers women's basketball|LSU]] on April 20, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Coach Mulkey Adds Gary Redus II As Assistant Coach |url=https://lsusports.net/news/2022/04/20/coach-mulkey-adds-gary-redus-ii-as-assistant-coach/ |website=LSU Athletics |access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref> Redus was credited as the program's lead recruiter, bringing in talent such as [[Angel Reese]], [[Hailey Van Lith]], and [[Aneesah Morrow]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jennings |first1=Chantel |title=Rutgers to hire LSU assistant Gary Redus II as head coach |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7101566/2026/03/09/rutgers-lsu-hire-gary-redus/ |website=The Athletic |access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref>

=== Rutgers ===
Redus was named the head coach at [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights women's basketball|Rutgers]] on March 9, 2026.<ref name="Rutgers hiring" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Franklin |first1=Paul |title=Gary Redus promises quick turnaround for Rutgers women's basketball |url=https://www.mycentraljersey.com/story/sports/college/rutgers/2026/03/18/rutgers-womens-basketball-gary-redus-coach/89202835007/ |website=MyCentralJersey.com |access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref> He signed a five-year contract worth $4 million.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fonseca |first1=Brian |title=Gary Redus contract details: Salary, assistant pool, more for Rutgers women’s hoops’ new coach |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgerswomen/2026/03/gary-redus-contract-details-salary-assistant-pool-more-for-rutgers-womens-hoops-new-coach.html |website=NJ.com |access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Kristian Strande''' (born 3 October 1997) is a Norwegian footballer who plays as a centre-back for [[Moss FK]].

==Career==
He was born in [[Molde]]<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|new_id=pe441865}}</ref> as a son of footballer [[Trond Strande]]. As he was brought up in his father's club [[Molde FK]], Kristian Strande trained with [[Sheffield United]] U18s in November–December 2015 and [[Kristiansund BK]] in January 2016. He was then given a paying contract with Molde, alongside midfielder Ola Husby.<ref>{{cite news|title=Får proffkontrakt i MFK|date=26 January 2016|work=Romsdals Budstikke|pages=12–13|language=no}}</ref> He was soon included in the Molde squad that faced [[Sevilla FC]] in the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League#Round of 32|2015–16 UEFA Europa League round of 32]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Han har ikke spilt ett sekund i eliteserien. Men Kristian (18) kan debutere mot Sevilla|date=24 February 2016|work=Romsdals Budstikke, onsdag|pages=12–13|language=no}}</ref> He also played in the [[2016 Norwegian Football Cup|2016 cup]], where he was credited with Molde's progress. As team struggled in the second round, Strande was awarded a penalty which was converted by [[Mohamed Elyounoussi]] to put Molde through.<ref>{{cite news|title=Her redder han MFK fra cupflause|date=28 April 2016|work=Romsdals Budstikke|pages=26–27|language=no}}</ref> Strande also won the 2016 [[Norwegian Youth Cup]] with Molde.<ref name=2div/>

In 2017, Strande and Ola Husby were loaned out to [[Brattvåg IL]] to gain more senior experience and secure promotion from the [[2017 3. divisjon]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Skal rykke opp med Brattvåg|date=18 August 2017|work=[[Nordre]]|page=12|language=nn}}</ref> Then, instead of seeing through his contract until the summer of 2018, Strande signed for [[Egersunds IK]] ahead of the [[2018 2. divisjon]] season.<ref name=2div>{{cite news|title=Derfor forlot han Molde før kontraktsslutt|date=8 May 2018|work=Romsdals Budstikke|pages=12–13|language=no}}</ref> In the following years, Strande became a bit of a [[Journeyman (sports)|journeyman]] player with single-season spells in Egersund, Brattvåg, [[Hamkam]] and [[Arendal Fotball|Arendal]].<ref name=nff>{{NFF|3813631}}</ref>

Ahead of the 2022 season, Strande announced his move to [[Levanger FK]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ilevanger.no/midtstopper-fra-molde-klar-for-lfk-kjempesignering/s/5-125-73803|title=Midtstopper fra Molde klar for LFK: – Kjempesignering|date=22 January 2022|work=I Levanger|language=no|access-date=10 April 2026}}</ref> However, he pulled out of the contract, stating that he wished to live closer to his girlfriend in the Oslo region. He also claimed that he had no binding written contract and that no transfer papers were signed. He played friendly matches for [[Moss FK]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Strande stoppes av trønderklubb|date=12 March 2022|work=Moss Avis|pages=26–27|language=no}}</ref> and eventually joined that club. He stayed for several years and became [[captain (association football)|team captain]], winning promotion to the [[2023 1. divisjon]]. In that season, he led the statistic for most yellow cards.<ref>{{cite news|title=OBOS-ligaens sindige råtass|date=30 September 2023|work=Moss Avis|page=16|language=no}}</ref>

'''Robin Rasch''' (born 10 January 1994) is a Norwegian footballer who plays as a midfielder for [[KFUM-Kameratene Oslo|KFUM]].

==Career==
Born in [[Akershus University Hospital|Lørenskog]],<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|new_id=pe325162}}</ref> he hails from [[Ski, Norway|Ski]] and started his youth career in [[Ski IL]]. He then progressed to the umbrella team in the region, [[Follo FK]], where he made his senior debut in the [[2012 2. divisjon]]. He helped win promotion to the [[2013 1. divisjon]], and in 2016 he moved to [[KFUM-Kameratene Oslo|KFUM]] on the same level.<ref name=nff>{{NFF|3683593}}</ref> KFUM were relegated in 2016, but re-promoted in 2018.

Rasch became a long-serving [[captain (association football)|team captain]], eventually leading KFUM to promotion to the [[2024 Eliteserien]], a level on which the club had never contested. He was the last squad member remaining from the previous promotion in 2018, and it had become a talking point that Rasch would not be picked up by other clubs, never reaching the [[Eliteserien]] unless he did so with KFUM.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nettavisen.no/sport/har-lengst-fartstid-i-kaffa-stallen-treneren-er-glad-ingen-har-plukket-ham-opp/s/5-95-1305367|title=Har lengst fartstid i Kåffa-stallen – treneren er glad ingen har plukket ham opp|date=9 September 2023|work=Nettavisen|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nettavisen.no/sport/kfum-helt-tok-til-tarene-folk-har-sagt-han-ikke-er-god-nok/s/5-95-1435826|title=KFUM-helt tok til tårene: – Folk har sagt han ikke er god nok|date=6 November 2023|work=Nettavisen|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> Rasch made his Eliteserien debut in April 2024 against Hamkam.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oblad.no/endelig-fikk-robin-30-fra-ski-drommen-oppfylt-jeg-er-ikke-overrasket/s/5-68-1612029|title=Endelig fikk Robin (30) fra Ski drømmen oppfylt: – Jeg er ikke overrasket|date=8 January 2025|work=Østlandets Blad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

Rasch is known as an able free kick taker.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://tipsbladet.no/robin-rasch-er-obos-ligaens-frispark-konge/|title=Robin Rasch er OBOS-ligaens frispark-konge|date=10 June 2023|work=Tipsbladet|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> Rasch's role in central midfield is that of a play-builder. He has stated inspiration from [[chess]], [[Fantasy Premier League]] and play-by-play analysis such as [[Wyscout]] in his modelling of his play.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.451.no/jeg-ma-styre-spillet-med-hodet-ikke-beina/|title=Rasch: – Fotball er som sjakk|date=28 June 2025|work=451.no|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> He has also competed on national level in the age-specific categories of [[golf]], and spends time on both racket games and card games.<ref name=nett/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oblad.no/sportssaker-fra-ski/sport/ski/utfordrer-eliten-med-brukket-ta/s/2-2.2610-1.5350697|title=Utfordrer eliten med brukket tå|date=4 June 2010|work=Østlandets Blad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> He beat [[Viktor Hovland]] on the Junior Tour in his teens, and has also beat [[Erling Haaland]] in a match where Follo faced Haaland's [[Bryne FK|Bryne]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oblad.no/robin-31-har-noe-pa-sin-cv-som-ingen-vil-klare-a-kopiere/s/5-68-1724807|title=Robin (31) har noe på sin CV som ingen vil klare å kopiere|date=10 September 2025|work=Østlandets Blad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

During his career Rasch has faced various injury breaks, partially owing to being diagnosed with both [[ulcerous colitis]] (which leads to inflammations) and [[ankylosing spondylitis]].<ref name=nett>{{cite news|url=https://www.nettavisen.no/sport/kfum-kapteinen-slet-med-skader-betennelser-og-blodninger-ny-medisin-endret-hverdagen-hans/s/5-95-1020892|title=KFUM-kapteinen slet med skader, betennelser og blødninger – ny medisin endret hverdagen hans|date=8 April 2023|work=Nettavisen|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> He missed major parts of the [[2025 Eliteserien]] season.

'''Remi-André Svindland''' (born 29 October 1997) is a Norwegian footballer who plays as a midfielder for [[Bryne FK]].

==Career==
Born<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|new_id=pe325016}}</ref> and raised in [[Elverum]], he started playing youth football in [[Elverum Fotball|Elverum IL]], where he made his senior debut in the [[2013 1. divisjon]].<ref name=nff>{{NFF|2885728}}</ref> Following Elverum's relegation, they returned to the second tier in [[2017 1. divisjon|2017]]. The following season, he moved to [[Moss FK]], having also been considered by [[Fredrikstad FK]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.f-b.no/remi-svindland/moss/ffk/aktuell-for-ffk-endte-opp-i-moss/s/5-59-1074514|title=Aktuell for FFK – endte opp i Moss|date=9 April 2018|work=Fredriksstad Blad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.moss-avis.no/moss-fk/fotball/serieforhands/remi-20-kan-fa-sin-mfk-debut/s/5-67-617808|title=Moss Fotballklubb serieåpner mot Bærum. Remi (20) kan få sin MFK-debut|date=13 April 2018|work=Moss Avis|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

In 2020 he moved on to [[KFUM-Kameratene Oslo|KFUM]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.moss-avis.no/kjarkomne-svindland-penger-for-mfk/s/5-67-1031959|title=Kjærkomne Svindland-penger for MFK|date=18 March 2020|work=Moss Avis|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> He achieved a special mention in the club history when he scored the goal that secured KFUM's promotion to the [[2024 Eliteserien]], the club's first-ever appearance on that level.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nettavisen.no/sport/historisk-opprykk-svindland-sendte-kfum-til-himmels/s/5-95-1420875|title=Historisk opprykk. Svindland sendte KFUM til himmels|date=5 November 2023|work=Nettavisen|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> He made his Eliteserien debut in April 2024 against Hamkam.<ref name=nff/>

In 2025 he left KFUM for another newly promoted Eliteserien team, [[Bryne FK]]. Already in his second training, he suffered an injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aftenbladet.no/sport/i/OoJVEV/paa-den-andre-treningen-gikk-det-galt-kjente-med-en-gang-at-dette-var-alvorlig|title=På den andre treningen gikk det galt: – Kjente med en gang at dette var alvorlig|date=6 April 2025|work=Stavanger Aftenblad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> As a result, he did not play a single competitive match in 2025.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.jbl.no/tilbakeslag-for-mannen-som-fikk-en-marerittstart/s/5-103-1179983|title=Tilbakeslag for mannen som fikk en marerittstart|date=7 August 2025|work=Jærbladet|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ostlendingen.no/remi-svindland-fra-elverum-jobber-for-a-komme-tilbake-pa-banen-etter-skademarerittet-i-bryne/s/80-69-113913|title=– Mitt tøffeste år hittil|date=13 October 2025|work=Østlendingen|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> When he played a full match in 2026, it was 532 minutes since last time.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aftenbladet.no/sport/i/V6gG3d/spilte-90-minutter-for-foerste-gang-paa-532-dager-det-har-vaert-toeft|title=Spilte 90 minutter for første gang på 532 dager: – Det har vært tøft|date=13 April 2026|work=Stavanger Aftenblad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

'''Mario Moore''' is a painter from Detroit, where he also lives and works. His work focuses on Black people and culture in America. His paintings "draw parallels" between modern and historical racial dynamics and portrays them in his art. He is known for the eye contact that the figures in his paintings seem to make with the viewer.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Mario Moore Bio |url=https://www.louisbuhl.com/mario-moore-bio |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=Louis Buhl Gallery / Detroit, MI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=ByStories & Insights |title=Meet Mario Moore |url=https://canvasrebel.com/meet-mario-moore/ |access-date=2026-07-07 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Exhibitions ==
Several art studios and fairs have shown Moore's work. Collections in which is work is a permanent staple are Studio Museum in Harlem; The Detroit Institute of Arts; and the Princeton University Art Museum, NJ. The "BUTTER" Art Fair showcased him as an artist along with other Black artists.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />

Other exhibitions include the Smart Museum of Art, Chicago, IL; David Klein Gallery, Detroit, MI; The Urban Institute of Contemporary Arts, Grand Rapids, MI; Cranbrook Art Museum, Bloomfield Hills, MI; Jeffrey Deitch Gallery, Los Angeles, CA; Arthur Roger Gallery, New Orleans, LA; The Cleveland Museum of Art, and Colby College Museum of Art.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mario Moore |url=https://www.studiomuseum.org/artists/mario-moore |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=Studio Museum in Harlem |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

His specific showcases have rotated between exhibits and shows. One of his exhibitions called "Presence & Preservation" was his first west cost solo exhibition, opened at Charles H. Wright Museum, Detroit in 2021 and moved to the California African American Museum (CAAM) in 2022. Another exhibition, Revolutionary Times, was shown at both the Flint Institute of Arts and Grand Rapids Art Museum in 2024.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Hollis |first=Phyllis |date=2024-12-11 |title=Episode 225 – A Conversation with Mario Moore {{!}} Cerebral Women |url=https://cerebralwomen.com/2024/12/11/episode-225-a-conversation-with-mario-moore/ |access-date=2026-07-07 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=2025 Artists |url=https://butterartfair.com/2025-artists/ |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=BUTTER 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=CAAM {{!}} Mario Moore {{!}} Enshrined: Presence + Preservation |url=https://caamuseum.org/exhibitions/2022/enshrined-presence-preservation |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=caamuseum.org |language=en}}</ref>
