'''Rafael Pereira Sousa''' (born 22 August 1990), also known as '''Rafafá''', is a Brazilian TV host, comedian, and politician who took office as a federal deputy after [[Pedro Cunha Lima]] took a leave of absence from the position.

== Political career ==

=== Federal Representative ===
He ran for federal deputy, championing animal rights, the rights of the poor, and [[LGBTQ people|LGBT]] issues, and received 13,940 votes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Poder 360 {{!}} RAFAFA |url=https://eleicoes.poder360.com.br/candidato/1226167#2018 |access-date=2021-04-15 |website=eleicoes.poder360.com.br |archive-date=2021-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415213834/https://eleicoes.poder360.com.br/candidato/1226167#2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

He took the office on 14 April 2021, while the then-incumbent, Representative [[Pedro Cunha Lima]], was on leave.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rafafá toma posse na Câmara Federal após licença de Pedro – Portal Correio |url=https://portalcorreio.com.br/rafafa-toma-posse-na-camara-federal-apos-licenca-de-pedro/ |access-date=2021-04-15 |website=portalcorreio.com.br |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

=== Municipal Elections ===
He ran in the 2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024 elections for city council in [[Campina Grande]], but was unsuccessful in his first three attempts, receiving 455 votes in 2012, 1,254 votes in 2016,<ref name=":02">{{cite web |access-date=2021-04-15 |title=Poder 360 {{!}} RAFAFA |url=https://eleicoes.poder360.com.br/candidato/1226167#2016 |website=eleicoes.poder360.com.br |archive-date=2021-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415213834/https://eleicoes.poder360.com.br/candidato/1226167#2016 |url-status=live }}<!-- auto-translated from Portuguese by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and 2,094 in 2020.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2021-04-15 |language=pt-BR |title=Rafafá PSD 55111 {{!}} Candidato a vereador {{!}} Campina Grande – PB {{!}} Eleições 2020 |url=https://politica.estadao.com.br/eleicoes/2020/candidatos/pb/campina-grande/vereador/rafafa,55111 |website=Estadão |archive-date=2021-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415213833/https://politica.estadao.com.br/eleicoes/2020/candidatos/pb/campina-grande/vereador/rafafa,55111 |url-status=dead }}<!-- auto-translated from Portuguese by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> But in 2024, he was elected with 4,820 votes, making him the candidate with the most votes and, historically, the first openly LGBTQIAPN+ person to be elected in Campina Grande.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2024-10-12 |date=2024-10-06 |first=David |language=pt-BR |last=Maia |title=Rafafá é eleito vereador de Campina Grande com 4.820 votos e slogan marcante |url=https://acessopolitico.com.br/rafafa-e-eleito-vereador-de-campina-grande-com-4-820-votos-e-slogan-marcante.html |website=Acesso Político |archive-date=2024-11-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241113180624/https://acessopolitico.com.br/rafafa-e-eleito-vereador-de-campina-grande-com-4-820-votos-e-slogan-marcante.html |url-status=live }}<!-- auto-translated from Portuguese by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

'''Fredrik Mani Pålerud''' (born 24 February 1994) is a Norwegian [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a right back for [[IK Start]].

==Career==
He hails from {{ill|Finnholt|no}} and played local youth football for Disenå, Oppstad and [[Sander IL]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.glomdalen.no/kil/na-er-kil-bade-unge-og-lokale/s/1-57-7300798|title=Nå er KIL både unge og lokale|date=16 April 2014|work=Glåmdalen|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> He made his senior debut for Sander in the [[2012 3. divisjon]] before moving north in the summer, joining the academy of [[Tromsø IL]].<ref name=nff>{{NFF|3697118}}</ref> He was not given the chance for the senior team, and moved back to his home region in 2014, this time playing for [[Kongsvinger IL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger IL]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nordlys.no/fredrik-fikk-ikke-til-sjansen-han-hapet-pa-det-var-ikke-et-enkelt-valg/s/5-34-1144836|title=Fredrik fikk ikke TIL-sjansen han håpet på: – Det var ikke et enkelt valg|date=20 June 2019|work=Nordlys|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>

Pålerud became a regular in the right-back position.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.glomdalen.no/gar-i-linnes-sine-fotspor/s/5-19-168027|title=Går i Linnes sine fotspor|date=12 March 2016|work=Glåmdalen|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> In 2016 the team was behind a major upset as they, a second-tier side, made it to the [[2016 Norwegian Football Cup final]]. Pålerud scored the winning goal in the semi-final against Strømsgodset.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.adressa.no/sport/fotball/i/PRy0Pz/kongsvinger-treneren-graat-av-glede-etter-seier-i-semifinalen-for-en-droem|title=Kongsvinger-treneren gråt av glede etter seier i semifinalen: – For en drøm!|date=27 October 2016|work=Adresseavisen|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.itromso.no/sport/til/n/wel0bA/tidligere-til-spiller-ble-helt-i-sensasjonell-cuptriumf|title=Tidligere TIL-spiller ble helt i sensasjonell cuptriumf|date=28 October 2016|work=iTromsø|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>

Needing new challenges, Pålerud moved to Western Norway in 2021 to play for fellow second-tier team [[Sandnes Ulf]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.glomdalen.no/arlig-fredrik-palerud-jeg-matte-komme-meg-vekk/s/5-19-937804|title=Ærlig Fredrik Pålerud: - Jeg måtte komme meg vekk|date=20 March 2021|work=Glåmdalen|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> In early August 2022 he left Sandnes Ulf as he was signed by [[Sandefjord Fotball]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sb.no/endelig-far-fredrik-28-sin-store-sjanse-jeg-er-utrolig-glad/s/5-73-1530373|title=Endelig får Fredrik (28) sin store sjanse: – Jeg er utrolig glad|date=5 August 2022|work=Sandefjords Blad|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> At the age of 28 Pålerud made his [[Eliteserien]] debut in August 2022 against Viking.<ref name=nff/> Sandefjord would meet Kongsvinger in the [[2022_Eliteserien#Relegation_play-offs|relegation play-offs]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.norskfotball.com/blogg/palerud-om-kompismotet-bor-aerlig-talt-klare-denne-oppgaven|title=Pålerud om kompismøtet: - Bør ærlig talt klare denne oppgaven|date=16 November 2022|work=Norskfotball.com|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> winning the two-legged bout.

Pålerud did not find a new club in the 2023–24 transfer window, but trained with [[IK Start]]. As clubs were still allowed to sign free agents, he penned a contract in April 2024 lasting until the end of the year. It was extended for two more years.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.krs.no/veldig-greit-a-fa-det-pa-plass/s/5-157-192435|title=– Veldig greit å få det på plass|date=17 April 2024|work=Avisen Kristiansand|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fvn.no/sport/start/i/7340R8/forsvarsspiller-skrev-ny-start-kontrakt|title=Forsvarsspiller skrev ny Start-kontrakt|date=13 December 2024|work=Fædrelandsvennen|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> Winning promotion and returning for his second Eliteserien spell in 2026, Pålerud saw Start struggling in the bottom of the table.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nrk.no/sorlandet/start-spillere-etterlyser-kynisme_-_-vi-har-noen-steg-a-ta-der-1.17861131|title=Etterlyser kynisme: – Vi har noen steg å ta der|date=25 April 2026|publisher=NRK|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Pålerud graduated in law in 2019.
In 2026 he was hired as a part-time adviser in the law firm of IK Start's chairman.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.glomdalen.no/fredrik-31-med-ny-jobb-jeg-far-muligheten-til-a-jobbe-sa-mange-timer-jeg-far-skvist-inn/s/80-19-192860|title=Fredrik (31) med ny jobb: – Jeg får muligheten til å jobbe så mange timer jeg får skvist inn|date=18 January 2026|work=Glåmdalen|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.krs.no/stortrives-i-ny-by-og-nytt-hus-livet-er-veldig-bra/s/5-157-510779|title=Stortrives i ny by og nytt hus: – Livet er veldig bra|date=14 September 2025|work=Avisen Kristiansand|language=no|access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Jessica Goicoechea Jover''' (born 22 November 1996) is a Spanish model, influencer, fashion designer and businesswoman. Rejected by modelling agencies over her height, she built her career through [[Instagram]] and went on to work for brands such as [[Calvin Klein]] and [[Victoria's Secret]]; in 2019 she founded the fashion label Goi. In 2026 she was a finalist on the [[Antena 3 (Spanish TV channel)|Antena 3]] television contest ''El Desafío'', and announced that the courts had ruled in her favour in a six-year gender violence case against her former partner, the model River Viiperi.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jessica Goicoechea gana el juicio contra River Viiperi por violencia de género: 'La verdad ha salido a la luz' |trans-title=Jessica Goicoechea wins the gender violence trial against River Viiperi: 'The truth has come out' |url=https://www.hola.com/actualidad/20260311888818/jessica-goicoechea-gana-el-juicio-contra-river-viiperi-por-violencia-de-genero/ |website=¡Hola! |language=es |date=11 March 2026 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and career beginnings ==

Goicoechea was born in [[Barcelona]] on 22 November 1996 and began modelling at 15 with the 5th Avenue agency, but at 1.67 m she was rejected repeatedly over her height, including at a [[Victoria's Secret]] casting.<ref>{{cite web |title=Así es Jessica Goicoechea, 'influencer', modelo y empresaria |trans-title=This is Jessica Goicoechea: influencer, model and businesswoman |url=https://www.20minutos.es/noticia/5148383/0/asi-es-jessica-goicoechea-influencer-modelo-empresaria/ |website=20minutos |language=es |date=18 July 2023 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> She began posting her work on Instagram, which became her route into the fashion industry; agencies that had rejected her later asked to work with her.<ref>{{cite web |last=Guerra |first=Andrés |title=Jessica Goicoechea: "Las mismas agencias que me rechazaron, hoy me reclaman que trabaje con ellas" |trans-title=Jessica Goicoechea: "The same agencies that rejected me are now asking me to work with them" |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/gente/20171204/433371988495/goicoechea-shopping-night.html |website=La Vanguardia |language=es |date=3 December 2017 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref>

== Modelling and film ==

Goicoechea went on to model for brands including [[Calvin Klein (fashion house)|Calvin Klein]], [[Calzedonia]], [[Puma (brand)|Puma]] and [[Rimmel]], appeared in magazines such as ''[[Vogue (magazine)|Vogue]]'', ''[[Elle (magazine)|Elle]]'' and ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]'', and in 2017 featured in the music video for [[Manel Navarro]]'s "Candle".<ref>{{cite web |title=Jessica Goicoechea ¡10 cosas que no sabes de la influencer! |trans-title=Jessica Goicoechea: 10 things you don't know about the influencer! |url=https://www.marie-claire.es/moda/30404.html |website=Marie Claire |language=es |date=2 January 2024 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> That same year she made her acting debut in the short film ''La fantasía'', by Daniel Maldonado.<ref>{{cite web |last=Farràs Pérez |first=Lorena |title=Jessica Goicoechea: Modelo, 'influencer', actriz y empresaria |trans-title=Jessica Goicoechea: Model, influencer, actress and businesswoman |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/economia/emprendedores/20210428/7134611/jessica-goicoechea-goi-empresa-instagram.html |website=La Vanguardia |language=es |date=28 April 2021 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref>

== Goi ==

Goicoechea founded the fashion label Goi in 2019, at first as its sole partner with a single designer. Within two years the firm's daily sales rose from 600 to 2,700 euros, its staff grew to eight people and it was selling in more than 100 countries, with a third of revenue coming through Instagram.<ref>{{cite web |last=Godoy |first=Marta |title=Por qué Goi, el proyecto de esta 'influencer' española con 1,7 millones de seguidores, está rompiendo las reglas de la moda: el secreto de su éxito es tener poco 'stock' |trans-title=Why Goi, the project of this Spanish influencer with 1.7 million followers, is breaking fashion's rules: the secret of its success is low stock |url=https://www.businessinsider.es/goi-firma-moda-influencer-jessica-goicoechea-975223 |website=Business Insider |language=es |date=19 December 2021 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> The Barcelona-based label, known for its swimwear, has received orders from [[Eva Longoria]] and from [[Lionel Messi]] for his wife [[Antonela Roccuzzo]], while singers [[Aitana (singer)|Aitana]], [[Nathy Peluso]] and [[Rosalía]] have worn its designs. Goi has also faced criticism on social media that its bikinis cater only to slim bodies, which Goicoechea has rejected: she says the label makes sizes from XS to XL.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rodríguez |first=Amanda |title=Jessica Goicoechea, la reina de los biquinis que se mueve entre el éxito y el debate en redes: "No llueve a gusto de todos y siempre va a haber críticas" |trans-title=Jessica Goicoechea, the bikini queen who moves between success and social media debate: "You can't please everyone and there will always be criticism" |url=https://elpais.com/gente/2026-07-28/jessica-goicoechea-la-reina-de-los-biquinis-que-se-mueve-entre-el-exito-y-el-debate-en-redes-no-llueve-a-gusto-de-todos-y-siempre-va-a-haber-criticas.html |website=El País |language=es |date=28 July 2026 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref>

== Television ==

In 2026 Goicoechea competed in the sixth season of the [[Antena 3 (Spanish TV channel)|Antena 3]] television contest ''El Desafío'' and reached the grand final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Final de la sexta edición de 'El Desafío': José Yélamo, Jessica Goicoechea, Patricia Conde y Daniel Illescas se juegan 30.000 euros y un BMW descapotable rojo |trans-title=Final of the sixth edition of 'El Desafío': José Yélamo, Jessica Goicoechea, Patricia Conde and Daniel Illescas compete for 30,000 euros and a red convertible BMW |url=https://www.larazon.es/television/programas/final-sexta-edicion-desafio-jose-yelamo-jessica-goicoechea-patricia-conde-daniel-illescas-juegan-30000-euros-bmw-descapotable-rojo_2026032569c3b6ff384f6f2489a37da2.html |website=La Razón |language=es |date=25 March 2026 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> She finished fourth with 202 points in the final, held on 27 March 2026 and won by Daniel Illescas.<ref>{{cite web |title=¿Quién ganó 'El Desafío 6'? Así queda la clasificación final |trans-title=Who won 'El Desafío 6'? The final standings |url=https://www.europafm.com/noticias/tv-cine/quien-gano-ayer-desafio-6-asi-queda-clasificacion-final_2026032869c78e5dbfc2456bae16d801.html |website=Europa FM |language=es |date=28 March 2026 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==

In March 2020, during the COVID-19 lockdown in Spain, Goicoechea reported an assault by her partner and manager, the Ibiza-born model River Viiperi, to the [[Mossos d'Esquadra]]; officers found her with visible injuries and arrested him, and a duty court released him on charges.<ref>{{cite web |title=River Viiperi, detenido por agredir a su novia, la influencer Jessica Goicoechea |trans-title=River Viiperi, arrested for assaulting his girlfriend, the influencer Jessica Goicoechea |url=https://www.rtve.es/playz/20200330/river-viiperi-detenido-por-agredir-a-jessica-goicoechea/2011112.shtml |website=RTVE |language=es |date=30 March 2020 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> Viiperi, whose relationship with Goicoechea had become public in late 2017, denied the accusations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Las primeras palabras de River Viiperi tras su detención |trans-title=River Viiperi's first words after his arrest |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/elotromundo/gente/20200403/48278798990/primeras-palabras-river-viiperi-tras-su-detencion.html |website=Mundo Deportivo |language=es |date=3 April 2020 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> She later said the abuse during the relationship had been both physical and psychological.<ref>{{cite web |title=Quién es Jessica Goicoechea, concursante de 'El Desafío': por qué es famosa, un novio deportista y el maltrato que sufrió de su expareja |trans-title=Who is Jessica Goicoechea, 'El Desafío' contestant: why she is famous, a sportsman boyfriend and the abuse she suffered from her ex-partner |url=https://www.abc.es/play/television/noticias/jessica-goicoechea-concursante-desafio-famosa-famoso-novio-20260109204500-nt.html |website=ABC |language=es |date=9 January 2026 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> In March 2026 she announced that a court ruling had recognized the facts she had denounced, six years after the events.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jessica Goicoechea gana el juicio contra River Viiperi por violencia de género: "El peor episodio de mi vida, seis años de silencio" |trans-title=Jessica Goicoechea wins the gender violence trial against River Viiperi: "The worst episode of my life, six years of silence" |url=https://www.20minutos.es/gente/jessica-goicoechea-gana-juicio-contra-river-viiperi-por-violencia-genero-peor-episodio-mi-vida-seis-anos-silencio_6944478_0.html |website=20minutos |language=es |date=11 March 2026 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref>

In 2021 Goicoechea confirmed a relationship with the actor [[Arón Piper]].<ref>{{cite web |last=del Rio |first=Judith |title=Las imágenes que confirman la relación entre Jessica Goicoechea y Arón Piper |trans-title=The images that confirm the relationship between Jessica Goicoechea and Arón Piper |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/gente/20210830/7688617/imagenes-confirman-relacion-jessica-goicoechea-aron-piper-mmn.html |website=La Vanguardia |language=es |date=30 August 2021 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> They separated in January 2022 after almost two years together.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jessica Goicoechea habla sobre las imágenes de su ex, Arón Piper, con Dua Lipa en actitud cariñosa |trans-title=Jessica Goicoechea on the photos of her ex Arón Piper getting close with Dua Lipa |url=https://www.hola.com/actualidad/20220610211537/reaccion-jessica-goicoechea-posible-romance-aron-piper-dua-lipa/ |website=¡Hola! |language=es |date=10 June 2022 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> In January 2023 the footballer [[Marc Bartra]] confirmed their relationship.<ref>{{cite web |title=L'exbarcelonista Marc Bartra confirma la seva relació amb la model Jessica Goicoechea |trans-title=Former Barcelona player Marc Bartra confirms his relationship with model Jessica Goicoechea |url=https://www.ara.cat/gent/famosos/l-exbarcelonista-marc-bartra-confirma-seva-relacio-model-jessica-goicoechea_1_4601104.html |website=Ara |language=ca |date=17 January 2023 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref> After they broke up, Goicoechea confirmed a relationship with the rugby player [[Manu Moreno]] in February 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jessica Goicoechea y el jugador de rugby Manu Moreno confirman su relación tras su escapada a Málaga: "Mi 'mujé'" |trans-title=Jessica Goicoechea and rugby player Manu Moreno confirm their relationship after their getaway to Málaga: "My 'wife'" |url=https://www.20minutos.es/noticia/5680917/0/jessica-goicoechea-jugador-rugby-manu-moreno-confirman-su-relacion-tras-su-escapada-malaga-mi-muje/ |website=20minutos |language=es |date=10 February 2025 |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref>

'''Jean Mangabeira da Silva'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Jean Mangabeira: Profile - I League|url=https://ileague.id/clubs/singleplayer/bri_super_league_2026-27/jean_mangabeira_da_silva?token=UDEwNjA0MDYy |website=ILeague |date=10 October 2026 |access-date=10 October 2026}}</ref> (born 10 March 1997) is a Brazilian professional [[footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Super League (Indonesia)|Super League]] club [[Dewa United Banten F.C.|Dewa United Banten]].

== Club career ==
Born in [[Rondonópolis]], Brazil, Mangabeira began his professional career within the youth academy of [[Criciúma Esporte Clube|Criciúma]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Visita ao Asilo São Vicente de Paulo |url=https://www.criciuma.com.br/m/noticias/o-clube/visita-ao-asilo-sao-vicente-de-paulo |website=www.criciuma.com.br |date=9 August 2018 |access-date=27 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref>

Mangabeira subsequently joined club [[Capivariano Futebol Clube|Capivariano]] before moved abroad to Europe to join [[Czech First League]] club [[MFK Karviná|Karviná]] on loan in 2020, he made his league debut on 10 June 2020, coming on as a starter in a 0–1 lose over [[FK Jablonec|Jablonec]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Těsná porážka! Jablonec-Karviná 1:0|url=https://www.mfkkarvina.cz/zapas.asp?ID=Tesna-porazkaJablonec-Karvina-1-0-4786 |website=www.mfkkarvina.cz |date=10 June 2020|access-date=30 August 2026 |language=cs}}</ref> During his time with the club, Mangabeira made 42 league appearances and without scoring.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rekam Jejak Jean Mangabeira, Jawaban Dewa United untuk Posisi Gelandang Bertahan |url=https://ileague.id/news/detail/rekam-jejak-jean-mangabeira--jawaban-dewa-united-untuk-posisi-gelandang-bertahan |work=ILeague |date=19 August 2026 |access-date=27 August 2026 |language=id}}</ref>

=== Náutico ===
In 2023, Mangabeira signed a contract with [[Clube Náutico Capibaribe|Náutico]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Náutico anuncia chegada do volante Jean Mangabeira|url=https://www.folhape.com.br/esportes/nautico-anuncia-chegada-do-volante-jean-mangabeira/250181/ |website=www.folhape.com |date=12 December 2022|access-date=27 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref> On 2 May 2023, he scored his first league goal in his debut match against [[Manaus Futebol Clube|Manaus]] despite losing 1–2 in the [[2023 Campeonato Brasileiro Série C]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Manaus vence o Náutico por 2×1 de virada na estreia da série C|url=https://portalmanaos.com.br/2023/05/03/manaus-vence-o-nautico-por-2x1-de-virada-na-estreia-da-serie-c/ |website=portalmanaos.com |date=2 May 2023|access-date=30 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref> He added his second goals of the season on 16 July 2023 with one goal against [[Figueirense FC|Figueirense]] in a 2–1 home win.<ref>{{cite news |title=Náutico 2–1 Figueirense|url=https://www.espn.com.br/futebol/partida?jogoId=667032 |website=www.espn.com |date=16 July 2023|access-date=30 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref>

=== Tacuary ===
In July 2024, he moved abroad, signed a contract with [[Tacuary FC|Tacuary]] in [[Paraguay]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ex-Criciúma, Jean fala sobre ida para o Paraguai: 'Liga mais competitiva' |url=https://tntsports.com.br/futebolbrasileiro/Ex-Criciuma-Jean-fala-sobre-ida-para-o-Paraguai-Liga-mais-competitiva-20240730-0011.html |website=tntsports |date=30 July 2024 |access-date=27 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref> He made his league debut on 27 July 2024, coming on as a starter in a 0–0 draw against [[Sportivo Ameliano]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ameliano 0-Tacuary 0: Marcador vacío en Trinidad |url=https://www.abc.com.py/deportes/futbol/2024/07/28/ameliano-0-tacuary-0-marcador-vacio-en-trinidad/?outputType=amp |website=www.abc.com |date=27 July 2024 |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=es}}</ref> On 18 August 2024, he picked up his first win with Tacuary in his third appearances in a 1–2 away win over [[Club Sol de América|Sol de América]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Sol de América 1–2 Tacuary |url=https://www.soccerway.com/match/sol-de-america-WMg3uAeT/tacuary-hxhlylJj/?mid=8zes8YDc |website=Soccerway |date=18 August 2024 |access-date=30 August 2026}}</ref>

=== Figuerense ===
Mangabeira subsequently return to Brazil, joined [[Botafogo Futebol Clube (SP)|Botafogo-SP]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Botafogo fecha a contratação do volante Jean Mangabeira |url=https://botafogofutebolsa.com.br/botafogo-fecha-a-contratacao-do-volante-jean-mangabeira/ |website=botafogofutebolsa |date=10 December 2024 |access-date=27 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref> and Série C side [[Brusque Futebol Clube|Brusque]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Brusque FC anuncia a contratação do volante Jean Mangabeira |url=https://brusquefutebolclube.com.br/blog/brusque-fc-anuncia-a-contratacao-do-volante-jean-mangabeira/ |website=brusquefutebolclube |date=25 March 2025 |access-date=27 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref> before signed a contract with another Série C club [[Figueirense FC|Figueirense]] in January 2026.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jean Mangabeira é o novo reforço do Figueirense |url=https://figueirense.com.br/jean-mangabeira-e-o-novo-reforco-do-figueirense/ |website=figueirense.com |date=1 January 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref> He made his club debut on 13 April 2026, coming on as a substituted in a 1–3 home lose against [[Maringá Futebol Clube|Maringá]].<ref>{{cite news |title=3 a 1: Maringá FC de Egert goleia Figueirense em Florianópolis |url=https://ofatomaringa.com/3-a-1-maringa-fc-de-egert-goleia-figueirense-em-florianopolis/ |website=ofatomaringa.com |date=13 April 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref> During the 2026 season with Figueirense, he made 26 league appearances and without scoring in all competitions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gelandang Brasil Jean Mangabeira Jadi Senjata Baru Dewa United |url=https://rri.co.id/sepak-bola/2654674/gelandang-brasil-jean-mangabeira-jadi-senjata-baru-dewa-united |work=[[Radio Republik Indonesia|RRI]] |date=15 August 2026 |access-date=27 August 2026 |language=id}}</ref>

=== Dewa United Banten ===
In mid-August 2026, Mangabeira officially completed a transfer to Indonesian [[Super League (Indonesia)|Super League]] club [[Dewa United Banten F.C.|Dewa United Banten]], marking his first venture into Asian football following his extensive career in Brazil, the Czech Republic, and Paraguay.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kehadiran Jean Mangabeira Diharapkan Mampu Membawa Dimensi Baru Dewa United |url=https://www.gonews.co/berita/baca/2026/08/17/kehadiran-jean-mangabeira-diharapkan-mampu-membawa-dimensi-baru-dewa-united |work=GoNews |date=17 August 2026 |access-date=27 August 2026 |language=id}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Dewa United Rekrut Jean Mangabeira, Gelandang Bertahan Brasil untuk Perkuat Lini Tengah |url=https://kuasakata.com/read/berita/128934-dewa-united-rekrut-jean-mangabeira-gelandang-bertahan-brasil-untuk-perkuat-lini-tengah |work=Kuasa Kata |date=20 August 2026 |access-date=27 August 2026 |language=id}}</ref> Mangabeira made his league debut for Dewa United Banten on 5 September 2026, coming on as a starter in a 0–1 away win against [[Persik Kediri]] at the [[Brawijaya Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hasil Persik Vs Dewa United: Gol Struick Tumbangkan Macan Putih 0-1
|url=https://www.detik.com/jatim/sepakbola/d-8649925/hasil-persik-vs-dewa-united-gol-struick-tumbangkan-macan-putih-0-1 |date=5 September 2026|publisher=www.detik.com|accessdate=6 September 2026|language=id}}</ref>

'''Max Flick''' (born June 29, 1994) is an American former [[association football]] player who played as a defender. He spent his professional career with [[North Carolina FC]] in [[USL League One]], where he played from 2021 to 2023. He retired after the 2023 season, which ended with North Carolina FC winning the USL League One championship.<ref name="MLS">{{cite web |title=Max Flick |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/players/max-flick/ |publisher=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="NCFCretire">{{cite web |title=Max Flick: From open tryout attendee to team MVP |url=https://www.northcarolinafc.com/news/2024/01/11/max-flick-i-had-a-dream-and-there-was-an-opportunity-to-play-and-i-took-it/ |publisher=North Carolina FC |date=January 11, 2024 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and college==
Flick was born in [[Beaver Falls, Pennsylvania]]. He attended [[Blackhawk High School (Pennsylvania)|Blackhawk High School]], where he played soccer as a midfielder and graduated in 2012.<ref name="Blackhawk">{{cite web |title=Max Flick's Blackhawk High School Bio |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/pa/beaver-falls/blackhawk-cougars/athletes/max-flick/bio/?careerid=hqcr5g143dhff |publisher=MaxPreps |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

Flick initially attended [[Geneva College]] and was listed on its men's soccer roster in 2012. He transferred to [[Point Park University]] in 2013 and played three seasons for the Pioneers.<ref name="Geneva">{{cite web |title=2012 Men's Soccer Roster |url=https://athletics.geneva.edu/sports/mens-soccer/roster/2012 |publisher=Geneva College Athletics |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="PointPark2013">{{cite web |title=Point Park's Dziak, Flick sweep KIAC Men's Soccer Player of the Week awards |url=https://pointparksports.com/news/2013/10/22/10_22_2013_1970.aspx |publisher=Point Park University Athletics |date=October 22, 2013 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

During his first season at Point Park, Flick was named the [[Kentucky Intercollegiate Athletic Conference]] Offensive Player of the Week in October 2013. At the time of the award, he had scored six goals and recorded five assists in 15 starts. In a 6–1 victory over Brescia University, he scored twice and provided two assists.<ref name="PointPark2013" /> Flick also scored in Point Park's 3–1 win over West Virginia Tech in September and recorded a goal in the Pioneers' first-round [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] tournament match against the University of Rio Grande later that season.<ref name="WVU">{{cite web |title=West Virginia Tech vs Point Park (Sep 17, 2013) |url=https://goldenbearathletics.com/sports/mens-soccer/stats/2013-2014/point-park-university-pa-/boxscore/834 |publisher=WVU Tech Athletics |date=September 17, 2013 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Rio">{{cite web |title=Rio Men's Soccer Defeats Point Park 2-1 |url=https://woub.org/2013/11/23/rio-mens-soccer-defeats-point-park-2-1/ |publisher=WOUB Public Media |date=November 23, 2013 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

He remained with Point Park through the 2015 season. The university's records list him as a senior midfielder in 2015, and he graduated from Point Park in 2016.<ref name="PointParkRoster">{{cite web |title=2015 Men's Soccer Roster |url=https://pointparksports.com/sports/mens-soccer/roster/2015 |publisher=Point Park University Athletics |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="HotspursBio">{{cite web |title=Spurs Signing: Max Flick |url=https://www.hotspurs-soccer.com/spurs-signing-max-flick/ |publisher=Pittsburgh Hotspurs |date=April 29, 2019 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

==Amateur career==
After college, Flick continued playing in the Pittsburgh area while pursuing a professional opportunity. He played for the [[Fort Pitt Regiment]] of the [[National Premier Soccer League]] and was selected to an NPSL Midwest Region East Conference XI in 2018.<ref name="NCFCsigning">{{cite web |title=North Carolina FC Signs Max Flick to Roster |url=https://www.northcarolinafc.com/news/2021/04/15/north-carolina-fc-signs-max-flick-to-roster/ |publisher=North Carolina FC |date=April 15, 2021 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

Flick later joined the Pittsburgh Hotspurs for their inaugural NPSL season in 2019. The club described him as a fullback and noted that he had previously played for the Pittsburgh Strikers and Century United. During his college years, he also played for the Pittsburgh Riverhounds' team in the [[Premier Development League]], later known as [[USL League Two]].<ref name="HotspursBio"/>

Flick's route toward professional soccer included repeated attempts at open tryouts. According to a later account published by North Carolina FC, he attended tryouts with several clubs and had previously been rejected by North Carolina FC before returning for the club's 2021 open tryout.<ref name="USLfeature">{{cite web |title=No Limitations, Only Opportunities: Max Flick |url=https://www.uslleagueone.com/news_article/show/1185979-no-limitations-only-opportunities-max-flick |publisher=USL League One |date=September 30, 2021 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="NCFCretire"/>

==Professional career==

===North Carolina FC===
Flick joined [[North Carolina FC]] in 2021 after attending the club's open tryout and subsequently being invited to preseason camp. The club signed him on April 15, 2021, making his professional debut that season. He had previously played only in college and amateur soccer before joining the club.<ref name="NCFCsigning"/><ref name="USLfeature"/>

In his first professional season, Flick made 25 appearances and scored two goals. He was named North Carolina FC's Defensive Player of the Year and, in a vote of his teammates, the club's Most Valuable Player. He was also selected to the USL League One Team of the Week in Week 12.<ref name="NCFC2021">{{cite web |title=Max Flick and Nelson Martinez Re-sign with North Carolina FC |url=https://www.northcarolinafc.com/news/2021/11/24/max-flick-and-nelson-martinez-re-sign-with-north-carolina-fc/ |publisher=North Carolina FC |date=November 24, 2021 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

Flick remained with North Carolina FC for the 2022 season. He made 24 appearances in USL League One, scoring one goal and recording two assists. He became a regular starter late in the season after initially serving in a more limited role. In August 2022, he scored his first goal of the season against the Richmond Kickers, and by the end of September he had started six of the club's previous seven matches.<ref name="FBref">{{cite web |title=Max Flick Stats, Goals, Records, Assists, Cups and more |url=https://fbref.com/en/players/832f2148/ |publisher=FBref |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="NCFC2022">{{cite web |title=MATCH PREVIEW: NCFC to Conclude Season Series Against Union Omaha Saturday |url=https://www.northcarolinafc.com/news/2022/09/30/match-preview-ncfc-to-conclude-season-series-against-union-omaha-saturday/ |publisher=North Carolina FC |date=September 30, 2022 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Richmond2022">{{cite web |title=MATCH PREVIEW: North Carolina FC to take on Forward Madison for First Time this Season |url=https://www.northcarolinafc.com/news/2022/08/08/match-preview-ncfc-to-take-on-forward-madison-for-first-time-this-season/ |publisher=North Carolina FC |date=August 8, 2022 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

Flick's final season came in 2023. He made 18 appearances in USL League One, generally as a substitute, for a total of 137 minutes. He made his 50th appearance for North Carolina FC on April 1, 2023.<ref name="FBref"/><ref name="50th">{{cite web |title=MATCH RECAP: NCFC picks up first win of 2023 season over Lexington SC |url=https://www.northcarolinafc.com/news/2023/04/01/match-recap-ncfc-picks-up-first-win-of-2023-season-over-lexington-sc/ |publisher=North Carolina FC |date=April 1, 2023 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

North Carolina FC reached the 2023 USL League One final and defeated the [[Charlotte Independence]] on penalties after a 1–1 draw. Flick was an unused substitute for most of the match but entered the game late in extra time and participated in the penalty shootout. The championship was the first USL League One title in North Carolina FC history.<ref name="Final">{{cite web |title=STARRY NIGHT! NCFC is 2023 USL League One Champion |url=https://www.northcarolinafc.com/news/2023/11/05/starry-night-ncfc-is-2023-usl-league-one-champion/ |publisher=North Carolina FC |date=November 5, 2023 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref>

Flick retired from professional soccer following the 2023 season. In a January 2024 interview with North Carolina FC, he said that he and his family had known before the championship match that it would be his final game. The club described the 2023 championship as the conclusion of his three-season professional career with North Carolina FC.<ref name="NCFCretire"/>

'''Walter Lobyn Hamilton''' is an African-American artist native to [[Indianapolis|Indianapolis, Indiana]]. His artwork utilizes smashed or cut [[vinyl record]] pieces as the medium for portraits and flags. Hamilton's work has been featured in the [[Indiana State Museum]], the [[Indianapolis Museum of Art]], and [[Long-Sharp Gallery]]. 

== Early life and education ==
Hamilton was raised in Indianapolis in the 1990s with his three brothers and sister. When Hamilton was in the ninth grade at [[Franklin Central High School]], his father, Clayton Hamilton, gifted his son a deejay kit.<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
Hamilton's career began as a freelance [[disc jockey]] often hired on to play [[turntables]] at college parties. After a leg injury and chronic pain prevented him from continuing his career as a DJ, Hamilton's frustration led him to going into his basement and smashing his vinyl records in an act of anger. His artwork developed from the broken pieces after seeing the shards in a new light several months later inspired him to utilize them as his artistic medium. From the pieces Hamilton created a portrait of [[Jimi Hendrix]] on wood board with a painted red background.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=PERRY |first=BRANDON A. |date=2012-02-09 |title=Art exhibit showcases unique talent |url=https://indianapolisrecorder.com/83a8b6cc-5338-11e1-9cb1-001871e3ce6c/ |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=Indianapolis Recorder |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

In 2011, Hamilton's vinyl record portraits were featured in the [[Indy Arts Council]]'s Art and Soul Festival.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Grossman |first=Dan |title=Art & Soul: Walter Lobyn Hamilton |url=https://www.nuvo.net/arts/visual/art-soul-walter-lobyn-hamilton/article_e0624b7f-22fd-55ab-978c-6f94d168586e.html |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20251225130334/https://www.nuvo.net/arts/visual/art-soul-walter-lobyn-hamilton/article_e0624b7f-22fd-55ab-978c-6f94d168586e.html |archive-date=2025-12-25 |access-date=2026-09-16 |work=NUVO |language=en}}</ref> 

The [[Indiana State Museum]] featured Hamilton's portrait piece, "Dark Fantasy", in their 2012 exhibit "REPRESENT: Art by African-Americans". The portrait displays Hamilton's usual medium of broken vinyl shards in order to create a silhouette representation of a woman with a large afro. Hamilton's inspiration for "Dark Fantasy" came from seeing his sister return home one day sporting a large afro with a red flower in her hair.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uh6tbCFYa_U |title=The Vinyl Artist |date=2012-05-31 |last=IndianaStateMuseum |access-date=2026-09-16 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

In [[Studio Museum in Harlem|Studio Museum Harlem]], a vinyl piece of [[Angela Davis]] was put on display in 2018 after its creation in 2015. Also in 2018, Hamilton had an exhibit shown in Long-Sharp Gallery, displaying multiple of his pieces. This exhibit was called "Narrative Not Included" and was also showcased in [[Johnson & Johnson]], [[Nas]], [[Kanye West]] and the [[Fox TV]] Show [[Empire (2015 TV series)|"Empire"]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Walter Lobyn Hamilton |url=https://www.studiomuseum.org/artists/walter-lobyn-hamilton |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Studio Museum in Harlem |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-03-02 |title=Narrative Not Included: Lobyn Hamilton |url=https://www.longsharpgallery.com/physical-galleries/narrative-not-included-lobyn-hamilton |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Long-Sharp Gallery |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Lobyn Hamilton: Narrative Not... {{!}} Exhibitions {{!}} MutualArt |url=https://www.mutualart.com/Exhibition/Lobyn-Hamilton--Narrative-Not-Included/11A879145DC7952F |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=www.mutualart.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, Hamilton's "One Nation Under A Groove" project was displayed in Brose Partington Studio, a large project utilizing vinyls of music throughout Hamilton's entire life. This art piece was also shown at Newfields later, albeit a smaller version titled "One Nation Under A Groove Box Set, Vol. 2" in the "What I Have You Have" exhibition in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Walter Lobyn Hamilton |url=https://brosepartingtonstudio.com/projects/walter-lobyn-hamilton |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Brose Partington Studio |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Newfields |date=2023-09-20 |title=What I Have You Have |url=https://discovernewfields.org/discovernewfields-qjihhwysu-newfields-lab.vercel.app |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=discovernewfields.org |language=en}}</ref>

The "What I Have You Have" exhibition in Newfields is a series of six art pieces made of broken vinyl, shaped like flags. It is present within Newfields as well as at partner locations; the [[Indianapolis Symphony Orchestra]], [[University of Indianapolis]], and [[Indianapolis Public Library|Indianapolis Central Library]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Walter Lobyn Hamilton What I Have You Have |url=https://discovernewfields.org/discovernewfields-qjihhwysu-newfields-lab.vercel.app |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=discovernewfields.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-04 |title=Walter Lobyn Hamilton Spins Albums Into Art: A Review of What I Have You Have |url=https://eratomagazine.wordpress.com/2024/07/04/walter-lobyn-hamilton-spins-albums-into-art-a-review-of-what-i-have-you-have/ |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=Erato |language=en}}</ref>

Dellafuente was born in [[Granada]] and raised in nearby [[Armilla, Granada|Armilla]],<ref name=vargas1/> specifically in its Corea neighbourhood, where he is known as "El Chino".<ref name=zenda>{{cite news |last1=Domínguez |first1=Irene |title=Dellafuente: de Granada para toda la vida, como Lorca|trans-title=Dellafuente: from Granada for his whole life, just like Lorca|url=https://www.zendalibros.com/dellafuente-de-granada-para-toda-la-vida-como-lorca/ |access-date=7 September 2026 |work=Zenda |date=2 September 2020 |language=Spanish}}</ref> His mother is Brazilian,<ref name=zenda/> and he took his artistic name from his paternal grandmother's surname, De la Fuente.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dellafuente |url=https://www.neo2.com/dellafuente/ |access-date=7 September 2026 |work=Neo2 |date=5 December 2016 |language=Spanish}}</ref> He did automotive training, and failed an audiovisual course due to absences; he worked fixing motorcycles and in his father's wardrobe shop.<ref name=zenda/>

==Musical style==
Dellafuente said that at 15, he listened to [[flamenco]] and [[reggaeton]], as well as a smaller amount of rap, such as [[Mala Rodríguez]]. He said that he should not be referred to exclusively as a rapper or [[trap music|trapper]], but as an "urban musical artist", which he said was a more common term in Latin America.<ref name=vargas1/> His music is inspired by the flamenco culture of his city, and he has named assassinated Granada author [[Federico García Lorca]] as an influence.<ref name=zenda/><ref name=pais/> Dellafuente has defended his use of [[AutoTune]], saying that he would be "dead from hunger" without it.<ref name=vargas1/> He has been described as part of [[New flamenco]].<ref>{{cite news |title=El nuevo flamenco|trans-title=New flamenco |url=https://www.vice.com/es/article/nuevo-flamenco-rosalia-nino-elche-morente-noisey/ |access-date=8 September 2026 |work=[[Vice Media|Vice]] |date=28 March 2017 |language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Stables |first1=Daniel |title=Want to learn the language of Spain's flamenco? Come to Granada in Andalucia |url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/travel/article/how-to-experience-flamenco-in-granada-spain |access-date=8 September 2026 |work=[[National Geographic]] |date=25 January 2025}}</ref>

'''Juan Pablo Cozzani''' (born 9 October 1998) is an Argentine professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Club Atlético Platense|Platense]].

==Club career==
Cozzani played for the youth teams of [[Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza|Gimnasia Mendoza]] and [[Talleres de Córdoba|Talleres]] before joining [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]], where he was a backup goalkeeper.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |date=2021-04-27 |title=Entrevista. Juan Pablo Cozzani: "El objetivo es ir a buscar la clasificación a Tokio" |url=https://www.vavel.com/ar/futbol-argentino/2020/01/07/seleccion-argentina/1008895-entrevista-juan-pablo-cozzani-el-objetivo-es-ir-a-buscar-la-clasificacion-a-tokio.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210517085220/https://www.vavel.com/ar/futbol-argentino/2020/01/07/seleccion-argentina/1008895-entrevista-juan-pablo-cozzani-el-objetivo-es-ir-a-buscar-la-clasificacion-a-tokio.html |archive-date=2021-05-17 |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=VAVEL |language=es-ar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Juan Cozzani: “Me defino como un arquero al que le gusta jugar adelantado” |url=https://www.losandes.com.ar/juan-cozzani |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=Los Andes |language=es-AR}}</ref>

In August 2020, he was loaned to [[Primera Nacional]] club [[San Martín de San Juan|San Martín SJ]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=El mendocino Juan Pablo Cozzani jugará en San Martín de San Juan |url=https://www.losandes.com.ar/mas-deportes/el-mendocino-juan-pablo-cozzani-jugara-en-san-martin-de-san-juan |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=Los Andes |language=es-AR}}</ref> He made his professional club debut on 29 November in a 1–0 win against [[Club Atlético Nueva Chicago|Nueva Chicago]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ascenso del Interior · San Martín (SJ) 1 - 0 Nueva Chicago |url=https://ascensodelinterior.com.ar/noticias/26458/san-martn-(sj)-1---0-nueva-chicago |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=ascensodelinterior.com.ar}}</ref>

In 2022, he joined [[Deportivo Maipú]] as a free agent. He quickly established himself as the starting goalkeeper.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Faria |first=Sergio |title=Juan Pablo Cozzani, una de las figuras de Maipú: “La continuidad me hizo crecer como arquero” |url=https://www.losandes.com.ar/mas-deportes/juan-pablo-cozzani-una-de-las-figuras-de-maipu-la-continuidad-me-hizo-crecer-como-arquero |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=Los Andes |language=es-AR}}</ref> On 2 December 2023, he started the [[2023 Primera Nacional|Primera Nacional promotion final]] against [[Deportivo Riestra]], which Maipú lost 1–0.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-02 |title=◉ Deportivo Maipú vs. Riestra, por la final del Reducido de la Primera Nacional: resultado, resumen y goles - TyC Sports |url=https://www.tycsports.com/primera-nacional/deportivo-maipu-vs-riestra-en-vivo-hora-donde-ver-y-formaciones-id550777.html |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.tycsports.com |language=es-AR}}</ref>

On 5 January 2024, he was loaned to [[AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol|Liga Profesional]] club [[Club Atlético Platense|Platense]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-06 |title=Platense presentó oficialmente a Cozzani y a Rivero como nuevos refuerzos |url=https://www.zonanortehoy.com/vicente-lopez/platense-presento-oficialmente-a-cozzani-y-a-rivero-como-nuevos-refuerzos/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.zonanortehoy.com |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zabalza |first=Ignacio |date=2024-01-05 |title=Juan Pablo Cozzani llega para reforzar el arco de Platense |url=https://cap.org.ar/2024/01/juan-pablo-cozzani-llega-para-reforzar-el-arco-de-platense/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |language=es}}</ref> He made his [[AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol|Liga Profesional]] debut on 27 January, keeping a clean sheet as Platense drew 0–0 with [[Boca Juniors]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zabalza |first=Ignacio |date=2024-01-27 |title=La Previa: Debut ante Boca Juniors, en el inicio oficial del ciclo Grazzini |url=https://cap.org.ar/2024/01/la-previa-debut-ante-boca-juniors-en-el-inicio-oficial-del-ciclo-grazzini/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |language=es}}</ref> On 28 October, Platense confirmed that they exercised their purchase option to sign Cozzani permanently, signing him to a contract until the end of 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zabalza |first=Ignacio |date=2024-10-28 |title=Cozzani 2028: Platense compró parte del pase de su arquero |url=https://cap.org.ar/2024/10/cozzani-2028-platense-compro-parte-del-pase-de-su-arquero/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |language=es}}</ref> He helped his club to the first title in their history on 1 June 2025, keeping a clean sheet in 1–0 win against [[Club Atlético Huracán|Huracán]] to win the [[2025 AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol|Torneo Apertura]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Platense es el nuevo campeón del fútbol argentino |url=https://www.afa.com.ar/es/posts/platense-es-el-nuevo-campeon-del-futbol-argentino |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=Sitio Oficial de la Asociación del Fútbol Argentino |language=es-AR}}</ref>

On 19 August 2025, his contract was extended to 2029 and he was loaned to [[Saudi Pro League]] club [[Al-Kholood Club|Al-Kholood]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zabalza |first=Ignacio |date=2025-08-19 |title=Juan Pablo Cozzani renovó con Platense y seguirá su carrera en Arabia Saudita |url=https://cap.org.ar/2025/08/juan-pablo-cozzani-renovo-con-platense-y-seguira-su-carrera-en-arabia-saudita/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |language=es}}</ref> He returned to Platense after the loan ended and subsequently made his debut in continental competition on 13 August 2026 in a 1–1 draw against [[Coquimbo Unido]] in the [[2026 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] round of 16. In the second leg, after a 0–0 draw, he scored the 6th penalty of the shootout and saved Coquimbo Unido's 7th to send Platense through to the next round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Juan Pablo Cozzani, the hero who returned home to write new chapters of history {{!}} CONMEBOL Libertadores |url=https://gol.conmebol.com/libertadores/en/news/juan-pablo-cozzani-hero-who-returned-home-write-new-chapters-history |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=gol.conmebol.com |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
In 2019, he was called up by [[Fernando Batista]] to play for the [[Argentina national under-23 football team|Argentina national under-23 team]] in the [[2020 CONMEBOL Pre-Olympic Tournament]], which Argentina won.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Juan Pablo Cozzani: “Me siento orgulloso de estar en la Selección” {{!}} + Deportes |url=https://www.losandes.com.ar/article/view/?slug=juan-pablo-cozzani-me-siento-orgulloso-de-estar-en-la-seleccion |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240228220732/https://www.losandes.com.ar/article/view/?slug=juan-pablo-cozzani-me-siento-orgulloso-de-estar-en-la-seleccion |archive-date=2024-02-28 |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=Los Andes |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Belmonte y Cozzani, campeones del Preolímpico |url=http://clublanus.com/secciones/futbol-profesional/noticias/belmonte-y-cozzani-campeones-del-preolimpico |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813024426/http://clublanus.com/secciones/futbol-profesional/noticias/belmonte-y-cozzani-campeones-del-preolimpico |archive-date=2020-08-13 |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=Clublanus.com |language=es}}</ref>

{{Nihongo|''' Riku Ogata'''|緒方 理貢|Ogata Riku|born September 22, 1998}} is a Japanese [[professional baseball]] [[Outfielder]] for the [[Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks]] of [[Nippon Professional Baseball]] (NPB).

==Early baseball career==
He went on to attend [[Komazawa University]], where he became a regular [[Left fielder]] during the autumn of his freshman year. He recorded a batting average of over .300 in the [[Tohto University Baseball League]] and contributed to the team's promotion from Division 2 to Division 1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/b81d649277a7fb867dcbd548eb8e7eeb6d3de741|title=Yahoo Japan baseball news 【ホークス育成新人File】駒大から入団の育成5位・緒方理貢は「周東2世」に！|language=ja-JP|website=[[Yahoo Japan]]|date=January 25, 2021|access-date=September 30, 2026}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On October 26, 2020, Ogata was drafted by the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks as a [[Developmental Player System|developmental player]] in the [[2020 Nippon Professional Baseball draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.komazawa-u.ac.jp/news/extracurricular/2020/1102-9721.html|title=Komazawa University Home > News > Extracurricular Activities > 2020 Academic Year 硬式野球部の緒方理貢選手と前田研輝選手がドラフト指名挨拶を受けました|language=ja-JP|website=[[Komazawa University]] Official site|date=November 2, 2020|access-date=September 30, 2026}}</ref>

From 2021 to 2023 season, he played in informal matches against [[Shikoku Island League Plus]]'s teams and amateur baseball teams, and played in the [[Western League (Japanese baseball)|Western League]] of NPB's second leagues.

On March 19, 2024, Ogata signed a 7 million yen re-contract with the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks as a [[Registration of players under control|registered player under control]] with [[Yuto Kawamura]] and [[Keisuke Nakata]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://full-count.jp/2024/03/19/post1529247/|title=full-count.jp baseball news ソフトバンク、異例の3選手同時昇格　仲田慶介、川村友斗、緒方理貢の支配下登録を発表|language=ja-JP|website=full-count.jp|date=March 19, 2024|access-date=September 29, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/baseball/news/202403190000448.html|title=Nikkan Sports baseball news 【ソフトバンク】21年ドラフト最終指名の仲田慶介が支配下昇格「はい上がってやる気持ちで」|language=ja-JP|newspaper=Nikkan Sports|date=March 19, 2024|accessdate=September 29, 2026}}</ref>

In 2024 season, Ogata made his [[Pacific League]] debut as a pinch-runner in the game against the [[Orix Buffaloes]] on March 29. And recorded his first hit in a game against the Orix Buffaloes April 20.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/baseball/news/202404200001610.html|title=Nikkan Sports baseball news 【ソフトバンク】緒方理貢がプロ初安打「貢献しようと」２度の満塁機で２三振には「悔しい」|language=ja-JP|newspaper=Nikkan Sports|date=April 20, 2024|accessdate=September 30, 2026}}</ref> Although he primarily appeared as a defensive substitute or pinch-runner, he remained on the first-team roster throughout the season, playing in 86 games and contributing to the team's Pacific League championship. And he signing a contract with 13 million yen.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/baseball/news/202411270000482.html|title=Nikkan Sports baseball news 【ソフトバンク】緒方理貢600万円増の1300万円「今年より多くスタメンで」来季へ意欲|language=ja-JP|newspaper=Nikkan Sports|date=November 27, 2024|accessdate=September 30, 2026}}</ref>

In 2025 season, he played in a career-high 101 games and contributed to the team's Japan Series championship. He also signed a contract worth 24 million yen.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/baseball/news/202512190000928.html|title=Nikkan Sports baseball news 【ソフトバンク】緒方理貢1100万円増の2400万円で更改「来年がすごく大事な年」|language=ja-JP|newspaper=Nikkan Sports|date=December 27, 2025|accessdate=September 30, 2026}}</ref>

In 2026 season, he injured his right calf muscle after being hit by a pitch on March 27 and spent the season rehabilitating, delaying his addition to the first-team roster until July 10.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/baseball/news/202607090001094.html|title=Nikkan Sports baseball news 【ソフトバンク】緒方理貢が今季初1軍昇格へ　斉藤2軍監督は期待「いい変化をしてほしい」|language=ja-JP|newspaper=Nikkan Sports|date=July 9, 2026|accessdate=September 30, 2026}}</ref>
